grade_2.focus: Discovering how different groups of people work together to keep a community safe and running.

lessons.title: Jobs That Keep Our Community Safe
lessons.brief: Learning about police officers, firefighters, and paramedics and the specific tasks they perform.

lessons.title: Places and Services in Our Neighbourhood
lessons.brief: Identifying local places like libraries, parks, stores, and hospitals and what services they provide.

lessons.title: Rules and Why We Need Them
lessons.brief: Understanding that rules at home, school, and in public spaces help keep everyone safe and fair.

lessons.title: Working Together as a Team
lessons.brief: Seeing how families, classrooms, and communities function better when people cooperate and share jobs.

grade_3.focus: Understanding how communities are organized and how citizens and leaders make decisions together.

lessons.title: Roles of Leaders in Our Community
lessons.brief: Identifying local leaders like mayors and principals and comparing what different leaders do.

lessons.title: Needs and Wants in Our Society
lessons.brief: Categorizing what people need to survive versus what they want, and how communities provide these.

lessons.title: Rights and Responsibilities
lessons.brief: Learning that citizens have rights to be safe and heard, and responsibilities to follow rules and help others.

lessons.title: Making Fair Decisions
lessons.brief: Exploring how groups make choices by voting, discussing, and finding solutions that work for everyone.

grade_4.focus: Examining the structure of local and regional government and how laws protect people and keep society organized.

lessons.title: How Local Government Works
lessons.brief: Understanding the roles of municipal councils, mayors, and local government in managing community resources and services.

lessons.title: Laws and Why Societies Create Them
lessons.brief: Tracing how laws are made, what they do, and how they connect to protecting people's rights and safety.

lessons.title: Systems of Service: From Water to Roads
lessons.brief: Mapping how different services and infrastructure systems are organized and maintained in a community.

lessons.title: Citizenship: Rights, Freedoms, and Duties
lessons.brief: Defining what it means to be a citizen and exploring the relationship between personal freedoms and community responsibilities.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how provincial and national government systems work and how citizens influence laws and policy.

lessons.title: Levels of Government and Their Powers
lessons.brief: Comparing the responsibilities of local, provincial, and federal governments and understanding how they interact.

lessons.title: How Laws Are Made: From Idea to Action
lessons.brief: Following the legislative process from when someone proposes an idea through debate, voting, and implementation.

lessons.title: Citizens as Voters and Participants
lessons.brief: Exploring how voting works, why elections matter, and what active citizenship looks like beyond voting.

lessons.title: Rights, Freedoms, and How We Protect Them
lessons.brief: Examining key rights in society like freedom of speech and equality, and how laws and courts protect these rights.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing power structures in government, examining how policy affects different groups, and evaluating civic participation.

lessons.title: Political Systems and How They Compare
lessons.brief: Examining different government structures around the world and analyzing how they distribute power differently.

lessons.title: Policy, Inequality, and Social Change
lessons.brief: Investigating how government decisions affect different groups unequally and tracing how citizens have pushed for change throughout history.

lessons.title: Media, Information, and Informed Citizenship
lessons.brief: Analyzing how media shapes public opinion, identifying bias and reliable sources, and evaluating claims about civic issues.

lessons.title: Civic Participation Beyond Voting
lessons.brief: Exploring activism, community organizing, advocacy, and how individuals and groups influence policy and social outcomes.

grade_7.focus: How democratic systems work: rights, responsibilities, and the structures that protect them.

lessons.title: What Are Rights and Where Do They Come From?
lessons.brief: Explores the difference between natural rights and legal rights, and how societies decide which rights matter.

lessons.title: How Parliament and Congress Make Laws
lessons.brief: Examines the role of elected representatives, the legislative process, and why checks and balances exist.

lessons.title: Voting: Who Gets to Vote and Why It Matters
lessons.brief: Traces the history of voting rights and explores how election systems shape who has power.

lessons.title: Courts, Justice, and the Rule of Law
lessons.brief: Introduces how courts work, the difference between criminal and civil law, and why an independent judiciary matters.

grade_8.focus: How power is distributed and contested: comparing different systems of government and identifying whose interests they serve.

lessons.title: Monarchy, Dictatorship, Democracy: Comparing Systems
lessons.brief: Analyzes how different governments distribute and limit power, and what each system promises and risks.

lessons.title: When Citizens Disagree: Political Ideologies and Parties
lessons.brief: Examines left-right political spectrum, how ideologies shape policy, and why reasonable people support different parties.

lessons.title: The Constitution as Living Document: Debate Over Interpretation
lessons.brief: Explores how constitutional meaning changes over time and why intelligent people interpret the same document differently.

lessons.title: Power Outside Government: Lobbying, Media, and Influence
lessons.brief: Investigates how interest groups, corporations, and media shape policy even when they don't hold office.

grade_9.focus: Building a personal civic framework: synthesizing how institutions, values, and history interact to create political reality.

lessons.title: How History Shaped Modern Institutions: Slavery, Suffrage, and Reform
lessons.brief: Connects historical injustices to present-day structures, showing how past conflicts echo in current debates.

lessons.title: Evaluating Arguments: Recognizing Bias, Rhetoric, and Evidence in Public Debate
lessons.brief: Develops critical reading skills to assess competing claims about policy, using real political speeches and opinion pieces.

lessons.title: Rights in Tension: When Freedom of Speech Meets Other Values
lessons.brief: Examines cases where rights conflict (e.g., free expression vs. safety, privacy vs. security) and how societies balance them.

lessons.title: Global Systems: How Different Nations Govern and Why That Matters
lessons.brief: Compares governance structures across continents and explores how international law and institutions attempt to solve shared problems.

grade_10.focus: Reading and interpreting the primary sources of civic life: constitutional documents, case law, policy, and historical testimony to understand how law and governance actually work.

lessons.title: Interpreting Constitutional Text: Close Reading and Judicial Philosophy
lessons.brief: Examines landmark Supreme Court cases and the different methodologies judges use to interpret the Constitution.

lessons.title: How Policy Actually Gets Written: From Proposal to Implementation
lessons.brief: Traces a real bill through legislature, analyzing compromises, lobbying, and the gap between intent and effect.

lessons.title: Civil Rights Through Documents: Petitions, Manifestos, and Legal Arguments
lessons.brief: Reads primary sources from freedom movements and analyzes the rhetorical and legal strategies used to demand change.

lessons.title: Economic Rights and Social Policy: Welfare, Labor, and the Market
lessons.brief: Examines how governments balance market freedom and social protection, using case studies and policy documents.

grade_11.focus: Developing rigorous critiques: comparing and evaluating competing frameworks for justice, legitimacy, and good governance.

lessons.title: Justice Theories in Conflict: Libertarian, Egalitarian, and Communitarian Approaches
lessons.brief: Compares philosophical frameworks that underlie real political debates and evaluates their internal consistency and practical consequences.

lessons.title: Legitimacy and Consent: What Makes a Government Actually Binding?
lessons.brief: Analyzes foundational theories of why we obey laws, from social contract to democratic mandate, and explores limits of obligation.

lessons.title: Institutional Analysis: Why Some Democracies Fail and Others Endure
lessons.brief: Examines structural features that strengthen or weaken democracies, using historical and contemporary examples to identify patterns.

lessons.title: Power, Knowledge, and Narrative: How Dominant Groups Shape Civic Discourse
lessons.brief: Applies critical theory to examine whose perspectives are centered in mainstream civics, media, and law—and what gets excluded.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent civic inquiry: researching, synthesizing evidence across sources, and building evidence-based arguments about governance, justice, and social change.

lessons.title: Research Design in Political Science: Methods, Sources, and Limits of Evidence
lessons.brief: Teaches evaluation of different research methodologies, identifying bias in data, and recognizing what questions remain unanswered.

lessons.title: Comparative Governance: Analyzing Real Institutional Choices and Their Outcomes
lessons.brief: Conducts original research comparing how different nations solve a shared problem, assessing tradeoffs and unexpected consequences.

lessons.title: Contemporary Policy Debates: Synthesizing Law, Economics, and Values
lessons.brief: Researches a live policy issue using legislative records, economic data, expert testimony, and ethical frameworks to develop independent position.

lessons.title: Building a Civic Vision: From Analysis to Advocacy and Action
lessons.brief: Integrates prior learning to articulate personal framework for justice, design an argument for change, and identify pathways to implementation.

grade_1.focus: Learning to name feelings and what makes them happen when people disagree.

lessons.title: What Does Angry Look Like?
lessons.brief: Students identify emotions in their bodies and faces during small disagreements.

lessons.title: When Toys Are Shared, Feelings Change
lessons.brief: Students see how the same thing (sharing) can make different feelings in different people.

lessons.title: My Words, Your Feelings
lessons.brief: Students learn that what they say affects how others feel, and practice gentle words.

grade_2.focus: Recognising that conflicts happen between people and learning simple ways to stop them getting worse.

lessons.title: Why Do We Fight Over Things?
lessons.brief: Students name common reasons for conflicts (toys, turns, space) and see the pattern.

lessons.title: The Calm-Down Trick
lessons.brief: Students learn and practise three ways to stop their body from staying angry (breathing, moving, waiting).

lessons.title: When Someone Is Upset With Me
lessons.brief: Students recognise signs that another person is upset and learn what *not* to do next.

lessons.title: Two People, Two Stories
lessons.brief: Students discover that both people in a fight think they're right and learn to listen to the other side.

grade_3.focus: Understanding that conflicts have causes and steps, and learning to solve small problems by talking.

lessons.title: How Conflicts Start and Grow
lessons.brief: Students map the sequence: something happens → feelings rise → words get sharp → conflict grows.

lessons.title: The Listening Skill
lessons.brief: Students practise waiting, looking, and repeating back what someone says without interrupting.

lessons.title: Finding the Real Problem
lessons.brief: Students learn to ask 'why' to discover what a conflict is *really* about (not just the surface fight).

lessons.title: Taking Turns to Talk
lessons.brief: Students use a structured turn-taking method to each say their side without shouting over each other.

grade_4.focus: Analysing the parts of a conflict and how they connect to solve problems using a fair process.

lessons.title: The Five Parts of Every Conflict
lessons.brief: Students identify the people involved, what happened, what each person wanted, what went wrong, and what the feelings were.

lessons.title: Positions vs. Interests: What Do You Really Want?
lessons.brief: Students distinguish between what someone says they want and what they actually need underneath.

lessons.title: The Four-Step Problem Solver
lessons.brief: Students learn and apply a repeatable process: describe the problem fairly, listen to all sides, brainstorm options, test a solution together.

lessons.title: Who Decides? Fair Ways to Choose
lessons.brief: Students compare different decision methods (voting, taking turns, coin flip, consensus) and when each is fair.

grade_5.focus: Examining why conflicts happen at deeper levels and designing solutions that address root causes, not just the fight.

lessons.title: Needs, Values, and Triggers: Why People React
lessons.brief: Students explore how unmet needs (safety, fairness, respect) and personal values drive conflict reactions.

lessons.title: Communication Patterns That Start and Fuel Conflicts
lessons.brief: Students analyse how tone, assumptions, blame language, and poor timing make conflicts worse and harder to solve.

lessons.title: Designing Solutions That Actually Work
lessons.brief: Students learn to test proposed solutions by asking: Is it fair to both sides? Can both people live with it? Will it prevent this problem next time?

lessons.title: When You Can't Solve It Alone
lessons.brief: Students identify when conflicts need a third person (mediator, teacher, trusted adult) and how to ask for that help.

grade_6.focus: Analysing conflict systems in groups and communities, and developing strategies for fair resolution that work across different contexts.

lessons.title: How Power, History, and Groups Shape Conflict
lessons.brief: Students examine how group identity, past disagreements, and unequal power complicate individual conflicts.

lessons.title: Bias in How We See Conflict
lessons.brief: Students identify their own blind spots and learn how assumptions about others distort what they see in a disagreement.

lessons.title: Designing Fair Systems for Groups
lessons.brief: Students apply principles of transparency, equal voice, and consequence to design conflict processes that work in a classroom or team.

lessons.title: Restorative Questions: Repair Instead of Punishment
lessons.brief: Students learn to use questions that focus on harm, responsibility, and fixing relationships instead of just assigning blame.

grade_7.focus: Recognizing conflict sources and practising basic strategies to resolve disagreements constructively.

lessons.title: What Triggers a Conflict?
lessons.brief: Students identify common sources of conflict (needs, values, resources, miscommunication) and recognize early warning signs in real situations.

lessons.title: Listening Without Defending
lessons.brief: Students learn active listening techniques and practise understanding another person's perspective before responding.

lessons.title: Finding the Middle Ground
lessons.brief: Students explore compromise and negotiation basics by working through peer disputes and school scenarios.

lessons.title: When to Ask for Help
lessons.brief: Students learn to recognize when a conflict is beyond peer resolution and identify appropriate adults or mediators.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating different conflict styles and understanding how personality and power dynamics shape disputes.

lessons.title: Five Ways People Fight
lessons.brief: Students analyse avoiding, accommodating, competing, compromising, and collaborating styles, then reflect on their own conflict patterns.

lessons.title: Power and Fairness in Arguments
lessons.brief: Students examine how differences in status, strength, or authority affect conflict outcomes and explore what 'fair' resolution means.

lessons.title: Reading Emotion in Conflict
lessons.brief: Students practise identifying underlying emotions (fear, anger, shame) in disputes and learn how emotions shape what people say and do.

lessons.title: Conflict in Groups vs. One-on-One
lessons.brief: Students compare how conflicts play out differently in pairs versus teams or classrooms, and why audience and reputation matter.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing conflict resolution methods into a personal framework and recognizing structural patterns in larger disputes.

lessons.title: Building Your Conflict Toolkit
lessons.brief: Students integrate lessons from previous years to design a personal decision-making process for choosing strategies based on context and goals.

lessons.title: Interests, Positions, and Needs
lessons.brief: Students learn to distinguish what people say they want (position) from what they actually need (interest) and use this to find creative solutions.

lessons.title: Cycles and Escalation
lessons.brief: Students trace how small conflicts spiral into bigger ones through cycles of action and reaction, and identify points to break the pattern.

lessons.title: Justice vs. Reconciliation
lessons.brief: Students explore whether conflict resolution should focus on fairness, healing, accountability, or some combination—with real historical examples.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting conflict in historical and contemporary contexts using primary sources and recognizing systemic factors beneath individual disputes.

lessons.title: Analysing Conflict Through Original Documents
lessons.brief: Students read letters, speeches, and testimony from real disputes (historical and recent) to identify underlying causes and rhetoric used by each side.

lessons.title: When Is Conflict Structural?
lessons.brief: Students distinguish personal conflicts from disputes rooted in systems of inequality, policy, or institutional power—and what each requires to resolve.

lessons.title: Ripple Effects: Unintended Consequences of Resolution
lessons.brief: Students examine cases where solving one conflict created new ones, and explore how solutions must account for wider impacts.

lessons.title: Neutrality, Bias, and Third-Party Roles
lessons.brief: Students investigate whether mediators can truly be neutral, how bias shapes intervention, and how different roles (arbitrator, mediator, advocate) affect outcomes.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing major conflict resolution frameworks and constructing evidence-based arguments about which approaches work best in different contexts.

lessons.title: Comparing Theories: Why Experts Disagree
lessons.brief: Students evaluate competing frameworks (game theory, social psychology, restorative justice, realism) and critique their assumptions and blind spots.

lessons.title: Conflict Resolution and Power: A Critique
lessons.brief: Students examine how resolution methods can reinforce or challenge existing power imbalances, and whether 'consensus' always serves justice.

lessons.title: Evidence, Anecdotes, and Myth in Conflict Work
lessons.brief: Students scrutinize claims about what 'works' in conflict resolution by evaluating research quality, alternative explanations, and cultural context.

lessons.title: Scaling Up: From Interpersonal to International
lessons.brief: Students investigate whether principles that work in school or small communities apply to wars, border disputes, and global tensions—and why or why not.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent research on conflict resolution and synthesizing insights across disciplines to develop a nuanced, evidence-based position on complex disputes.

lessons.title: Designing Your Own Conflict Research Question
lessons.brief: Students formulate, scope, and research an original question about conflict (historical, contemporary, or hypothetical) using multiple sources and methods.

lessons.title: Interdisciplinary Analysis: Psychology, History, and Systems
lessons.brief: Students integrate insights from psychology, history, economics, and political science to explain a single dispute and evaluate competing interpretations.

lessons.title: Ethics in Conflict Resolution Practice
lessons.brief: Students examine moral dilemmas faced by mediators, peacebuilders, and negotiators—including questions of complicity, harm, and whose voices matter.

lessons.title: Synthesis and Argument: What You Actually Believe Works
lessons.brief: Students produce a sustained argument about conflict resolution, grounded in research, that acknowledges limitations and explains when their approach applies.

grade_1.focus: Learning to name kitchen tools and ingredients, and using our senses to explore how food looks, feels, smells, and tastes.

lessons.title: Kitchen Tools We Hold and Use
lessons.brief: Exploring spoons, knives, pans, and bowls—what they are, what they feel like, and what we do with them.

lessons.title: Fruits and Vegetables: Colours, Shapes, and Textures
lessons.brief: Touching, looking at, and smelling fresh produce to learn their names and notice differences.

lessons.title: Mixing, Pouring, and Breaking Foods Apart
lessons.brief: Using hands and tools to mix, pour, crumble, and tear ingredients and noticing what happens.

lessons.title: Hot and Cold: Safe Cooking Words
lessons.brief: Learning what 'hot', 'cold', 'raw', and 'cooked' mean through touching (safely) and tasting.

grade_2.focus: Following simple recipes step-by-step and understanding that mixing ingredients in order creates food we can eat.

lessons.title: Reading a Recipe: Steps and Pictures
lessons.brief: Learning how recipes tell us what to do first, second, and third using words and images.

lessons.title: Wet Ingredients and Dry Ingredients: What's the Difference?
lessons.brief: Sorting and naming ingredients by whether they pour, crumble, or stick together.

lessons.title: Simple Recipes We Can Make: No Cooking Required
lessons.brief: Making sandwiches, fruit salads, and no-bake snacks by following steps in order.

lessons.title: What Happens When We Mix Things Together
lessons.brief: Observing how ingredients change when we stir, blend, or combine them.

grade_3.focus: Categorising ingredients and equipment, and discovering that heat changes food in different ways.

lessons.title: Sorting Ingredients: Grains, Proteins, Vegetables, and Dairy
lessons.brief: Grouping foods by type and learning which group does what for our bodies.

lessons.title: Heat Makes Food Change: Cooking vs. Not Cooking
lessons.brief: Comparing raw and cooked versions of the same food and describing how they look and taste different.

lessons.title: Kitchen Equipment Families: Measuring, Mixing, and Heating
lessons.brief: Organising tools by their job and learning why we use each one.

lessons.title: Following a Recipe from Start to Finish
lessons.brief: Making a simple hot dish (baked goods or stovetop meal) by reading and completing all steps in order.

grade_4.focus: Understanding cooking methods as systems where heat, time, and ingredients work together to transform food.

lessons.title: Cooking Methods and How They Work: Baking, Boiling, Frying, and Steaming
lessons.brief: Learning how different heat methods (dry, wet, oil, steam) affect food differently and when to use each one.

lessons.title: Timing and Temperature: Why Recipes Tell Us How Hot and How Long
lessons.brief: Exploring how heat level and cooking duration change the result, and why recipes specify both.

lessons.title: Ingredients Work Together: Ratios and Substitutions
lessons.brief: Understanding that some ingredients do specific jobs and learning what happens if you change amounts or swap them.

lessons.title: Planning a Meal: Choosing Recipes That Work Together
lessons.brief: Selecting multiple dishes, managing timing so food is ready together, and thinking about variety.

grade_5.focus: Asking 'why' about cooking—exploring the science of how ingredients interact, how heat works, and how to adapt recipes when things go wrong.

lessons.title: Why Heat Transforms Food: Chemical Changes During Cooking
lessons.brief: Learning how proteins set, starches soften, and colours change when heat is applied, and why it matters.

lessons.title: Flavor, Texture, and Balance: How Ingredients Create Taste
lessons.brief: Exploring how salt, acid, fat, and spices work together, and why balance makes food taste better.

lessons.title: Fixing Cooking Mistakes: Diagnosing and Solving Problems
lessons.brief: Learning what went wrong when food burns, doesn't cook, tastes flat, or falls apart—and how to prevent it next time.

lessons.title: Adapting Recipes: Making Substitutions and Scaling Amounts
lessons.brief: Understanding why you can swap similar ingredients and how to double or halve a recipe without ruining it.

grade_6.focus: Thinking analytically about food systems: how culture shapes cooking, how nutrition connects to ingredients, and how different cuisines solve the same cooking problems differently.

lessons.title: Cuisines Around the World: How Culture, Geography, and Ingredients Connect
lessons.brief: Examining why different cultures use different methods, spices, and ingredients, and how climate and history shape food.

lessons.title: Nutrition, Ingredients, and Health: Reading Labels and Planning Balanced Meals
lessons.brief: Learning how to evaluate what's in food, understand nutritional needs, and build meals that are both tasty and nourishing.

lessons.title: Technique Mastery: Why Professional Cooks Do Things a Certain Way
lessons.brief: Exploring the reasoning behind professional methods—knife skills, temperature precision, mise en place—and how they prevent mistakes.

lessons.title: Food Waste and Smart Shopping: Planning Meals from What You Have
lessons.brief: Learning to inventory ingredients, plan meals strategically, and reduce waste while still eating well.

grade_7.focus: Master fundamental cooking techniques and understand how ingredients behave through heat and time.

lessons.title: Heat, Time, and Transformation
lessons.brief: How different cooking methods (boiling, frying, baking, steaming) change food at the molecular level and why timing matters.

lessons.title: Building Flavour Through Layering
lessons.brief: How to combine acids, fats, salt, and spices to create depth and balance in simple dishes.

lessons.title: Reading a Recipe Like an Instruction Manual
lessons.brief: Decoding recipe language, understanding mise en place, and troubleshooting common mistakes.

lessons.title: Where Food Comes From: Local vs. Global Ingredients
lessons.brief: Tracing the journey of common ingredients and how seasonality and geography affect what we cook.

grade_8.focus: Evaluate cooking traditions and techniques across cultures, and understand the 'why' behind regional food practices.

lessons.title: Why Cultures Cook the Way They Do
lessons.brief: How geography, climate, available ingredients, and history shaped distinct cooking styles in different regions.

lessons.title: Technique Variations: One Dish, Many Approaches
lessons.brief: Comparing how the same dish (e.g., dumplings, stew, bread) is made differently across cultures and evaluating the trade-offs.

lessons.title: Food Preservation Then and Now
lessons.brief: Exploring pickling, fermenting, smoking, and salting as both historical necessity and modern flavour choice.

lessons.title: Ingredients Under Scrutiny: Sugar, Salt, and Fat
lessons.brief: Investigating the role and debate around key ingredients—what they do, why they're used, and when alternatives work.

grade_9.focus: Synthesise food science, nutrition, and cooking practice to make informed, intentional choices about what and how to cook.

lessons.title: Proteins, Starches, and Fats: How They Behave and Why It Matters
lessons.brief: Connecting food chemistry to technique—why proteins denature, starches gelatinise, and fats emulsify, and how to use this knowledge.

lessons.title: Designing a Meal: Nutrition, Flavour, and Budget
lessons.brief: Building balanced dishes that meet nutritional needs while controlling cost and creating cohesive flavour profiles.

lessons.title: Substitutions and Adaptations: When and How They Work
lessons.brief: Understanding which ingredients can be swapped and which cannot; creating recipes for dietary restrictions with scientific reasoning.

lessons.title: The Global Food System: Tracing Ethics and Impact
lessons.brief: Examining where ingredients come from, the environmental and labour practices involved, and how consumer choices matter.

grade_10.focus: Interpret original culinary sources and analyse food systems, developing a personal cooking philosophy grounded in evidence.

lessons.title: Reading Historical Recipes and Adapting Them for Today
lessons.brief: Decoding archaic cookbooks and manuscripts, understanding historical context, and making informed adjustments for modern ingredients and palates.

lessons.title: The Science of Flavour Pairing: Evidence and Intuition
lessons.brief: Examining flavour pairing theories (aromatic compounds, umami, cultural tradition) and testing them against real-world cooking.

lessons.title: Food Systems and Supply Chains: Following One Ingredient
lessons.brief: Tracing a single ingredient from production through distribution to plate, analysing environmental, economic, and social implications.

lessons.title: Cooking for Health vs. Cooking for Pleasure: Finding Balance
lessons.brief: Evaluating nutritional science claims, understanding taste preferences, and crafting a personal approach to eating well.

grade_11.focus: Critique culinary frameworks, compare competing food philosophies, and construct evidence-based arguments about food, cooking, and culture.

lessons.title: Interrogating 'Authenticity' in Food Culture
lessons.brief: Critiquing the concept of authentic cuisine, examining power dynamics in food narratives, and analysing how tradition and innovation coexist.

lessons.title: Competing Nutritional Paradigms: Separating Science from Marketing
lessons.brief: Comparing frameworks (low-fat, low-carb, plant-based, ancestral diets) by evaluating evidence quality, identifying bias, and understanding context.

lessons.title: Sustainability in Food: Environmental, Economic, and Social Dimensions
lessons.brief: Analysing trade-offs between local, organic, conventional, and industrial food systems; evaluating claims with real data.

lessons.title: The Politics of Taste: How Food Reflects and Shapes Society
lessons.brief: Exploring how taste, status, identity, and access to food intersect; examining culinary gatekeeping and whose voices dominate food discourse.

grade_12.focus: Conduct independent research in food studies, synthesise across disciplines, and develop a nuanced, evidence-based perspective on contemporary food issues.

lessons.title: Food Systems Research: Designing and Interpreting Original Inquiry
lessons.brief: Conducting primary research (interviews, experiments, analysis) on a food-related question; evaluating methodology and limitations.

lessons.title: The Future of Food: Technology, Sustainability, and Ethics in Conversation
lessons.brief: Examining emerging food technologies (lab-grown meat, precision fermentation, vertical farming) through ecological, ethical, economic, and cultural lenses.

lessons.title: Deconstructing Food Media: Rhetoric, Evidence, and Influence
lessons.brief: Critically analysing cookbooks, food documentaries, influencer content, and advertising to identify persuasion techniques, bias, and reliability.

lessons.title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Food Justice
lessons.brief: Synthesising perspectives from nutrition, economics, anthropology, and environmental science to understand and critique food inequality systems.

grade_1.focus: Learning to notice things carefully and ask simple questions about what you see.

lessons.title: What Do I See?
lessons.brief: Using your eyes and ears to notice details about objects and people around you.

lessons.title: Why Did That Happen?
lessons.brief: Finding simple reasons for everyday things (why did the ball roll, why did it rain).

lessons.title: Same or Different?
lessons.brief: Spotting what is the same and what is different between two things.

grade_2.focus: Describing what things do and how they work in everyday life.

lessons.title: How Things Work Around Us
lessons.brief: Naming and describing what happens when you use a door, a cup, shoes, or a toy.

lessons.title: What Comes First?
lessons.brief: Following the order of events (first, next, last) in a simple story or activity.

lessons.title: Sorting Things Into Groups
lessons.brief: Putting objects into categories based on what they look like or what they do.

lessons.title: When Something Goes Wrong
lessons.brief: Figuring out what happened when something breaks or doesn't work as expected.

grade_3.focus: Understanding cause and effect, and learning vocabulary to talk about how things connect.

lessons.title: Why Did That Cause That?
lessons.brief: Connecting actions to results (if I push the swing, it moves; if I water a plant, it grows).

lessons.title: Fact or Guess?
lessons.brief: Telling the difference between what you know for sure and what you are making up.

lessons.title: Grouping by Features
lessons.brief: Sorting things by colour, size, shape, or how they work, and explaining your choices.

lessons.title: Steps in a Process
lessons.brief: Following and describing the stages of how something happens (planting seeds, cooking, building).

grade_4.focus: Seeing how parts of a system work together and how one change affects another.

lessons.title: Parts Working as a Team
lessons.brief: Learning how different parts of something (a bicycle, a body, a classroom) depend on each other.

lessons.title: Finding the Main Idea
lessons.brief: Picking out the most important message from a story, article, or explanation.

lessons.title: Chains of Cause and Effect
lessons.brief: Tracing how one action leads to another, which leads to another (dominoes of events).

lessons.title: Comparing Methods and Solutions
lessons.brief: Looking at different ways to solve a problem and deciding which might work best and why.

grade_5.focus: Asking deeper 'why' questions and understanding how processes work over time and in sequence.

lessons.title: Asking Better Questions
lessons.brief: Moving beyond 'what' to ask 'why,' 'how,' and 'what if' to dig deeper into a topic.

lessons.title: Assumptions: What We Think We Know
lessons.brief: Identifying the beliefs we hold without proof and testing whether they are actually true.

lessons.title: Evidence and Reasons
lessons.brief: Learning to support an idea with examples, facts, or observations instead of just opinions.

lessons.title: Patterns Across Time
lessons.brief: Spotting patterns in nature, history, behaviour, and systems to predict what might happen next.

grade_6.focus: Thinking analytically across systems and seeing how complex ideas connect to each other and the wider world.

lessons.title: Evaluating Claims and Sources
lessons.brief: Deciding whether a claim is reliable by checking the source, evidence, and potential bias.

lessons.title: Systems Within Systems
lessons.brief: Analysing how nested systems (person → community → city → country) interact and influence each other.

lessons.title: Trade-offs and Consequences
lessons.brief: Understanding that choices have multiple effects, and weighing benefits against costs in real scenarios.

lessons.title: Connecting Knowledge Across Subjects
lessons.brief: Using ideas from science, history, maths, and art to think critically about problems and situations.

grade_7.focus: Identifying the structure of arguments and recognizing common logical fallacies in everyday claims.

lessons.title: Claims, Evidence, and Reasoning
lessons.brief: Learning to break down any argument into its three core parts and evaluate whether the evidence actually supports the claim.

lessons.title: Spotting Logical Fallacies in Real Debates
lessons.brief: Recognizing ad hominem attacks, false dilemmas, appeals to authority, and other common tricks used to manipulate thinking.

lessons.title: Sources: Who's Speaking and Why
lessons.brief: Evaluating the credibility of a source by examining their expertise, bias, and motivation to tell the truth.

lessons.title: Building Your Own Argument
lessons.brief: Constructing a simple, clear argument with evidence that actually supports your claim without logical fallacies.

grade_8.focus: Analyzing multiple perspectives on the same issue and evaluating the strength of competing arguments.

lessons.title: Steelman vs. Strawman: Arguing Against the Best Version
lessons.brief: Learning to present opposing views fairly and strongly before responding, rather than attacking weak versions of arguments.

lessons.title: Weighing Evidence: Which Argument Is Stronger?
lessons.brief: Comparing two arguments on the same topic by examining the quality, relevance, and amount of evidence each one presents.

lessons.title: Bias, Confirmation, and Echo Chambers
lessons.brief: Identifying how personal beliefs create bias, why we seek out confirming information, and how this limits our thinking.

lessons.title: The Middle Ground Trap
lessons.brief: Recognizing when a compromise between two positions is wise and when splitting the difference actually avoids the real issue.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing ideas from different sources and building a coherent personal position on complex issues.

lessons.title: Mapping a Debate: Finding the Root Disagreement
lessons.brief: Analyzing multiple arguments on an issue to identify what fundamental assumptions or values the disagreement actually rests on.

lessons.title: Assembling Your Argument from Multiple Sources
lessons.brief: Gathering claims and evidence from different thinkers, identifying where they agree or conflict, and weaving them into a unified position.

lessons.title: Testing Your Own Reasoning
lessons.brief: Applying the same critical tools you use on others' arguments to your own beliefs to find inconsistencies and weak points.

lessons.title: Distinguishing Fact from Interpretation
lessons.brief: Learning how the same factual information can be interpreted differently based on framework, values, or what you choose to emphasize.

grade_10.focus: Reading original sources with nuance and building arguments grounded in textual evidence and historical context.

lessons.title: Reading Between the Lines: What Authors Don't Say Directly
lessons.brief: Inferring unstated assumptions, intended audience, and historical context from a primary source to understand its full meaning.

lessons.title: Evaluating Primary Sources: Credibility, Motivation, and Limitation
lessons.brief: Assessing how reliable a first-hand account is by considering the author's knowledge, position, possible motives, and what they couldn't have witnessed.

lessons.title: Building Arguments From Text: Quote, Explain, Prove
lessons.brief: Using evidence from sources effectively by selecting the right quote, explaining its meaning, and showing how it proves your larger point.

lessons.title: Contradiction and Complexity in Historical Narratives
lessons.brief: Handling conflicting accounts and nuance by examining multiple perspectives on the same historical event without forcing false resolution.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing different philosophical and analytical frameworks and constructing independent, evidence-based arguments.

lessons.title: Comparing Frameworks: Utilitarian, Deontological, and Virtue-Based Thinking
lessons.brief: Analyzing how different ethical frameworks lead to different conclusions on the same moral question and assessing their strengths and limits.

lessons.title: Interrogating Assumptions: What Is This Framework Built On?
lessons.brief: Identifying the unstated premises and value judgments underlying different intellectual frameworks and deciding whether to accept them.

lessons.title: Constructing a Defensible Position Across Disciplinary Boundaries
lessons.brief: Building an original argument that draws evidence and logic from history, science, ethics, or other fields while defending it against counterarguments.

lessons.title: The Limits of Evidence: When Does Data Prove Something?
lessons.brief: Understanding correlation vs. causation, statistical significance, sample bias, and the gap between evidence and certainty in real research.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent research, synthesizing across disciplines, and presenting original arguments at university-ready depth.

lessons.title: Designing a Research Question That Matters
lessons.brief: Formulating a question that is specific enough to research but broad enough to be meaningful, and that avoids confirmation-seeking bias.

lessons.title: Evaluating and Synthesizing Peer-Reviewed and Popular Sources
lessons.brief: Distinguishing reliable scholarship from opinion, identifying methodology flaws, and integrating conflicting findings into a coherent narrative.

lessons.title: Making an Original Argument in Conversation with Existing Scholarship
lessons.brief: Positioning your own thesis in relation to established work, showing what is new about your thinking and why it matters beyond the academy.

lessons.title: Defending Your Reasoning Against Sophisticated Objections
lessons.brief: Anticipating and responding to complex counterarguments, acknowledging limitations of your evidence, and distinguishing between refinement and retreat.

grade_1.focus: Learning to move your body in different ways and noticing how movement feels.

lessons.title: Moving Like Animals
lessons.brief: Students copy how real animals walk, jump, and crawl to discover their own body can move in many ways.

lessons.title: Fast and Slow
lessons.brief: Students explore moving quickly and slowly, feeling how their muscles and breathing change.

lessons.title: Dancing with Sounds
lessons.brief: Students move their bodies in response to different sounds and music, learning that movement and sound go together.

grade_2.focus: Naming different movements and learning that dancers can tell stories with their bodies.

lessons.title: Steps and Turns
lessons.brief: Students learn names for basic movements like walking, skipping, spinning, and bending, and practice each one.

lessons.title: Moving Through Space
lessons.brief: Students discover they can move forwards, backwards, sideways, and in circles, and that the floor is their stage.

lessons.title: Telling a Story Without Words
lessons.brief: Students act out a simple story (like getting ready for bed) using only movement, learning that dance can show feelings and actions.

lessons.title: Loud and Quiet Movements
lessons.brief: Students compare big, noisy movements with small, gentle movements and match them to different kinds of music.

grade_3.focus: Understanding the different parts of the body and how they work together to create balanced, controlled dance.

lessons.title: Heads, Arms, Legs: Moving Separately
lessons.brief: Students isolate different body parts and move them independently, discovering how each part has its own range of motion.

lessons.title: Finding Your Balance Point
lessons.brief: Students explore their center of gravity, learning why some movements feel stable and others wobbly, and how balance keeps dancers safe.

lessons.title: Levels: High, Middle, and Low
lessons.brief: Students move at different heights—standing tall, moving in the middle, crouching low—and notice how levels change the look of a dance.

lessons.title: Rhythm Patterns in Movement
lessons.brief: Students clap and move to repeating beat patterns, learning that dance, like music, follows patterns that repeat.

grade_4.focus: Recognizing how basic dance vocabulary, rhythm, and intentional body control combine to create technique.

lessons.title: Alignment: Standing Tall
lessons.brief: Students learn correct posture and alignment—how their skeleton should line up—and practice how good alignment makes movements cleaner and safer.

lessons.title: Combining Steps into Sequences
lessons.brief: Students link simple steps together in order and repeat them, understanding that dance is made of connected movement sequences.

lessons.title: Tempo and Counting Music
lessons.brief: Students count beats and phrases in music, learning to move in time with rhythm and adjust their speed to match different tempos.

lessons.title: The Role of Weight and Force
lessons.brief: Students explore how using different amounts of weight and effort (light, heavy, sharp, smooth) changes how a movement looks and feels.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how choreography is built from movement choices and understanding the relationship between body, music, and meaning.

lessons.title: Choreographic Choices: Why Dancers Move That Way
lessons.brief: Students examine why a choreographer chooses specific movements, levels, and directions, and how those choices create effect and emotion.

lessons.title: Exploring Movement Quality
lessons.brief: Students study Laban Effort—how movement has qualities like sustained or percussive, smooth or jagged—and use these qualities to express different ideas.

lessons.title: Building Your Own Short Phrase
lessons.brief: Students create a sequence of 8–16 counts with a beginning, middle, and end, practicing how to compose dance intentionally.

lessons.title: How Dance Responds to Music Structure
lessons.brief: Students listen for sections in music (verse, chorus, bridge) and experiment with how movement can echo or contrast those structures.

grade_6.focus: Synthesizing technique, cultural styles, and personal expression to understand dance as communication across different traditions and forms.

lessons.title: Origins and Purpose: Why Cultures Dance
lessons.brief: Students explore how dance serves different purposes across cultures—celebration, storytelling, ritual, social bonding—and how those purposes shape movement.

lessons.title: Technical Foundations Across Dance Styles
lessons.brief: Students compare core technique principles in different styles (ballet alignment, hip-hop isolation, contemporary flow) and analyze why each style developed its own language.

lessons.title: Interpreting Choreography: Reading the Dancer's Choice
lessons.brief: Students watch and analyze professional dance, identifying choreographic themes, spatial patterns, and how movement communicates mood and narrative.

lessons.title: Creating Meaning Through Movement
lessons.brief: Students design a short solo or group piece that combines learned technique with personal or cultural expression, reflecting on how their choices create meaning.

grade_7.focus: Dance as a language: how movement communicates meaning across cultures and time periods.

lessons.title: What Does a Movement Mean? Gesture and Symbol in Dance
lessons.brief: Students learn how the same gesture carries different meanings in different cultures and contexts.

lessons.title: Dance Tells Stories: Narrative Forms from Ballet to Hip-Hop
lessons.brief: Students explore how dance creates narrative through structure, character, and sequence.

lessons.title: Why Do Cultures Dance? Ritual, Celebration, and Survival
lessons.brief: Students investigate the social and spiritual functions of dance across historical societies.

grade_8.focus: The body as evidence: how dancers' choices reflect (and sometimes challenge) the values of their time.

lessons.title: Who Gets to Move? Gender, Power, and the Dancing Body
lessons.brief: Students examine how social rules about gender have shaped what dancers—especially women—were allowed to do.

lessons.title: From Court to Street: How Dance Reflected Social Change
lessons.brief: Students trace how dance styles shifted when power structures changed (e.g., ballet under monarchy vs. modern dance in the 20th century).

lessons.title: The Body Doesn't Lie: Reading Emotion and Intent in Movement
lessons.brief: Students learn to interpret what a dancer's posture, rhythm, and effort reveal about the choreographer's intent or cultural context.

lessons.title: Dance as Resistance: When Movement Breaks Rules
lessons.brief: Students analyse dances that challenged social norms—from flapper dances to protest movements—and why authorities sometimes banned them.

grade_9.focus: Dance as a mirror and tool: examining how choreography both reflects and shapes identity, politics, and belonging.

lessons.title: Movement and Memory: How Dance Preserves Cultural Identity
lessons.brief: Students investigate how communities use dance to maintain identity during displacement, oppression, or cultural change.

lessons.title: Choreographing Power: Authority, Representation, and Who Gets Seen
lessons.brief: Students analyse whose stories get told through major dance institutions and how marginalized artists have created alternative platforms.

lessons.title: The Body as Text: Race, Ethnicity, and Movement Vocabulary
lessons.brief: Students examine how movement styles have been claimed, appropriated, or racialized, and what that reveals about access and ownership.

lessons.title: Dance and Activism: When Choreography Becomes Political Statement
lessons.brief: Students study specific dances created in response to social movements and learn how movement can articulate resistance.

grade_10.focus: Reading dance as primary source: using movement, notation, and documentation to understand historical claims and artistic intent.

lessons.title: Decoding the Archive: How Notations, Video, and Memory Shape Our Understanding of Lost Dances
lessons.brief: Students learn multiple notation systems (Labanotation, Benesh) and evaluate how documentation choices affect what we know about historical dances.

lessons.title: The Choreographer's Argument: Analysing Intent Through Form and Structure
lessons.brief: Students close-read choreography as texts with deliberate formal choices that make claims about time, community, or the body.

lessons.title: Dance in Dialogue: How Artists Reference, Critique, and Revise Each Other's Work
lessons.brief: Students trace how choreographers explicitly or implicitly respond to earlier works, creating lineages and counter-arguments.

lessons.title: The Politics of Technique: Who Teaches What, and Why It Matters
lessons.brief: Students examine how dance training systems (ballet, contemporary, hip-hop) encode cultural values and who benefits from each form's gatekeeping.

grade_11.focus: Comparative frameworks: critically evaluating competing theories of what dance means, does, and represents across disciplines.

lessons.title: Whose Theory Is It? Decolonizing Dance Scholarship and Practice
lessons.brief: Students critique Western academic approaches to dance history and explore alternative frameworks from non-Western scholars.

lessons.title: Dance and the Body: Biomechanics, Phenomenology, and What It Means to Be Present
lessons.brief: Students engage with philosophical and scientific approaches to embodiment and evaluate how each shapes what choreographers create.

lessons.title: The Audience Effect: How Documentation, Venue, and Spectatorship Change a Dance's Meaning
lessons.brief: Students analyse how the same choreography functions differently in a concert hall, on film, in a museum, or online—and examine what is gained or lost.

lessons.title: Making an Argument in Movement: Comparing Dance to Other Forms of Knowledge
lessons.brief: Students develop claims about what dance can express or prove that writing, visual art, or speech cannot.

grade_12.focus: Independent inquiry: students pose original research questions about dance and construct evidence-based arguments using primary and secondary sources.

lessons.title: Designing a Dance History Research Project: From Question to Evidence
lessons.brief: Students learn to formulate researchable questions, locate and evaluate primary sources (video, notation, interviews, reviews), and build historical arguments.

lessons.title: Dance Across Disciplines: What Choreography Reveals About Economics, Medicine, Technology, or Philosophy
lessons.brief: Students synthesise dance with other fields—examining how artists respond to scientific discovery, economic change, or intellectual movements.

lessons.title: Critical Curation: Designing an Exhibition or Program That Makes an Argument
lessons.brief: Students learn how the selection and sequencing of dances makes a claim, and design a curated experience (exhibition, festival, program) that articulates a thesis.

lessons.title: Responding Choreographically: Creating New Work in Dialogue with Existing Scholarship
lessons.brief: Students develop an original choreographic response to a historical or theoretical problem they've studied, articulating what their movement contributes to scholarly conversation.

grade_1.focus: Learning what digital devices are and what we can do with them using our hands and senses.

lessons.title: Buttons, Screens, and Keyboards
lessons.brief: Explore the parts of a computer or tablet we can touch and see, and what happens when we press them.

lessons.title: Pictures and Words on a Screen
lessons.brief: Learn to find and name things displayed on digital devices, like icons, letters, and photos.

lessons.title: Using a Mouse and Trackpad
lessons.brief: Practice moving and clicking to make things happen on a screen.

lessons.title: On and Off: Making Devices Wake Up and Sleep
lessons.brief: Understand how to safely start and stop digital devices.

grade_2.focus: Naming what digital devices do and describing how we use them for different tasks.

lessons.title: Computers, Tablets, and Phones Do Different Jobs
lessons.brief: Compare different digital devices and describe what makes each one special and useful.

lessons.title: Apps and Programs: Tools on Our Devices
lessons.brief: Identify and name different apps, and explain what each one helps us do.

lessons.title: Typing and Writing Words Digitally
lessons.brief: Practice entering text using a keyboard or touchscreen, and see it appear on screen.

lessons.title: Files, Folders, and Finding Things
lessons.brief: Learn how devices organize and store pictures, documents, and other things we create.

grade_3.focus: Understanding how digital devices follow simple instructions and how to organize information digitally.

lessons.title: Instructions Make Devices Work
lessons.brief: Explore how clicking, typing, and dragging are instructions that make the device respond in predictable ways.

lessons.title: Organizing Digital Information into Categories
lessons.brief: Sort files and photos into folders and subfolders, and explain why sorting helps us find things.

lessons.title: Basic Typing and Text Editing
lessons.brief: Write sentences on a device, use backspace to fix mistakes, and format text with bold or different sizes.

lessons.title: What Is a Digital File?
lessons.brief: Learn that pictures, documents, and videos are all files with names and types.

grade_4.focus: Recognizing that digital devices are systems made of connected parts that work together to process information.

lessons.title: Hardware and Software: The Physical and Invisible Parts
lessons.brief: Distinguish between the parts you can touch (hardware) and the invisible instructions that make devices work (software).

lessons.title: How Input Becomes Output on a Device
lessons.brief: Trace a complete path: typing or clicking an input → the device processes it → something appears on screen as output.

lessons.title: Saving, Copying, and Moving Digital Work
lessons.brief: Manage your own files by creating, saving, duplicating, and organizing documents and media.

lessons.title: What Is a Browser and How Do We Explore the Internet?
lessons.brief: Learn that a browser is a tool that helps us visit and view websites, and understand addresses (URLs) on the web.

grade_5.focus: Explaining how digital information travels, is stored, and processed in sequences that follow logical rules.

lessons.title: From Device to Network: How Information Travels
lessons.brief: Understand that devices connect to each other and to the internet through networks, and data moves between them.

lessons.title: Storing and Backing Up Your Digital Information
lessons.brief: Learn why backing up files matters, and explain the difference between saving on a device versus cloud storage.

lessons.title: Step-by-Step Instructions: Creating Simple Sequences
lessons.brief: Write clear numbered instructions that tell a device or person to perform a task in order, and test whether the sequence works.

lessons.title: Searching, Filtering, and Finding Data
lessons.brief: Use search tools and filters to locate specific information in files, folders, and websites efficiently.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how digital systems interconnect across the world, and how data is processed, shared, and represented.

lessons.title: The Internet as a Global System of Connected Networks
lessons.brief: Explore how the internet links billions of devices worldwide, and understand basic concepts like IP addresses and servers.

lessons.title: Data Representation: Numbers, Images, and Code
lessons.brief: Discover that all digital information—text, images, sound—is encoded as numbers and binary code that computers understand.

lessons.title: Algorithms: How Devices Make Decisions and Solve Problems
lessons.brief: Analyze real-world algorithms (sorting, searching, recommendations) and recognize patterns in how digital systems follow logical rules.

lessons.title: Digital Citizenship: Sharing, Privacy, and Safety Online
lessons.brief: Examine the consequences of digital sharing, discuss what personal information is and why protecting it matters, and identify online risks.

grade_7.focus: How digital tools shape the way we communicate, create, and share information.

lessons.title: The Hidden Rules of Social Media Algorithms
lessons.brief: Students learn how feeds are personalized, why certain posts appear, and how algorithms influence what they see.

lessons.title: Spotting Fake Images and Manipulated Media
lessons.brief: Students practice identifying doctored photos, deepfakes, and misleading visual content online.

lessons.title: From Private Message to Public: Digital Permanence
lessons.brief: Students explore what happens to data they share online, who can access it, and why deletion isn't always permanent.

lessons.title: Building Your Digital Footprint Intentionally
lessons.brief: Students audit their own online presence and make decisions about what they want to be known for digitally.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating information quality and recognizing persuasion techniques across digital platforms.

lessons.title: Source Credibility: Comparing News Sites, Blogs, and Social Posts
lessons.brief: Students develop criteria to judge whether a digital source is reliable and learn why the same story differs across platforms.

lessons.title: Sponsored Content and Native Advertising: When Ads Hide
lessons.brief: Students identify how brands embed marketing into entertainment, influencer posts, and news to blur the line between content and selling.

lessons.title: Emotional Reasoning Online: How Posts Manipulate Anger and Outrage
lessons.brief: Students analyze how language, images, and headlines trigger emotional reactions and why that matters for critical thinking.

lessons.title: The Case For and Against Digital Privacy Laws
lessons.brief: Students examine arguments on both sides of data protection regulation and weigh competing values like privacy and innovation.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing multiple perspectives on digital technology's impact on society, identity, and power.

lessons.title: How Recommendation Algorithms Shape Worldviews
lessons.brief: Students trace how feed personalization can create filter bubbles, expose diverse views, or radicalize users—and examine real examples.

lessons.title: Digital Identity: Performance vs. Authenticity Across Platforms
lessons.brief: Students analyze how people present different versions of themselves on different platforms and what this reveals about identity in the digital age.

lessons.title: Who Profits From Your Data? Tracing the Value Chain
lessons.brief: Students map how personal data flows from collection to sale to use, identifying who benefits and who pays the hidden cost.

lessons.title: Disinformation Campaigns: Anatomy of a Digital Lie
lessons.brief: Students deconstruct a real disinformation case study to understand how false narratives are created, amplified, and believed at scale.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting original digital sources and understanding the political, economic, and cultural forces shaping technology policy.

lessons.title: Reading Platform Terms of Service: What You Actually Agreed To
lessons.brief: Students parse dense legal language from real platforms to understand data ownership, liability, and user rights.

lessons.title: Surveillance Capitalism: Unpacking the Business Model Behind 'Free' Services
lessons.brief: Students examine how platforms monetize attention and data, drawing on case studies and primary sources from company filings and research.

lessons.title: The Global Digital Divide: Access, Literacy, and Power Imbalances
lessons.brief: Students analyze disparities in internet access, digital skills, and technology use across countries and socioeconomic groups, using data and interviews.

lessons.title: Content Moderation at Scale: Free Speech vs. Harm Prevention
lessons.brief: Students examine how platforms make decisions about what content to remove or amplify and engage with competing frameworks for moderation.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing competing frameworks for understanding digital power, and constructing evidence-based arguments about technology's role in society.

lessons.title: Comparing Theories of Digital Influence: Individual Agency vs. Systemic Design
lessons.brief: Students compare perspectives (behavioral economics, critical theory, tech utopianism, regulation-focused) to evaluate competing explanations for why people behave online as they do.

lessons.title: Ethical Frameworks in AI and Automation: Whose Values Get Coded?
lessons.brief: Students examine how design choices embed values in algorithms, who decides those values, and analyze case studies where AI systems produced biased or harmful outcomes.

lessons.title: Digital Activism and Manipulation: When Online Movements Succeed or Fail
lessons.brief: Students analyze the mechanisms behind digital campaigns—from grassroots movements to astroturfing—to understand when digital organizing creates real change.

lessons.title: Building an Argument: Technology Policy and the Common Good
lessons.brief: Students construct evidence-based positions on a technology policy question (encryption, regulation, innovation) by integrating multiple stakeholder perspectives.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent research and synthesis on digital technology's relationship to power, knowledge, and justice across disciplines.

lessons.title: Research Seminar: Tracing Digital Infrastructure and Global Inequality
lessons.brief: Students conduct original research on how digital systems (cables, data centers, devices) are distributed globally and who bears environmental and labor costs.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Evidence: Building a Case Study on Platform Governance and Democratic Participation
lessons.brief: Students synthesize journalism, academic research, platform data, and policy documents to construct an argument about how one platform shapes political discourse.

lessons.title: Critiquing Digital Utopias and Dystopias: Analyzing Competing Narratives
lessons.brief: Students compare how different stakeholders (technologists, activists, regulators, scholars) construct narratives about digital futures and evaluate the evidence behind each.

lessons.title: Independent Project: Designing a Technology Intervention and Defending Its Assumptions
lessons.brief: Students propose a solution to a digital literacy, equity, or policy challenge and defend their approach by identifying underlying assumptions and limitations.

grade_1.focus: Using your body and voice to act out stories and feelings.

lessons.title: My Body Can Show Feelings
lessons.brief: Learning to use faces, arms, and movement to show happy, sad, angry, and surprised.

lessons.title: Making Animal Sounds and Movements
lessons.brief: Acting like different animals by copying their sounds and the way they move.

lessons.title: Acting Out Nursery Rhymes
lessons.brief: Using your whole body to tell stories from rhymes like 'Humpty Dumpty' and 'Jack and Jill'.

lessons.title: Being a Character in a Simple Play
lessons.brief: Playing a role like a farmer, a queen, or a cat in a short story acted out with your class.

grade_2.focus: Creating characters and acting them out in short stories with other students.

lessons.title: What Makes a Character Real
lessons.brief: Learning how a character looks, talks, and acts—giving each character their own special way of being.

lessons.title: Using Props and Costumes to Become Someone Else
lessons.brief: How a hat, a stick, or a scarf can help you look and feel like a different person.

lessons.title: Acting Together Without Words
lessons.brief: Telling a story with a group using only movement and facial expressions, no talking.

lessons.title: Performing a Fairy Tale Scene
lessons.brief: Working with other students to act out a short part of a story like Cinderella or The Three Bears.

grade_3.focus: Understanding how characters think and feel, and how scenes build stories.

lessons.title: Why a Character Does What They Do
lessons.brief: Learning that characters have reasons and feelings that explain their actions in a story.

lessons.title: How Scenes Connect to Tell a Whole Story
lessons.brief: Seeing how one scene leads to the next and how the story moves from beginning to middle to end.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Giving Characters Their Own Words
lessons.brief: Creating conversations between characters that sound real and show what each character is thinking.

lessons.title: Improvisation: Making Up a Scene on the Spot
lessons.brief: Inventing actions, words, and reactions without a script when given a simple situation or character.

grade_4.focus: Building scenes with structure, tension, and character development.

lessons.title: The Basic Plot Structure in Drama
lessons.brief: How scenes are organized with a setup, a problem, and a resolution that audiences can follow.

lessons.title: Blocking: Planning Where Actors Move and Stand
lessons.brief: Learning how to position actors on stage so the audience can see what's happening and feel the story's meaning.

lessons.title: Building Tension: What Makes a Scene Exciting
lessons.brief: Using timing, conflict between characters, and surprise moments to keep the audience interested.

lessons.title: Creating a Multi-Scene Play from a Story
lessons.brief: Taking a longer story and breaking it into separate scenes with different characters and settings to perform.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how drama techniques create meaning and how different genres approach storytelling.

lessons.title: How Lighting, Sound, and Scenery Shape What We Feel
lessons.brief: Exploring how technical elements (not just acting) influence the mood and the audience's understanding of a scene.

lessons.title: Comedy and Tragedy: Different Ways to Tell a Story
lessons.brief: Comparing how comedies and tragedies use character, conflict, and endings to create different emotional responses.

lessons.title: Character Development: How a Person Changes Across a Play
lessons.brief: Tracking how a character's thoughts, feelings, and actions evolve through the course of a story.

lessons.title: Subtext: What Characters Really Mean When They Speak
lessons.brief: Understanding that characters sometimes say one thing but mean or feel another, and how actors show this.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing dramatic structure, cultural contexts, and using drama to explore social themes.

lessons.title: Comparing Dramatic Genres: Genre Conventions and How They Change Meaning
lessons.brief: Examining how genres like melodrama, farce, or realism use different rules and techniques to convey distinct messages.

lessons.title: Staging Decisions: How Directors Interpret a Script Differently
lessons.brief: Exploring how different directors make choices about blocking, tone, and design to create unique meanings from the same play.

lessons.title: Drama Across Cultures: Different Theatrical Traditions
lessons.brief: Studying how theatre traditions from different cultures (puppet theatre, musical theatre, storytelling) reflect their values and histories.

lessons.title: Using Drama to Explore Real Issues
lessons.brief: Creating and analyzing scenes that examine social themes like friendship, fairness, identity, or conflict in ways that help audiences think deeply.

grade_7.focus: Drama as a tool for exploring character, emotion, and storytelling through performance and improvisation.

lessons.title: Building a Character from the Ground Up
lessons.brief: Students create believable characters by developing backstory, motivation, and physical choices that reveal personality.

lessons.title: Emotion, Action, and Reaction on Stage
lessons.brief: Students learn how to physicalize emotions authentically and respond truthfully to other performers in scene work.

lessons.title: Improvisation as Problem-Solving
lessons.brief: Students use structured improv games to develop quick thinking, listening skills, and spontaneous storytelling.

lessons.title: Narrative Structure in Monologues and Scenes
lessons.brief: Students analyze how stories are told through drama and perform monologues that reveal character arc and conflict.

grade_8.focus: Drama as a mirror to social issues: how theatre reflects real-world problems and allows audiences to examine multiple perspectives.

lessons.title: Staging Social Conflict: Whose Story Gets Told?
lessons.brief: Students examine how dramatic choices reveal bias, power dynamics, and whose voices are centered or marginalized in stories.

lessons.title: Adapting Real Events into Theatre
lessons.brief: Students transform historical or contemporary events into dramatic scenes, making decisions about which details matter and how to represent truth.

lessons.title: The Antagonist's Argument: Playing the Other Side
lessons.brief: Students perform and defend characters with opposing viewpoints, learning to argue convincingly for positions they may not personally hold.

lessons.title: Audience, Context, and Moral Judgment
lessons.brief: Students explore how the same scene affects different audiences differently, and how setting and timing change what a story means.

grade_9.focus: Theatre as a system of signs: how playwrights, directors, and performers communicate meaning through language, movement, design, and convention.

lessons.title: Decoding Dramatic Language: Subtext and What Characters Don't Say
lessons.brief: Students analyze scenes to identify what lies beneath dialogue—desire, fear, deception—and perform with awareness of subtext.

lessons.title: Theatrical Convention: How Rules Create Meaning
lessons.brief: Students study how different theatre traditions (realism, expressionism, absurdism, etc.) use distinct conventions to communicate ideas and emotions.

lessons.title: Mise-en-Scène: The Language of Visual Storytelling
lessons.brief: Students learn how directors use space, lighting, colour, and object placement to reinforce or complicate a play's themes.

lessons.title: Text Analysis: Finding the Play's Central Question
lessons.brief: Students read full dramatic texts and identify the moral, philosophical, or emotional core that drives the action and shapes performance choices.

grade_10.focus: Dramatic interpretation as cultural and historical act: understanding how playwrights construct meaning within—and against—the norms of their time.

lessons.title: Close Reading Drama: How Playwrights Build Theme Through Structure
lessons.brief: Students analyze how a playwright's choices in plot, pacing, repetition, and language reinforce or question the play's central ideas.

lessons.title: Theatre in Context: History, Society, and the Stage
lessons.brief: Students examine how specific plays emerged from and spoke to their historical moment, and how revivals reinterpret plays for new audiences.

lessons.title: Directing a Scene: Translating Text into Embodied Action
lessons.brief: Students make concrete directorial choices—blocking, tempo, tone—and defend them with evidence from the script and an understanding of the play's meaning.

lessons.title: Representation and Erasure in Classic Texts
lessons.brief: Students critically examine whose stories appear in canonical drama, whose perspectives are absent, and how modern productions reckon with historical bias.

grade_11.focus: Comparative dramatic analysis: evaluating how different playwrights, traditions, and historical periods approach similar human questions through form and content.

lessons.title: Competing Visions: How Different Playwrights Answer the Same Dramatic Question
lessons.brief: Students compare how multiple writers tackle shared themes (guilt, ambition, belonging, justice) and evaluate the philosophical and aesthetic implications of their choices.

lessons.title: Form as Argument: Why a Playwright Chooses Tragedy, Comedy, or Experimental Structure
lessons.brief: Students analyze how genre and formal innovation serve thematic purpose, and argue whether form and content can contradict productively.

lessons.title: Power, Language, and Silence: Feminist and Postcolonial Readings of Drama
lessons.brief: Students apply critical frameworks to examine how plays construct gender, race, nation, and power, and how counter-readings challenge dominant interpretations.

lessons.title: Adaptation and Fidelity: What Is Lost and Gained When Plays Are Remade
lessons.brief: Students compare source texts with stage, film, or cross-cultural adaptations, arguing what is essential to preserve and what benefits from radical change.

grade_12.focus: Drama as a research practice: investigating how theatre generates knowledge about human experience, ethics, and society through performance and critical analysis.

lessons.title: Research Question as Performance: Designing a Devised Theatre Project
lessons.brief: Students develop original research questions, gather evidence from interviews, archives, or lived experience, and shape it into a coherent theatrical argument.

lessons.title: Philosophies of Theatre: What Does Drama Do That Other Art Forms Cannot?
lessons.brief: Students engage with theorists (Stanislavski, Brecht, Artaud, Butler, Boal) to construct a personal framework for understanding theatre's ethical and epistemological possibilities.

lessons.title: Global Dramaturgy: Reading Drama Across Cultures, Languages, and Traditions
lessons.brief: Students analyze dramatic texts from non-Western traditions on their own terms, investigating how cultural context shapes form, and what is lost and gained in translation.

lessons.title: Theatre as Witness: How Drama Engages with Trauma, History, and Social Change
lessons.brief: Students study documentary theatre, verbatim performance, and activist drama, investigating the ethics and efficacy of using theatre to represent difficult truths.

grade_1.focus: Learning that people trade things they have for things they need, and that work helps us get what we want.

lessons.title: Jobs People Do
lessons.brief: Children explore real jobs in their community (teacher, baker, mail carrier) and what each person makes or does.

lessons.title: Needs and Wants
lessons.brief: Students learn the difference between things we must have (food, shelter) and things we wish for (toys, candy).

lessons.title: Trading and Sharing
lessons.brief: Children act out simple trades: swapping toys, sharing snacks, and discovering why people exchange things.

lessons.title: Money Is a Tool
lessons.brief: Students see that money is used to buy things instead of trading, and handle real coins and notes.

grade_2.focus: Understanding that goods come from workers and nature, money is used in stores, and families make choices about spending.

lessons.title: Where Things Come From
lessons.brief: Students trace a simple product (bread, toy, shirt) from raw materials through workers to the store shelf.

lessons.title: Buying at the Store
lessons.brief: Children learn how stores work: shelves, prices, paying with money, and getting change.

lessons.title: Family Money Choices
lessons.brief: Students discover that families decide what to buy with their money and sometimes have to choose one thing over another.

lessons.title: Saving and Spending
lessons.brief: Children explore why people keep some money instead of spending it all, and what happens when you save.

grade_3.focus: Learning how producers make goods, how supply and demand work in simple markets, and how communities depend on different jobs.

lessons.title: Producers and Consumers
lessons.brief: Students categorise people as those who make/grow things and those who buy and use them, and see how both are needed.

lessons.title: Why Prices Change
lessons.brief: Children explore simple cause-and-effect: when many people want something, the price goes up; when few want it, the price goes down.

lessons.title: Jobs in Our Town
lessons.brief: Students map out different occupations and explain how each job provides a service or product the community needs.

lessons.title: Making and Selling
lessons.brief: Children learn the basic steps: making a product, deciding a price, and trying to sell it to customers.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how systems of production, trade, and resources work together to create goods, and how choices affect communities.

lessons.title: Resources and Production
lessons.brief: Students identify natural resources, capital (tools and factories), and labour, and explain how they combine to make products.

lessons.title: Supply Chains
lessons.brief: Children map out the pathway from raw material to final customer, identifying each step and the workers involved.

lessons.title: Trade Between Communities
lessons.brief: Students learn why places trade with each other: some areas have different resources or make things better, and exchange benefits both sides.

lessons.title: Scarcity and Choice
lessons.brief: Children explore that resources are limited, so people and governments must make decisions about what to produce and who gets what.

grade_5.focus: Examining how economies organise production and distribution, how markets respond to human behaviour, and how global trade shapes what we buy.

lessons.title: Economic Systems: How Societies Organise
lessons.brief: Students compare different ways economies work: who decides what to make, who owns factories, and how goods are shared.

lessons.title: Markets and Competition
lessons.brief: Children investigate how businesses compete on price and quality, how consumers choose, and what happens when markets have few or many sellers.

lessons.title: Money, Banks, and Borrowing
lessons.brief: Students learn how banks hold money, lend it out with interest, and why people and businesses borrow to invest in growth.

lessons.title: Global Trade and Transport
lessons.brief: Children trace how goods travel across borders, why countries specialise in what they're best at, and how this affects prices and choice.
