grade_6.focus: Analysing how economic decisions interconnect across markets, nations, and time; understanding inequality and sustainability in economic systems.

lessons.title: Consumer Behaviour and Market Power
lessons.brief: Students examine how advertising, trends, and consumer choices drive production decisions, and how large companies shape what people buy.

lessons.title: Wages, Work, and Inequality
lessons.brief: Children investigate why some jobs pay more than others, how education affects earning potential, and why wealth and income are distributed unevenly.

lessons.title: Costs of Production and Hidden Impact
lessons.brief: Students analyse how environmental damage, labour conditions, and resource depletion are often not included in prices but affect communities and the planet.

lessons.title: Economic Growth and Sustainability
lessons.brief: Children explore the tension between producing more goods (growth) and protecting natural resources and ecosystems for the future.

grade_7.focus: How people make choices about scarce resources and what that reveals about how economies work.

lessons.title: Why We Can't Have Everything: The Problem of Scarcity
lessons.brief: Explore why scarcity exists, how it affects individuals and societies, and how different people prioritize their choices.

lessons.title: From Barter to Money: How Trade Evolved
lessons.brief: Trace the history of exchange systems from direct barter to modern currency and understand why money solves real problems.

lessons.title: Jobs, Wages, and Your Local Economy
lessons.brief: Examine how people earn income, what determines wages, and how money flows through neighborhoods and communities.

lessons.title: Needs vs. Wants: Marketing and Consumer Choices
lessons.brief: Analyze how advertising influences spending decisions and practice distinguishing between genuine needs and manufactured desires.

grade_8.focus: How markets work as systems where supply and demand create prices, and why different countries organize economies differently.

lessons.title: Supply and Demand: Why Prices Rise and Fall
lessons.brief: Investigate how the availability of goods and consumer desire interact to set prices, using real examples from current events.

lessons.title: Profit, Competition, and Business Strategy
lessons.brief: Examine why businesses aim for profit, how competition drives innovation, and what happens when one company dominates a market.

lessons.title: Command Economies vs. Market Economies: Two Different Systems
lessons.brief: Compare how centrally planned and market-based economies make decisions about production and distribution, with historical examples.

lessons.title: Taxes and Government Spending: Who Pays and Why
lessons.brief: Explore how governments collect revenue through taxes and decide how to allocate it to public goods and services.

grade_9.focus: How different economic systems balance efficiency, fairness, and growth, and how global trade connects economies across borders.

lessons.title: Measuring Economic Health: GDP, Inflation, and Unemployment
lessons.brief: Learn how economists measure whether an economy is growing or shrinking and what those metrics actually tell us about people's lives.

lessons.title: Globalization and Comparative Advantage: Why Countries Trade
lessons.brief: Understand the economic logic behind international trade, specialization, and why some nations benefit more than others from globalization.

lessons.title: The Role of Banks and Money Supply in Economic Stability
lessons.brief: Investigate how central banks manage money, control inflation, and influence whether economies expand or contract.

lessons.title: Market Failures: When Competition Alone Isn't Enough
lessons.brief: Analyze situations where markets produce inefficient outcomes—monopolies, pollution, information gaps—and examine potential solutions.

grade_10.focus: How institutions shape economic outcomes and how historical events demonstrate the consequences of economic choices.

lessons.title: Property Rights, Contracts, and Rule of Law in Economic Growth
lessons.brief: Examine how legal institutions enable economic activity and why economies fail when property rights and contracts are weak or corrupt.

lessons.title: The Great Depression and the 2008 Financial Crisis: Causes and Policy Responses
lessons.brief: Analyze primary sources and competing explanations for major economic collapses and evaluate the effectiveness of different government interventions.

lessons.title: Labor Markets, Unions, and the Distribution of Income
lessons.brief: Investigate what determines wages, how labor power differs from other commodities, and tensions between worker power and employer control.

lessons.title: Development Economics: Why Some Countries Remain Poor
lessons.brief: Examine structural barriers to economic development—geography, institutions, colonialism, debt—and evaluate solutions proposed by different economists.

grade_11.focus: How competing economic philosophies explain the world differently and how to evaluate their strengths and weaknesses.

lessons.title: Classical, Keynesian, and Modern Schools: Competing Theories of How Economies Work
lessons.brief: Compare foundational frameworks for understanding economic behavior and identify the assumptions and evidence each school prioritizes.

lessons.title: Critique of Market Efficiency: Behavioral Economics and Inequality
lessons.brief: Challenge the rational actor model using research on human bias and examine how markets persistently generate unequal outcomes.

lessons.title: Monetary Policy vs. Fiscal Policy: The Debate Over How to Manage Recessions
lessons.brief: Evaluate competing arguments about which tools—interest rates or government spending—more effectively stabilize economies.

lessons.title: Globalization and Inequality: Winners and Losers in the Modern Economy
lessons.brief: Synthesize evidence on how global trade affects wages, employment, and wealth distribution within and between nations.

grade_12.focus: How to conduct independent economic analysis using multiple frameworks and engage with unsolved problems at the frontier of economic thinking.

lessons.title: Reading and Interpreting Economic Research: Methods, Biases, and Limitations
lessons.brief: Learn to evaluate empirical studies, identify causal claims versus correlations, and recognize how funding and methodology influence conclusions.

lessons.title: Sustainability and the Economics of Climate Change: Valuing the Future
lessons.brief: Analyze how standard economics treats environmental costs, explore the debate over carbon pricing and growth, and engage with critiques from ecological economics.

lessons.title: The Future of Work: Automation, Inequality, and Policy Alternatives
lessons.brief: Investigate competing predictions about technological displacement, evaluate proposals from universal basic income to wage floors, and construct your own argument.

lessons.title: Independent Research Project: Designing and Testing an Economic Question
lessons.brief: Conduct original analysis on a topic of your choice using data, evidence, and multiple theoretical lenses to develop and defend your conclusions.

grade_1.focus: Learning to name and recognise the four basic feelings in your body and face.

lessons.title: Happy, Sad, Angry, Scared: What Do They Feel Like?
lessons.brief: Students identify the four basic emotions and where they feel them in their body.

lessons.title: Faces Tell Stories
lessons.brief: Students learn to read facial expressions and match them to the four feelings.

lessons.title: My Feelings Change
lessons.brief: Students discover that feelings come and go throughout the day, and that's normal.

grade_2.focus: Describing what triggers feelings and how they show up in behaviour.

lessons.title: What Makes Me Feel This Way?
lessons.brief: Students explore simple cause-and-effect: what happens, then how they feel.

lessons.title: How My Body Shows What I Feel
lessons.brief: Students describe physical signs of emotions: tears, clenched fists, tight chest, smiles.

lessons.title: When Others Feel Different Things
lessons.brief: Students recognise that the same event can make different people feel different ways.

lessons.title: What I Do When I Feel Big Feelings
lessons.brief: Students name simple actions they take when happy, sad, angry, or scared.

grade_3.focus: Categorising emotions, understanding intensity levels, and recognising patterns in feelings.

lessons.title: Feelings Come in Different Sizes
lessons.brief: Students learn that emotions exist on a scale—from tiny to huge—and use vocabulary like frustrated, upset, furious.

lessons.title: Feelings Have Families
lessons.brief: Students group similar emotions together and see how sadness, disappointment, and loneliness are connected.

lessons.title: The Story Before My Feeling
lessons.brief: Students trace simple sequences: what happened, what I thought, what I felt, what I did.

lessons.title: My Feeling Patterns
lessons.brief: Students notice which situations, people, or times of day tend to trigger the same feelings.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how thoughts, feelings, and actions form a connected system and how to influence it.

lessons.title: The Three-Part System: Thought, Feeling, Action
lessons.brief: Students map out how what they think influences what they feel, which then shapes what they do.

lessons.title: When My Thoughts Get Stuck
lessons.brief: Students identify unhelpful thought patterns (catastrophising, all-or-nothing thinking) and how they intensify feelings.

lessons.title: Strategies That Actually Work
lessons.brief: Students learn and practise concrete techniques to calm their nervous system: breathing, movement, talking it through.

lessons.title: Reading the Room: What Others Are Feeling
lessons.brief: Students develop empathy by noticing tone of voice, body language, and context to understand what others might feel.

grade_5.focus: Exploring the purpose and wisdom of all emotions, and developing agency in emotional responses.

lessons.title: Why Emotions Exist: The Message Behind the Feeling
lessons.brief: Students learn that every emotion—even anger and fear—carries useful information about what we need or value.

lessons.title: The Emotion Cycle: From Trigger to Recovery
lessons.brief: Students trace the full arc of an emotional experience and understand why feelings naturally rise, peak, and fade.

lessons.title: What I Can Control and What I Can't
lessons.brief: Students distinguish between triggers they can't choose and responses they can influence through awareness and practice.

lessons.title: Emotions Across Cultures and People
lessons.brief: Students explore how different families, cultures, and individuals express and value emotions differently.

grade_6.focus: Integrating emotional awareness into decision-making, relationships, and identity; connecting emotion to ethics and purpose.

lessons.title: How Emotions Shape My Choices
lessons.brief: Students analyse how unexamined feelings can drive impulsive decisions, and how emotional awareness improves judgment.

lessons.title: Managing Conflict: When My Emotions Meet Someone Else's
lessons.brief: Students learn to hold their own feelings while staying curious about another person's perspective and needs.

lessons.title: Vulnerability, Shame, and Belonging
lessons.brief: Students explore the difference between shame and healthy discomfort, and how courage involves emotional risk.

lessons.title: Emotion, Values, and Who I'm Becoming
lessons.brief: Students connect their emotional responses to their core values and reflect on how they want to respond emotionally as they grow.

grade_7.focus: Recognizing and naming your own emotions, and understanding how they show up in your body and choices.

lessons.title: The Emotion Map: Where Feelings Live in Your Body
lessons.brief: Students learn to identify physical sensations that accompany different emotions and create a personal 'map' of how their body signals emotion.

lessons.title: Emotion vs. Reaction: Why You Act the Way You Do
lessons.brief: Students explore the gap between feeling an emotion and choosing a response, using real teen scenarios to practice pausing before reacting.

lessons.title: Naming the Mess: Beyond 'Fine' and 'Mad'
lessons.brief: Students expand their emotional vocabulary by learning to distinguish between similar emotions (frustrated vs. overwhelmed, embarrassed vs. ashamed) and why precision matters.

lessons.title: Emotion Triggers: What Sets You Off and Why
lessons.brief: Students identify personal triggers—situations, people, or events that spark strong emotions—and begin to notice patterns in what affects them.

grade_8.focus: Understanding how emotions influence social relationships and learning to read emotions in others.

lessons.title: The Ripple Effect: How Your Mood Shapes the Room
lessons.brief: Students examine how their emotional state affects peer dynamics, using video and role-play to see how one person's mood influences a group.

lessons.title: Reading the Unspoken: Decoding Body Language and Tone
lessons.brief: Students practice interpreting facial expressions, posture, and voice tone to understand what others are feeling, even when they don't say it aloud.

lessons.title: Empathy in Action: Feeling With, Not For
lessons.brief: Students learn the difference between sympathy and empathy, and practice genuinely understanding another person's emotional experience without trying to fix it.

lessons.title: Conflict as Information: What Arguments Reveal About What Matters
lessons.brief: Students analyze real conflicts (historical and personal) to uncover the underlying emotions and values driving disagreement.

grade_9.focus: Examining how emotions drive values and decisions, and building awareness of emotional patterns in yourself and culture.

lessons.title: Emotions and Identity: Why You Care What You Care About
lessons.brief: Students explore how emotional responses shape their values, interests, and beliefs, and begin to notice which emotions are uniquely theirs versus culturally influenced.

lessons.title: The Stories We Tell: How Emotion Shapes Memory and Meaning
lessons.brief: Students analyze how emotions color memory and narrative—why we remember some events vividly and forget others, and how emotion rewrites the story we tell about ourselves.

lessons.title: Emotional Contagion: Why Feelings Spread (and How to Think for Yourself)
lessons.brief: Students examine how emotions spread through groups, media, and online spaces, and develop strategies to feel their own emotions while resisting blind emotional contagion.

lessons.title: Managing Intensity: When Emotions Become Overwhelming
lessons.brief: Students learn to recognize emotional dysregulation and practice evidence-based grounding and regulation techniques tailored to their personal response style.

grade_10.focus: Analyzing emotional reasoning, distinguishing feeling from fact, and understanding emotions in ethical and civic contexts.

lessons.title: Feeling Certain vs. Being Right: The Limits of Emotional Logic
lessons.brief: Students examine when emotional conviction misleads us, using case studies (politics, relationships, justice) to critique arguments built on feeling alone.

lessons.title: Moral Emotions: Shame, Guilt, Anger, and Justice
lessons.brief: Students analyze how emotions like guilt and moral outrage drive ethical behavior and social change, while examining how shame can paralyze or corrupt action.

lessons.title: Emotional Privilege and Bias: Whose Feelings Get Heard?
lessons.brief: Students explore how power dynamics affect whose emotions are validated or dismissed in relationships and institutions, connecting to identity and social equity.

lessons.title: Emotional Reasoning in Media and Persuasion
lessons.brief: Students deconstruct how advertising, news, and social media use emotional triggers to persuade, and analyze their own susceptibility to emotional manipulation.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing emotional frameworks, synthesizing psychology and philosophy, and developing a personal theory of emotional authenticity and growth.

lessons.title: Competing Emotional Philosophies: Stoicism vs. Romanticism vs. Acceptance
lessons.brief: Students read and compare historical and philosophical approaches to emotion (Epictetus, Rousseau, modern ACT), evaluating which frameworks serve which goals.

lessons.title: Emotional Authenticity Under Construction: Culture, Context, and Performance
lessons.brief: Students investigate whether authentic emotion exists, examining how culture, gender, and social role shape emotional expression and questioning the myth of the 'true self.'

lessons.title: The Neuroscience-Ethics Intersection: Emotion, Responsibility, and Blame
lessons.brief: Students synthesize neuroscience on emotional processing with ethical and legal frameworks, grappling with questions of culpability and choice.

lessons.title: Building Your Emotional Framework: Testing Values Against Reality
lessons.brief: Students articulate their own developing theory of healthy emotion—what role emotion should play in decision-making, relationships, and meaning—and stress-test it against real dilemmas.

grade_12.focus: Conducting research-informed analysis of emotion across contexts, and developing evidence-based positions on emotional wellbeing, society, and the self.

lessons.title: Emotion Research Methods: Interpreting Studies on Feelings, Decisions, and Behavior
lessons.brief: Students learn to read and critique empirical research on emotion (psychology, neuroscience), identifying limitations, cultural assumptions, and what findings actually support.

lessons.title: The Emotion Industry: Profit, Wellness, and Manufactured Needs
lessons.brief: Students analyze how emotion is commodified in therapy culture, social media, self-help, and marketing—examining claims critically and evaluating evidence for interventions.

lessons.title: Comparative Emotional Cultures: How Different Societies Shape What You Feel
lessons.brief: Students investigate cross-cultural research on emotion, interrogating whether feelings are universal or culturally constructed, and what assumptions underlie Western emotional frameworks.

lessons.title: Designing Your Emotional Life: Integration Across Theory, Research, and Experience
lessons.brief: Students synthesize readings, research, neuroscience, philosophy, and personal reflection to construct a evidence-informed personal stance on emotion, wellbeing, and their role in a good life.

grade_1.focus: Learning that engineers are people who build and fix things using their hands and simple tools.

lessons.title: What Do Engineers Do?
lessons.brief: Meeting different engineers and seeing the real things they build and fix.

lessons.title: Tools in My Hand
lessons.brief: Learning to safely use simple tools like hammers, screwdrivers, and wrenches.

lessons.title: Building With Blocks and Sticks
lessons.brief: Stacking and joining materials to make simple structures that stand up.

lessons.title: Things That Roll and Slide
lessons.brief: Exploring how objects move on wheels, ramps, and smooth surfaces.

grade_2.focus: Understanding that machines have parts that work together to do a job.

lessons.title: Parts of a Machine
lessons.brief: Taking apart simple objects to see the different pieces and what each one does.

lessons.title: Wheels, Axles, and Movement
lessons.brief: Learning how wheels spin on axles to make things move.

lessons.title: Pushing and Pulling: Making Things Work
lessons.brief: Discovering how force moves objects and how levers help us push or pull with less effort.

lessons.title: Building a Rolling Machine
lessons.brief: Designing and creating a simple cart or toy that moves using wheels.

grade_3.focus: Recognizing that engineers solve problems by understanding cause and effect and choosing the right materials.

lessons.title: Cause and Effect in Simple Machines
lessons.brief: Exploring how pushing a lever, turning a wheel, or pulling a string makes something happen.

lessons.title: Materials Have Properties
lessons.brief: Testing different materials to see which ones are hard, soft, stretchy, or waterproof.

lessons.title: Bridges: Why Do They Stand Up?
lessons.brief: Comparing different bridge shapes and testing which ones hold weight without breaking.

lessons.title: Pulleys and Ramps: Doing Work Easier
lessons.brief: Learning how pulleys lift heavy things and how ramps help move objects up and down.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how systems work: the way all the parts fit together and depend on each other to solve a problem.

lessons.title: Systems and Subsystems
lessons.brief: Examining a bicycle or toy car as a system made of smaller parts that all work together.

lessons.title: Energy and Motion in Machines
lessons.brief: Investigating how energy moves through simple machines and turns into work and movement.

lessons.title: Structures That Hold Load
lessons.brief: Designing and testing towers, beams, and frames to understand how structures resist bending and breaking.

lessons.title: Gears, Chains, and Power Transfer
lessons.brief: Learning how gears change speed and direction, and how chains carry power from one place to another.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how engineers use the design process to improve systems by testing, measuring, and making changes based on evidence.

lessons.title: The Engineering Design Process
lessons.brief: Following the steps engineers use: identify a problem, brainstorm solutions, build, test, and improve.

lessons.title: Measuring and Comparing Performance
lessons.brief: Using data to test which design works best, fastest, or most efficiently.

lessons.title: Mechanical Advantage and Efficiency
lessons.brief: Calculating how machines make work easier and exploring why some designs waste less energy than others.

lessons.title: Building a Device to Solve a Real Problem
lessons.brief: Designing and refining a machine or structure that solves an actual classroom or community challenge.

grade_6.focus: Evaluating how engineering decisions affect systems, environments, and people, and how different fields of engineering connect and overlap.

lessons.title: Trade-offs and Constraints in Design
lessons.brief: Analyzing how engineers balance competing needs like cost, strength, weight, and environmental impact when making decisions.

lessons.title: How Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical Engineering Connect
lessons.brief: Examining real structures and machines to see how different engineering disciplines work together in one system.

lessons.title: Engineering and the Environment
lessons.brief: Investigating how engineering choices affect ecosystems and exploring sustainable design solutions.

lessons.title: Reverse Engineering: Learning From Existing Designs
lessons.brief: Taking apart a manufactured product to understand the engineering decisions made and proposing improvements based on data.

grade_7.focus: Engineering as problem-solving: how engineers identify real problems and design solutions using a structured process.

lessons.title: What Do Engineers Actually Do?
lessons.brief: Explore different engineering fields (civil, mechanical, electrical, software) through real projects that solved actual human problems.

lessons.title: The Design Process in Action
lessons.brief: Learn the engineering design cycle (define, ideate, prototype, test, refine) by designing and building a simple solution to a classroom challenge.

lessons.title: Constraints, Trade-offs, and Why Engineers Can't Have Everything
lessons.brief: Understand how budget, time, materials, and safety limits force engineers to make choices and why those limits actually make better designs.

lessons.title: Reading and Creating Technical Drawings
lessons.brief: Develop skills in sketching, labeling, and interpreting engineering diagrams so designs can be clearly communicated to others.

grade_8.focus: How everyday engineered systems work: examining the technology around us to understand the principles and trade-offs behind common devices.

lessons.title: The Physics Inside Machines: Force, Motion, and Energy Transfer
lessons.brief: Analyze how levers, pulleys, gears, and inclined planes convert effort into useful work, and apply these principles to real devices.

lessons.title: Why Bridges Don't Fall Down: Materials, Loads, and Structural Design
lessons.brief: Investigate how different bridge types (beam, arch, suspension, cable-stayed) distribute weight, and why material choice matters.

lessons.title: Water Systems and the Engineering Behind Getting Water to Your Home
lessons.brief: Trace water from source through treatment, pumping, and distribution networks to understand the infrastructure that serves cities.

lessons.title: Failure Analysis: Learning from Engineering Disasters
lessons.brief: Examine historical engineering failures (Tacoma Narrows Bridge, Challenger disaster, building collapses) to understand why they happened and how we prevent them.

grade_9.focus: Systems thinking in engineering: how interconnected components work together, and how changing one part affects the whole system.

lessons.title: Feedback Loops and Control Systems
lessons.brief: Understand how engineers use sensors, feedback, and automatic control to regulate systems like thermostats, cruise control, and water treatment plants.

lessons.title: Energy Efficiency and Power Generation
lessons.brief: Compare fossil fuel, nuclear, and renewable energy systems by analyzing their efficiency, environmental cost, and engineering feasibility.

lessons.title: Networks and Infrastructure Interdependence
lessons.brief: Map how electrical grids, transportation networks, and communication systems depend on each other and why system failures can cascade.

lessons.title: Engineering Design for the Real World: Cost, Sustainability, and Ethics
lessons.brief: Evaluate how engineers balance performance, cost, environmental impact, and social responsibility when designing products and systems.

grade_10.focus: Quantitative engineering: using mathematics and measurement to model systems, predict behavior, and validate designs.

lessons.title: Structural Analysis and Calculations
lessons.brief: Apply force equations and stress-strain relationships to calculate load capacity, safety factors, and material requirements in structural design.

lessons.title: Fluid Dynamics and Flow Systems
lessons.brief: Model fluid behavior in pipes, channels, and machines using principles of pressure, velocity, and conservation of mass.

lessons.title: Electrical Circuit Analysis and Power Distribution
lessons.brief: Use Ohm's law and circuit analysis to understand current flow, voltage drops, and power consumption in residential and industrial systems.

lessons.title: Thermal Engineering: Heat Transfer and Temperature Control
lessons.brief: Quantify conduction, convection, and radiation to analyze heating/cooling systems, insulation requirements, and thermal efficiency.

grade_11.focus: Advanced problem-solving and optimization: comparing engineering solutions, making evidence-based decisions, and understanding the limitations of models.

lessons.title: Competing Engineering Solutions: Trade-off Analysis and Decision-Making
lessons.brief: Evaluate multiple design approaches for a single problem using weighted criteria, cost-benefit analysis, and lifecycle assessment.

lessons.title: Modeling and Simulation: Predicting Real-World Behavior
lessons.brief: Explore how engineers use computational models to predict system behavior, and critically examine the assumptions and limitations built into models.

lessons.title: Scaling Up: From Prototype to Production
lessons.brief: Analyze the challenges of manufacturing at scale, including quality control, repeatability, automation, and the differences between lab and factory conditions.

lessons.title: Engineering Innovation and Disruption
lessons.brief: Examine how new materials, technologies, and methods have disrupted industries, and identify patterns in what makes some innovations succeed while others fail.

grade_12.focus: Interdisciplinary engineering research: investigating emerging challenges, synthesizing knowledge across domains, and evaluating evidence in real engineering contexts.

lessons.title: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure: Engineering Solutions to Environmental Change
lessons.brief: Research how infrastructure is being redesigned for climate impacts (flooding, heat, drought), evaluate competing solutions, and assess implementation barriers.

lessons.title: Bioengineering and Engineering Biology: Designing Living Systems
lessons.brief: Explore how engineering principles apply to biological systems—synthetic biology, tissue engineering, and the ethical implications of engineering life.

lessons.title: Critical Analysis of Engineering Claims and Evidence
lessons.brief: Learn to read engineering literature, evaluate research methodology, identify bias and limitations, and construct evidence-based arguments about engineering feasibility.

lessons.title: Engineering Ethics in Complex Systems: Power, Justice, and Unintended Consequences
lessons.brief: Examine how engineering decisions affect different populations unequally, analyze historical cases of technological injustice, and develop frameworks for ethical engineering.

grade_1.focus: Discovering that people make and sell things, and that you can make simple things to share or trade.

lessons.title: What Do Grown-Ups Make and Sell?
lessons.brief: Learning about real jobs where people create things—bakers, builders, artists—and seeing what they make.

lessons.title: Making Something and Trading It
lessons.brief: Creating a simple craft or snack and trading it with a friend to learn what exchange feels like.

lessons.title: My First Lemonade Stand
lessons.brief: Setting up a tiny stand to sell lemonade or homemade items to family, learning money and customers.

grade_2.focus: Understanding that businesses need customers, and learning how to ask what people want before making something.

lessons.title: What Do Customers Really Want?
lessons.brief: Asking friends and family simple questions about what they like, need, or would buy.

lessons.title: Making a Product People Will Buy
lessons.brief: Designing and making a simple item—friendship bracelets, decorated pencils, cookies—based on what you learned customers want.

lessons.title: Telling People About Your Product
lessons.brief: Creating simple posters or telling people face-to-face about what you made and why they should try it.

lessons.title: Counting Money and Keeping Track
lessons.brief: Learning to add up coins and bills, and recording what you sold and earned.

grade_3.focus: Recognizing that successful products solve problems or meet needs, and comparing different ways to run a small business.

lessons.title: Problems People Have and How to Solve Them
lessons.brief: Spotting everyday problems—messy backpacks, lost socks, bored friends—and brainstorming product ideas that solve them.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Businesses Side by Side
lessons.brief: Looking at two real businesses (a bakery and a grocery store, or two lemonade stands) and seeing what they do differently.

lessons.title: Costs, Prices, and Making a Profit
lessons.brief: Understanding that businesses buy materials, spend money to make products, then charge more to customers so they earn profit.

lessons.title: Your Business Plan on One Page
lessons.brief: Writing down your idea, what you'll sell, who will buy it, and how much money you need to start.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how businesses operate as a system: inputs, processes, outputs, customers, and money flowing in and out.

lessons.title: The Business System: From Raw Materials to Customer
lessons.brief: Mapping out how a product moves from materials to making to selling, seeing each step as part of one connected flow.

lessons.title: Customers, Competition, and Market Position
lessons.brief: Identifying who your customers are, what competitors offer, and how your product is different or better.

lessons.title: The Money Cycle: Income, Expenses, and Profit
lessons.brief: Creating a simple budget showing money coming in from sales and money going out for materials, learning why profit matters.

lessons.title: Marketing: Why People Choose Your Product Over Another
lessons.brief: Designing advertisements, logos, or taglines that explain your product's unique value to potential buyers.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how businesses make decisions based on data, feedback, and changing conditions; learning to adapt and improve over time.

lessons.title: Using Customer Feedback to Improve Your Product
lessons.brief: Collecting what customers say about your product, identifying patterns, and deciding what to change.

lessons.title: Testing Ideas Before Investing Money
lessons.brief: Learning to run small experiments—surveys, prototypes, trial sales—to test if a business idea will work before spending big.

lessons.title: Scaling: Making More Without Breaking Your System
lessons.brief: Understanding how businesses grow bigger while keeping quality consistent, and what problems appear when they scale too fast.

lessons.title: Reading Financial Statements and Making Smart Decisions
lessons.brief: Learning to read a simple income statement and balance sheet, and using the numbers to decide whether to expand, cut costs, or pivot.

grade_6.focus: Examining entrepreneurship as a broader system involving supply chains, market forces, innovation, and social responsibility; connecting business to real-world impact.

lessons.title: Supply Chains and Where Products Really Come From
lessons.brief: Tracing a product from raw materials through suppliers, manufacturers, and distribution to understand invisible global networks.

lessons.title: Market Forces: Why Prices Go Up and Down
lessons.brief: Investigating how demand, supply, competition, and trends shape what businesses charge and which ones survive.

lessons.title: Business Models and How Companies Make Money Differently
lessons.brief: Comparing different ways to earn—selling products, subscriptions, advertising, licensing—and analyzing when each model works.

lessons.title: Entrepreneurship With Purpose: Business and Social Impact
lessons.brief: Exploring how entrepreneurs solve social or environmental problems while making money, and evaluating the trade-offs between profit and purpose.

grade_7.focus: Recognizing entrepreneurship in the real world and understanding why people start businesses.

lessons.title: What Makes Someone an Entrepreneur?
lessons.brief: Identify the traits, motivations, and stories of entrepreneurs across different industries and backgrounds.

lessons.title: From Problem to Business Idea
lessons.brief: Learn how entrepreneurs spot problems in their daily lives and turn them into business opportunities.

lessons.title: The Cost of Starting: Money, Time, and Risk
lessons.brief: Explore what resources entrepreneurs need and the personal risks they take when launching a venture.

lessons.title: Famous Fails: Learning from Entrepreneurial Mistakes
lessons.brief: Analyze real cases where businesses failed and what entrepreneurs learned from those experiences.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating business ideas critically and understanding how entrepreneurs test and refine their assumptions.

lessons.title: Is It a Good Idea or Just an Interesting One?
lessons.brief: Develop criteria to evaluate whether a business idea solves a real problem and has market potential.

lessons.title: Talking to Your Customer: The Art of Validation
lessons.brief: Practice methods entrepreneurs use to ask potential customers questions and validate assumptions before investing heavily.

lessons.title: Revenue Models: How Do Businesses Actually Make Money?
lessons.brief: Examine different ways businesses earn income (subscriptions, one-time sales, advertising, licensing) and when each works.

lessons.title: Competition Doesn't Mean Failure
lessons.brief: Analyze how entrepreneurs position themselves against competitors and find their unique advantage in crowded markets.

grade_9.focus: Building a foundational business framework by synthesizing market research, value creation, and resource planning.

lessons.title: Mapping the Ecosystem: Who Are Your Stakeholders?
lessons.brief: Identify and analyze all players in a business ecosystem—customers, suppliers, regulators, partners—and their competing interests.

lessons.title: The Value Proposition: Why Should Anyone Choose You?
lessons.brief: Craft and test a clear statement of what value a business delivers and to whom, and why that matters.

lessons.title: Building a Lean Business Model Canvas
lessons.brief: Apply a structured framework to organize key assumptions about customers, revenue, costs, and operations in one visual model.

lessons.title: Pitching Your Idea: Persuasion and Storytelling
lessons.brief: Learn how entrepreneurs communicate their vision to investors, customers, and team members through narrative and data.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting financial realities and understanding how entrepreneurial decisions connect to profit, growth, and sustainability.

lessons.title: Reading the Numbers: Profit, Cash Flow, and Burn Rate
lessons.brief: Analyze financial statements and learn why cash flow matters more than profit when a business is young.

lessons.title: Funding Your Dream: Bootstrapping vs. Investment vs. Debt
lessons.brief: Evaluate trade-offs between different funding sources and how each shapes control, risk, and growth expectations.

lessons.title: Pricing Strategy: Art and Science
lessons.brief: Examine how entrepreneurs set prices using cost analysis, competitor research, and psychological factors, with real case studies.

lessons.title: Scaling: When Growth Becomes the Problem
lessons.brief: Investigate how successful startups manage rapid growth, and why scaling too fast or too slow can destroy a business.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing entrepreneurial frameworks and developing independent analysis of how context, strategy, and execution shape outcomes.

lessons.title: Disruption vs. Incremental Innovation: Competing Narratives
lessons.brief: Compare the 'disruption theory' against critiques and examine when each lens actually explains real business outcomes.

lessons.title: Strategy Under Uncertainty: Pivot, Persevere, or Pivot?
lessons.brief: Analyze frameworks for making high-stakes decisions with incomplete information and critique their assumptions and limits.

lessons.title: The Role of Timing, Luck, and Founder Skill
lessons.brief: Deconstruct how much of entrepreneurial success comes from timing, randomness, skill, or narrative—and what evidence supports each claim.

lessons.title: Ethics, Power, and Unintended Consequences
lessons.brief: Examine how entrepreneurial ventures create winners and losers, externalities, and ethical tensions that aren't solved by profit.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent research into entrepreneurship across contexts and synthesizing evidence to build a personal argument about how ventures create value and change.

lessons.title: Comparative Entrepreneurship: Culture, Regulation, and Geography
lessons.brief: Research how entrepreneurship differs across countries and systems, and analyze how institutions shape who can start and what succeeds.

lessons.title: The Entrepreneur in Economic Theory: Schumpeter, Kirzner, and Beyond
lessons.brief: Engage with original economic thought on entrepreneurship and evaluate competing theories against historical and contemporary evidence.

lessons.title: Building Your Own Research Project: From Question to Findings
lessons.brief: Design and conduct original research into a specific entrepreneurial phenomenon, integrating interviews, financial analysis, or archival sources.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Evidence: What Creates Sustainable Enterprise?
lessons.brief: Draw conclusions from research and reading about what separates ventures that create lasting value from those that extract it or fail.

grade_1.focus: Learning to notice and name the living and non-living things in the world around us.

lessons.title: What Lives Outside?
lessons.brief: Students observe and name animals and plants they see in their neighbourhood.

lessons.title: Sun, Water, and Air
lessons.brief: Students explore three things all living things need and experience them with their senses.

lessons.title: Seasons Change What We See
lessons.brief: Students notice how weather and nature look different in each season.

grade_2.focus: Discovering how living things grow, change, and depend on their surroundings.

lessons.title: How Plants Grow from Seeds
lessons.brief: Students plant seeds, observe growth over time, and describe what plants need.

lessons.title: Animals and Their Homes
lessons.brief: Students identify different animal habitats and match animals to where they live.

lessons.title: Day and Night in Nature
lessons.brief: Students explore how daylight and darkness affect which animals are awake and what plants do.

lessons.title: Staying Warm and Cool
lessons.brief: Students observe how animals and plants respond to hot and cold weather.

grade_3.focus: Sorting living things into groups and tracking how they depend on each other and their environment.

lessons.title: Sorting Animals and Plants
lessons.brief: Students classify organisms by traits like size, where they live, and what they eat.

lessons.title: Food Chains: Who Eats What
lessons.brief: Students trace simple paths of energy from plants through animals to understand feeding relationships.

lessons.title: Habitats and Basic Needs
lessons.brief: Students investigate how different environments provide food, water, and shelter for their inhabitants.

lessons.title: How Humans Change the Land
lessons.brief: Students observe and describe ways people build on, remove, or alter natural spaces.

grade_4.focus: Understanding ecosystems as interconnected systems where organisms and their physical environment interact and influence each other.

lessons.title: Energy Flow Through Ecosystems
lessons.brief: Students map food webs to see how energy and nutrients move among multiple species and between living and non-living parts.

lessons.title: Adaptations: How Organisms Fit Their Environment
lessons.brief: Students examine specific traits that help plants and animals survive in their particular ecosystems.

lessons.title: Water Cycles and Living Systems
lessons.brief: Students trace water movement through atmosphere, land, and organisms, and explain how organisms depend on this cycle.

lessons.title: Biomes and Their Characteristics
lessons.brief: Students compare distinct biome types by their climate, plant and animal life, and physical features.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how ecosystems respond to change, how organisms reproduce and inherit traits, and what threatens or sustains biodiversity.

lessons.title: Inheritance and Variation in Populations
lessons.brief: Students investigate how traits pass from parents to offspring and how variation within a species relates to survival.

lessons.title: Ecosystem Balance and Disruption
lessons.brief: Students trace the consequences when a species is added, removed, or its population changes dramatically in an ecosystem.

lessons.title: Weathering, Soil, and Nutrient Cycles
lessons.brief: Students explain how rocks break down, soil forms, and nutrients cycle back through living systems.

lessons.title: Human Impact on Biodiversity
lessons.brief: Students examine how human activities affect species populations, habitats, and ecosystem health.

grade_6.focus: Integrating ecology, evolution, and Earth systems to understand how life adapts, populations change over time, and human decisions shape the biosphere.

lessons.title: Natural Selection and Evolution
lessons.brief: Students apply the concept of inheritance, variation, and differential survival to explain how populations adapt and species diverge.

lessons.title: Biogeochemical Cycles at Scale
lessons.brief: Students model carbon, nitrogen, and phosphorus cycles to understand how living systems and geology exchange elements globally.

lessons.title: Biodiversity, Stability, and Resilience
lessons.brief: Students analyse relationships between species diversity, ecosystem function, and capacity to recover from disturbance.

lessons.title: Sustainability and Environmental Decision-Making
lessons.brief: Students evaluate human choices in resource use, conservation, and pollution through the lens of long-term ecosystem and societal health.

grade_7.focus: How Earth's systems (atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, biosphere) interact to create the conditions that support life.

lessons.title: The Water Cycle and Weather Patterns
lessons.brief: Traces how water moves through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation to shape climate and weather.

lessons.title: Energy Flow from the Sun
lessons.brief: Explores how solar energy drives weather, ocean currents, and the greenhouse effect.

lessons.title: Biomes and Adaptation
lessons.brief: Examines how organisms are adapted to survive in different climate zones and ecosystems around the world.

lessons.title: Soil Formation and Nutrient Cycles
lessons.brief: Investigates how rock weathering, decomposition, and nutrient cycling sustain life in terrestrial ecosystems.

grade_8.focus: How human activities disrupt natural cycles and what evidence shows about the consequences for ecosystems and human societies.

lessons.title: Carbon Cycling and Climate Change
lessons.brief: Analyzes how fossil fuel burning alters atmospheric carbon and its measurable impacts on global temperatures.

lessons.title: Pollution and Ecosystem Collapse
lessons.brief: Examines how toxins in air, water, and soil accumulate in organisms and degrade biodiversity.

lessons.title: Resource Depletion: Forests, Fisheries, and Freshwater
lessons.brief: Investigates how overexploitation of natural resources threatens food security and water availability.

lessons.title: Evaluating Competing Claims About Environmental Problems
lessons.brief: Develops skills to assess scientific evidence, industry arguments, and policy proposals critically.

grade_9.focus: How ecosystems maintain stability through feedback loops and what happens when those loops are broken by human interference.

lessons.title: Population Dynamics and Carrying Capacity
lessons.brief: Models how predator-prey relationships, competition, and resource limits regulate population growth in nature and in human systems.

lessons.title: Tipping Points and Regime Shifts
lessons.brief: Explores how ecosystems can shift suddenly and irreversibly when critical thresholds are exceeded.

lessons.title: Invasive Species and Ecosystem Disruption
lessons.brief: Analyzes how non-native organisms disrupt established food webs and outcompete native species.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Local and Global Environmental Issues
lessons.brief: Connects local environmental observations to global patterns and identifies feedback loops operating at multiple scales.

grade_10.focus: How to interpret environmental data, evaluate competing scientific models, and recognize the assumptions and limitations of different approaches to environmental problems.

lessons.title: Reading and Critiquing Climate Data and Models
lessons.brief: Analyzes primary climate datasets, model outputs, and confidence intervals to evaluate the reliability of climate projections.

lessons.title: Life Cycle Assessment and Hidden Environmental Costs
lessons.brief: Applies quantitative analysis to measure the full environmental impact of products from extraction through disposal.

lessons.title: Comparing Environmental Management Strategies: Trade-offs and Evidence
lessons.brief: Evaluates case studies of different approaches (regulation, market mechanisms, conservation) using original sources and data.

lessons.title: Environmental Justice and Unequal Exposure to Risk
lessons.brief: Examines how environmental hazards, resource access, and decision-making power are distributed unequally across communities and nations.

grade_11.focus: How different environmental frameworks (economic, ecological, social) explain environmental problems differently and how to construct evidence-based arguments about environmental solutions.

lessons.title: Competing Theories of Environmental Value: Market vs. Intrinsic Worth
lessons.brief: Compares how neoclassical economics, ecological economics, and environmental ethics approach valuation and propose different solutions.

lessons.title: The Politics of Environmental Knowledge: Science, Industry, and Policy
lessons.brief: Critically examines how environmental science is conducted, funded, communicated, and translated into policy decisions.

lessons.title: Resilience, Adaptation, and Transformation in Human-Environment Systems
lessons.brief: Analyzes frameworks for building resilient systems and evaluates when incremental adaptation fails and transformative change is necessary.

lessons.title: Constructing and Defending Environmental Arguments with Evidence
lessons.brief: Develops capacity to build multi-layered arguments about environmental problems, drawing on multiple disciplines and acknowledging counterarguments.

grade_12.focus: How to conduct independent environmental research, synthesize knowledge across disciplines, and critically evaluate the feasibility and ethics of proposed environmental solutions at local and global scales.

lessons.title: Designing Environmental Research: Methods, Ethics, and Limitations
lessons.brief: Examines research methodologies in environmental science, including field studies, modeling, and social science approaches; considers bias, uncertainty, and ethical constraints.

lessons.title: Scaling Solutions: From Local Pilots to Global Policy
lessons.brief: Analyzes how environmental interventions are scaled up, identifying barriers to scaling, unintended consequences, and context-dependency of solutions.

lessons.title: Integrating Environmental Science with Economics, Society, and Governance
lessons.brief: Synthesizes insights from ecology, economics, political science, and ethics to evaluate real-world environmental proposals and policies.

lessons.title: Independent Environmental Investigation and Capstone Project
lessons.brief: Conducts original research or policy analysis on an environmental question of choice, integrating multiple forms of evidence and communicating findings to a real audience.

grade_1.focus: Movies are made of real people, places, and things we can see and hear.

lessons.title: What Is a Movie?
lessons.brief: Students watch short clips and learn that movies show moving pictures with sound, made by real people.

lessons.title: Cameras Catch What We See
lessons.brief: Students explore how cameras record pictures and video, comparing what the camera sees to what their own eyes see.

lessons.title: Sounds in Stories
lessons.brief: Students listen to movie sounds and music, noticing how sounds help tell the story and make them feel things.

lessons.title: People Who Make Movies
lessons.brief: Students meet the main movie jobs: actors (who pretend), directors (who lead), and camera operators (who film).

grade_2.focus: Movies are built from shots and scenes that show us a story in a special order.

lessons.title: Shots: Close-Up, Medium, and Far Away
lessons.brief: Students identify different camera distances and describe what we see in each—a face, a person, or a whole room.

lessons.title: Scenes Tell One Part of the Story
lessons.brief: Students watch complete scenes and notice that each one shows one event or moment before moving to the next.

lessons.title: Actors Show Feelings with Their Faces and Bodies
lessons.brief: Students observe how actors use expressions, gestures, and movement to show emotions and make us understand what they feel.

lessons.title: Before and After: The Order Matters
lessons.brief: Students compare movies where scenes are shown in different orders and see how the order changes what the story means.

grade_3.focus: Every choice in a movie—what we see, hear, and how it's arranged—affects how we feel and what we understand.

lessons.title: Camera Angles: Looking Up, Down, and Straight On
lessons.brief: Students learn that the camera angle changes how we feel about a character—looking up makes them seem powerful, looking down makes them seem small.

lessons.title: Light and Shadow Shape the Mood
lessons.brief: Students compare bright scenes to dark ones and discover that lighting changes whether we feel happy, scared, or mysterious.

lessons.title: Cuts and Edits: Joining Shots Together
lessons.brief: Students trace how editors choose which shots to show and in what order to build excitement or tell the story clearly.

lessons.title: Music and Sound Effects Create Feeling
lessons.brief: Students match different sounds and music to scenes and explain why certain sounds make us happy, sad, nervous, or thrilled.

grade_4.focus: A film is a system where camera, light, sound, and editing work together to create a complete artistic experience.

lessons.title: Composition: Arranging What's in the Frame
lessons.brief: Students analyze how filmmakers position actors, objects, and backgrounds within the frame to guide the viewer's eye and create balance.

lessons.title: Depth of Field: Focus and Blur as Tools
lessons.brief: Students examine how filmmakers choose what to focus on sharply and what to blur, controlling what the audience pays attention to.

lessons.title: Pacing: How Editing Speed Changes Emotion
lessons.brief: Students compare sequences cut slowly (building suspense) to sequences cut quickly (creating excitement) and measure how this affects tension.

lessons.title: Color Palette: How Color Choices Communicate Meaning
lessons.brief: Students observe deliberate color schemes in films—warm tones for comfort, cool tones for danger—and discuss what colors suggest about setting and mood.

grade_5.focus: Filmmakers use visual and audio language strategically to develop characters, themes, and plots across a complete narrative.

lessons.title: Visual Storytelling: Showing Information Without Words
lessons.brief: Students analyze scenes where filmmaking choices reveal character, backstory, and emotion without dialogue, understanding how cinema communicates differently than words.

lessons.title: Character Development Through Camera and Performance
lessons.brief: Students trace how a character changes across a film by examining performance choices, camera treatment, and narrative structure.

lessons.title: Mise-en-Scène: Everything in the Frame Means Something
lessons.brief: Students learn that set design, props, costumes, and blocking work together as a unified language to support themes and tell the story.

lessons.title: Sound Design: Dialogue, Music, and Ambient Sound as Layers
lessons.brief: Students examine how dialogue, musical score, and background sound are layered independently and mixed to create immersive, meaningful audio experiences.

grade_6.focus: Film is an art form and a medium of cultural communication where technical, narrative, and thematic choices reflect and shape meaning.

lessons.title: Genre Conventions: How Films Use and Break Expectations
lessons.brief: Students identify recurring visual, narrative, and sound patterns in genres (action, horror, romance) and analyze how filmmakers either follow or subvert these conventions for effect.

lessons.title: Point of View and Perspective in Cinematography
lessons.brief: Students examine how camera position, framing, and movement influence whose story we follow and what we know, exploring unreliable narration through visual technique.

lessons.title: Symbolism and Visual Metaphor in Film
lessons.brief: Students decode recurring visual symbols and metaphors in films—objects, colors, settings, camera movement—and discuss how filmmakers embed layers of meaning.

lessons.title: Film as Cultural Reflection: How Movies Show and Shape Society
lessons.brief: Students compare films from different eras and cultures, analyzing how filmmaking choices reveal cultural values and how widely seen films influence what audiences believe.

grade_7.focus: Film as a storytelling medium: how movies tell stories differently than books or theater.

lessons.title: How Films Show, Don't Tell
lessons.brief: Comparing visual storytelling in film to narrative description in books, using shot composition and editing.

lessons.title: The Grammar of Shots and Cuts
lessons.brief: Learning how camera angles, framing, and editing choices create meaning and emotion without dialogue.

lessons.title: Genres and What They Promise
lessons.brief: Exploring how different film genres (action, comedy, horror, drama) set audience expectations and use conventions.

lessons.title: The Director's Vision: One Film, Many Choices
lessons.brief: Analyzing how a director's choices in casting, music, color, and pacing shape the entire film's impact.

grade_8.focus: Film as cultural artifact: what movies reveal about the time and society that made them.

lessons.title: Reading a Film's Historical Context
lessons.brief: Examining how films reflect the values, fears, and politics of the era they were made in.

lessons.title: Representation and Stereotypes in Cinema
lessons.brief: Investigating how films portray different groups of people and the real-world impact of media representation.

lessons.title: The Business Behind the Scenes
lessons.brief: Understanding how studios, budgets, and distribution networks shape what stories get told and who sees them.

lessons.title: Adaptation: From Page to Screen
lessons.brief: Comparing how films adapt books or true events, and evaluating the creative choices made in translation.

grade_9.focus: Film as argument: how movies persuade audiences through emotion, image, and structure.

lessons.title: Framing an Argument Visually
lessons.brief: Analyzing how cinematography, mise-en-scène, and editing construct a specific viewpoint about events or characters.

lessons.title: Authorship and Interpretation
lessons.brief: Exploring the tension between a filmmaker's stated intent and what audiences actually take away from a film.

lessons.title: Documentary Objectivity and Bias
lessons.brief: Examining how documentary films claim to show truth while still making deliberate creative and editorial choices.

lessons.title: Sound Design as Persuasion
lessons.brief: Studying how music, dialogue, silence, and sound effects work with image to guide emotional and intellectual response.

grade_10.focus: Film analysis through critical frameworks: applying theory to interpret meaning and evaluate claims.

lessons.title: Auteur Theory and Its Limits
lessons.brief: Evaluating whether crediting a single 'author' (director) is useful or reductive when analyzing collaborative art.

lessons.title: Semiotics: Decoding Signs and Symbols in Film
lessons.brief: Learning how images, objects, and visual patterns function as signs that carry cultural and narrative meaning.

lessons.title: Narrative Structure Across Cultures
lessons.brief: Comparing how different filmmaking traditions structure stories, time, and causality based on cultural norms.

lessons.title: The Camera's Gaze: Power, Gender, and Perspective
lessons.brief: Analyzing how the camera position and editing choices reflect and reinforce power dynamics and point of view.

grade_11.focus: Film criticism and synthesis: developing independent arguments about form, meaning, and cultural significance.

lessons.title: Comparative Formal Analysis: Style as Argument
lessons.brief: Building evidence-based arguments about how two films use different formal strategies to express competing ideas.

lessons.title: Historiography in Film: Constructing the Past on Screen
lessons.brief: Critiquing how historical films construct narratives about real events and examining their claims to authenticity.

lessons.title: Ideology and Naturalization in Mainstream Cinema
lessons.brief: Investigating how conventional filmmaking techniques normalize particular worldviews and whose interests they serve.

lessons.title: Experimental Form and Resistance to Convention
lessons.brief: Studying avant-garde and innovative filmmaking as critiques of narrative and visual norms, and evaluating their effectiveness.

grade_12.focus: Film as a research subject: conducting original analysis and situating film within intellectual discourse.

lessons.title: Methodology: Designing a Film Analysis Project
lessons.brief: Developing rigorous research questions, defining analytical scope, and choosing appropriate critical frameworks.

lessons.title: Film and Interdisciplinary Inquiry
lessons.brief: Applying perspectives from philosophy, sociology, psychology, and history to complex film analysis and interpretation.

lessons.title: Archival Work and Film Restoration as Interpretation
lessons.brief: Examining how preservation decisions, lost footage, and restoration choices shape our access to and understanding of cinema.

lessons.title: Writing and Defending Film Criticism
lessons.brief: Constructing evidence-based arguments about film, engaging with existing scholarship, and articulating original claims.

grade_1.focus: Learning to recognise when someone is hurt and how to get help right away.

lessons.title: Spotting When Someone Needs Help
lessons.brief: Recognising signs that a person is hurt, sick, or in trouble using your eyes and ears.

lessons.title: Calling for Help: Adults and Emergency Numbers
lessons.brief: Learning who to tell when someone is hurt and that grown-ups know what to do.

lessons.title: Simple Safety Around Me
lessons.brief: Identifying common dangers at home, school, and play that can cause injuries.

lessons.title: My Body and What Hurts
lessons.brief: Naming body parts and learning which injuries are small and which need an adult's help.

grade_2.focus: Understanding basic first aid: what to do when someone is hurt and how to help safely.

lessons.title: The Recovery Position: Keeping Someone Safe
lessons.brief: Learning how to place an injured person in a safe, stable position if they cannot sit up.

lessons.title: Wounds and Bleeding: Cleaning and Covering
lessons.brief: Practical steps for caring for cuts and scrapes using water, cloth, and bandages.

lessons.title: Bumps, Bruises, and Sprains: What RICE Means
lessons.brief: Using Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation to care for minor injuries.

lessons.title: Burns and Choking: Quick Actions That Help
lessons.brief: Immediate, safe responses to burns and airway blockages before adults arrive.

grade_3.focus: Categorising injuries and illnesses, understanding what makes them serious, and practising appropriate responses.

lessons.title: Types of Injuries: How They Happen and What to Do
lessons.brief: Sorting injuries into categories (cuts, fractures, sprains, burns) and matching each to the right care.

lessons.title: Signs That an Injury Is Serious
lessons.brief: Learning what symptoms mean you must call emergency services rather than waiting for a regular appointment.

lessons.title: Illnesses and Fevers: When to Tell an Adult
lessons.brief: Recognising common illness signs and understanding which need medical attention.

lessons.title: First Aid Kit: What's Inside and Why It's There
lessons.brief: Exploring what tools and supplies are in a first aid kit and what job each one does.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how the body responds to injury and how first aid supports the body's natural healing.

lessons.title: How Bleeding and Shock Affect the Body
lessons.brief: Explaining why blood loss matters, what shock is, and how first aid slows bleeding and keeps the body stable.

lessons.title: Bones, Joints, and Immobilisation
lessons.brief: Understanding fractures and dislocations, and how keeping an injured limb still prevents further damage.

lessons.title: The Airway: Why Breathing Comes First
lessons.brief: Learning how the airway works and why clearing it is the priority in any emergency.

lessons.title: Infection and Wound Healing
lessons.brief: Exploring how germs cause infection, why cleanliness matters, and the stages of how skin repairs itself.

grade_5.focus: Applying first aid systematically using assessment frameworks and understanding decision-making in emergencies.

lessons.title: The ABC Check: Assessing an Unconscious Person
lessons.brief: Using Airway, Breathing, and Circulation checks to decide what help a person needs and in what order.

lessons.title: Resuscitation: CPR and Rescue Breathing Basics
lessons.brief: Learning the principles of chest compressions and rescue breathing and how they keep blood and oxygen moving.

lessons.title: Head, Neck, and Spine Injuries: Why Movement Matters
lessons.brief: Understanding how these injuries happen, why moving the patient can be dangerous, and how to stabilise safely.

lessons.title: Medical Emergencies: Recognising Heart Attacks, Strokes, and Seizures
lessons.brief: Identifying these conditions by their symptoms and knowing what first aid can and cannot do for each.

grade_6.focus: Analysing complex emergency scenarios, making ethical decisions under pressure, and understanding the limits and scope of first aid.

lessons.title: Triage: Deciding Who Needs Help First in Multi-Casualty Incidents
lessons.brief: Learning how to categorise multiple injured people by severity and allocate help logically when resources are limited.

lessons.title: Psychological First Aid: Recognising and Responding to Trauma
lessons.brief: Understanding shock, panic, and emotional distress in emergencies and how calm presence and reassurance help.

lessons.title: Legal and Ethical Responsibilities: Duty of Care and Consent
lessons.brief: Exploring when you are legally expected to help, how to get permission to treat someone, and when to step back.

lessons.title: Integrated Emergency Response: From Scene Assessment to Handover
lessons.brief: Planning a complete first aid response—safety first, assessing danger, treating injuries in priority order, and communicating with paramedics.

grade_7.focus: Learn the core skills and decision-making framework for responding to common emergencies.

lessons.title: The Chain of Survival: Why Minutes Matter
lessons.brief: Understand how early recognition, CPR, defibrillation, and advanced care work together to save lives in cardiac emergencies.

lessons.title: Recognizing and Treating Choking, Severe Bleeding, and Shock
lessons.brief: Identify the warning signs of life-threatening conditions and apply immediate, practical interventions.

lessons.title: When to Call for Help: Decision Trees in Real Situations
lessons.brief: Learn when to call emergency services, what information to give dispatchers, and how to stay calm while waiting for help.

lessons.title: Recovery Position and Moving an Injured Person Safely
lessons.brief: Master techniques for keeping an unconscious person's airway open and transporting casualties without causing further injury.

grade_8.focus: Evaluate different first aid approaches and understand the reasoning behind competing methods.

lessons.title: The Debate Over CPR Depth and Speed: What Does Evidence Show?
lessons.brief: Compare hands-only CPR versus conventional CPR; analyze why guidelines have changed and what research supports each approach.

lessons.title: Burn Treatment: Old Myths vs. Current Best Practice
lessons.brief: Investigate why outdated remedies (ice, butter, ointment) persist and examine the evidence for modern cooling and wound care.

lessons.title: Head, Neck, and Spinal Injuries: To Move or Not to Move?
lessons.brief: Explore the tension between preventing further spinal damage and the need to move someone from immediate danger; analyze real-world dilemmas.

lessons.title: Allergic Reactions and Anaphylaxis: Recognizing Severity Levels
lessons.brief: Distinguish between minor allergic reactions and life-threatening anaphylaxis; understand when and how to use an EpiPen.

grade_9.focus: Synthesize anatomical, physiological, and psychological knowledge to make complex decisions in messy real-world scenarios.

lessons.title: Shock States: Why the Body Fails and How to Support It
lessons.brief: Connect blood loss, organ perfusion, and compensatory mechanisms; learn to recognize and manage hypovolemic, anaphylactic, septic, and cardiogenic shock.

lessons.title: Head Injury Assessment: From Concussion to Intracranial Bleeding
lessons.brief: Use the Glasgow Coma Scale and loss-of-consciousness duration to assess severity; understand delayed presentation of epidural and subdural hematomas.

lessons.title: Psychological First Aid: Supporting Mental Health in Crisis
lessons.brief: Apply trauma-informed communication to victims and bystanders; explore how psychological shock affects decision-making and recovery.

lessons.title: Chest Injuries and Breathing Compromise: Anatomy in Action
lessons.brief: Analyze pneumothorax, flail chest, and cardiac tamponade; understand how anatomical disruption impairs breathing and circulation.

grade_10.focus: Interpret clinical evidence and medical literature to refine first aid protocols for different populations and contexts.

lessons.title: Reading and Critiquing First Aid Guidelines: From Trial Data to Practice
lessons.brief: Examine how randomized controlled trials shape resuscitation guidelines; analyze limitations of evidence and regional variations in recommendations.

lessons.title: Pediatric and Geriatric First Aid: How Age Changes Physiology and Treatment
lessons.brief: Compare child and adult anatomy, drug metabolism, and injury patterns; adapt CPR, medication dosing, and assessment for different age groups.

lessons.title: Wilderness First Aid: Managing Emergencies Without Hospital Access
lessons.brief: Explore how distance, terrain, and communication constraints change decision-making; study evacuation protocols and improvisation strategies.

lessons.title: Infection Control and Bloodborne Pathogen Risk in First Aid Practice
lessons.brief: Analyze transmission routes for HIV, hepatitis B and C; apply risk assessment frameworks and appropriate protective barriers in real scenarios.

grade_11.focus: Critique frameworks for first aid delivery across systems and evaluate ethical tensions in emergency care decision-making.

lessons.title: Triage Logic: How to Allocate Limited Resources When Everyone Needs Help
lessons.brief: Analyze START (Simple Triage and Rapid Treatment) and other triage systems; critique ethical assumptions and real-world failures in mass casualty events.

lessons.title: The Duty to Intervene vs. The Right to Refuse: Legal and Ethical Boundaries
lessons.brief: Examine Good Samaritan laws across jurisdictions; debate scenarios involving refusal of treatment, capacity assessment, and liability.

lessons.title: Resuscitation Ethics: When Should CPR Be Withheld or Stopped?
lessons.brief: Analyze DNR orders, futility, age, comorbidity, and time-to-treatment; compare utilitarian and rights-based approaches to withholding resuscitation.

lessons.title: First Aid System Design: Comparing Outcomes Across Countries and Models
lessons.brief: Research and compare first aid training prevalence, bystander CPR rates, and survival outcomes in different healthcare systems; critique equity of access.

grade_12.focus: Conduct original research on first aid effectiveness and make evidence-based arguments for policy and practice improvement.

lessons.title: Conducting a Systematic Review: What First Aid Interventions Actually Save Lives?
lessons.brief: Design a literature search strategy; evaluate study quality; synthesize evidence hierarchies; identify gaps and conflicting findings in first aid research.

lessons.title: Implementation Science: Why Good Evidence Doesn't Always Reach Practice
lessons.brief: Analyze barriers to adoption of evidence-based first aid (training accessibility, guideline inertia, regional variation); propose strategies for implementation and sustainability.

lessons.title: Designing First Aid Training Programs: Evidence, Equity, and Scalability
lessons.brief: Critique existing curricula; research effectiveness metrics (retention, skill decay, real-world application); propose evidence-based improvements for diverse populations.

lessons.title: The Future of First Aid: Technology, AI, and Global Health Perspectives
lessons.brief: Evaluate emerging interventions (automated external defibrillators, compression devices, telemedicine); assess feasibility and impact in low-resource settings.

grade_1.focus: Learning to hear, repeat, and name everyday objects and simple actions in a new language.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.brief: Students learn how to say hello, goodbye, and basic greetings, and practice the unique sounds of the new language.

lessons.title: Naming Things Around Us
lessons.brief: Students identify and name common objects in their classroom and home using single words and simple pointing.

lessons.title: Colors and Shapes
lessons.brief: Students learn to name and recognize colors and basic shapes, and match words to objects they can see.

lessons.title: Simple Actions We Do
lessons.brief: Students learn verbs for everyday movements like running, sitting, and eating by repeating and acting them out.

grade_2.focus: Building simple two-word sentences and describing what things are and what they do.

lessons.title: Who and What: Naming People and Things
lessons.brief: Students expand vocabulary to include family members, animals, and more objects, and start combining them into short phrases.

lessons.title: Doing and Being: Present Tense Verbs
lessons.brief: Students learn how to say what people and animals are doing right now using present tense verb forms.

lessons.title: Describing With Adjectives
lessons.brief: Students learn adjectives like big, small, happy, and sad, and practice placing them with nouns to make simple descriptions.

lessons.title: My Body and Senses
lessons.brief: Students name body parts and describe what they can see, hear, touch, and feel using new vocabulary.

grade_3.focus: Organizing vocabulary into categories and understanding how simple sentences work together to tell a story or explain something.

lessons.title: Sorting by Type: Food, Animals, and Clothes
lessons.brief: Students group vocabulary into clear categories and understand how objects belong to larger sets.

lessons.title: Cause and Effect With Simple Sentences
lessons.brief: Students learn to connect two ideas with 'because' and 'so' to explain why things happen in a sequence.

lessons.title: Days, Months, and Weather Patterns
lessons.brief: Students learn the calendar, seasons, and weather words, and notice how they follow a predictable order.

lessons.title: Subject and Verb Agreement
lessons.brief: Students learn that the verb must match the subject (I go, he goes) and practice building correct sentences.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how grammar systems work and using them to build more complex sentences that connect ideas logically.

lessons.title: Tense Systems: Past, Present, and Future
lessons.brief: Students learn how verbs change to show when actions happen and practice using regular and common irregular verbs.

lessons.title: Prepositions and Spatial Relationships
lessons.brief: Students master words like 'in,' 'on,' 'under,' and 'between' to describe where objects are positioned in relation to each other.

lessons.title: Building Longer Sentences With Conjunctions
lessons.brief: Students learn to connect independent clauses using 'and,' 'but,' 'or,' and 'because' to express more complex ideas.

lessons.title: Question Formation and Interrogative Words
lessons.brief: Students learn how to ask questions using who, what, where, when, and why, and understand how word order changes in questions.

grade_5.focus: Following multi-step processes and understanding how language varies depending on context, purpose, and audience.

lessons.title: Sequencing a Process: Instructions and Procedures
lessons.brief: Students learn to follow and write out multi-step instructions using ordinal numbers and transition words like 'first,' 'next,' and 'finally.'

lessons.title: Formal vs. Informal Speech
lessons.brief: Students discover that language changes depending on who you're talking to and why, and practice switching between casual and respectful forms.

lessons.title: Present Perfect: Connecting Past and Present
lessons.brief: Students learn to talk about recent actions that still matter now and understand how this tense differs from simple past.

lessons.title: Conditional Sentences: If This, Then That
lessons.brief: Students learn to express possibilities, consequences, and hypothetical situations using if-then structures.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how language works across different texts and contexts, and using complex grammar to express nuanced ideas and perspectives.

lessons.title: Text Types and Their Language Patterns
lessons.brief: Students examine how narrative, descriptive, persuasive, and informative texts each use grammar and vocabulary differently to achieve their purpose.

lessons.title: Subjunctive Mood and Expressing Uncertainty
lessons.brief: Students learn to express doubt, wishes, and hypothetical situations using subjunctive forms and modal verbs like 'might' and 'could.'

lessons.title: Embedded Clauses and Advanced Sentence Structure
lessons.brief: Students nest relative clauses and adverbial clauses within complex sentences to add detail and show relationships between ideas.

lessons.title: Register, Tone, and Cultural Context
lessons.brief: Students analyze how speakers adjust vocabulary, formality, and tone for different audiences and social situations across the target culture.

grade_7.focus: Building foundational communication skills and understanding how language reflects culture and identity.

lessons.title: Everyday Conversations Across Cultures
lessons.brief: Learning authentic dialogue patterns, greetings, and social conventions in the target language through real-world scenarios.

lessons.title: Stories That Shape Identity
lessons.brief: Exploring folktales, legends, and cultural narratives to understand how communities use language to express values and history.

lessons.title: The Geography of Language
lessons.brief: Investigating how geography, migration, and trade influenced the development and spread of the target language across regions.

grade_8.focus: Analyzing how language choices convey perspective and evaluating competing viewpoints within cultural texts.

lessons.title: Tone, Audience, and Persuasion in Media
lessons.brief: Examining how advertisements, news reports, and social media in the target language use language strategically to influence different audiences.

lessons.title: Debate: Presenting Both Sides
lessons.brief: Constructing and defending arguments on contemporary issues while understanding counterarguments, all conducted in the target language.

lessons.title: Historical Voices: Reading Primary Sources
lessons.brief: Interpreting letters, speeches, and documents from different time periods to understand how language reveals historical perspectives and biases.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing ideas from multiple sources to develop a coherent understanding of how language, literature, and society interconnect.

lessons.title: Literary Movements and Social Change
lessons.brief: Tracing how literary styles (Romanticism, Realism, Modernism) in the target language reflected and responded to social upheaval and ideological shifts.
