lessons.title: Power and Language: Who Speaks and Who Is Silenced
lessons.brief: Analyzing how language has been used to assert dominance, resist oppression, and give voice to marginalized communities across cultures.

lessons.title: Building a Personal Framework: What Texts Mean to Me
lessons.brief: Developing a critical lens by comparing personal interpretations of literature and media with established literary criticism and cultural theory.

grade_10.focus: Reading and interpreting original sources with nuance, recognizing ambiguity, subtext, and the limitations of single perspectives.

lessons.title: Decoding Subtext and Symbolism in Literature
lessons.brief: Close reading of poetry, novels, and drama to uncover implied meanings, metaphorical language, and how authors communicate beyond explicit statements.

lessons.title: Historical Context and Textual Interpretation
lessons.brief: Using archival research and historical documentation to understand how a text's meaning shifts depending on when and where it is read.

lessons.title: Reliability and Bias in Primary Sources
lessons.brief: Evaluating the credibility, limitations, and hidden agendas in letters, memoirs, speeches, and documents written in the target language.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing competing interpretative frameworks and constructing original arguments about literature, language, and culture with analytical rigor.

lessons.title: Competing Theories: How Critics Read the Same Text Differently
lessons.brief: Comparing feminist, postcolonial, Marxist, and psychoanalytic readings of canonical works to understand how theoretical frameworks shape interpretation.

lessons.title: Constructing an Argument: Evidence, Logic, and Counterargument
lessons.brief: Developing sophisticated written and oral arguments about texts with properly sourced evidence, logical structure, and deliberate engagement with opposing views.

lessons.title: Language as a System of Power: Deconstruction and Critique
lessons.brief: Examining how language itself encodes ideology, how translation transforms meaning, and how linguistic choices reinforce or challenge social hierarchies.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent research, synthesizing across disciplines, and producing original scholarship on language, literature, and culture.

lessons.title: Designing and Conducting Original Research
lessons.brief: Formulating research questions, locating primary and secondary sources, and building a defensible thesis through systematic investigation of cultural or linguistic phenomena.

lessons.title: Translation as Interpretation: Text, Culture, and Loss
lessons.brief: Analyzing how translation choices reflect interpretative decisions, exploring what is preserved and lost, and producing translations with critical commentary.

lessons.title: Interdisciplinary Synthesis: Connecting Literature to History, Philosophy, and Science
lessons.brief: Drawing connections across disciplines to explore how literary and linguistic works engage with broader intellectual movements and contemporary debates.

grade_1.focus: Learning to spot what is the same and what is different in the world around you.

lessons.title: Sorting Things by One Rule
lessons.brief: Students learn to group objects by a single property, like colour, size, or shape.

lessons.title: What Matches and What Doesn't
lessons.brief: Students identify whether two things belong together or are different.

lessons.title: Yes or No: True Statements About Real Things
lessons.brief: Students learn that some statements about objects are true and some are false.

grade_2.focus: Understanding how things fit into groups and what makes them belong together.

lessons.title: Sorting by More Than One Rule
lessons.brief: Students sort objects using two or more properties at the same time.

lessons.title: What Goes Where: Belonging and Not Belonging
lessons.brief: Students learn why some things belong in a group and why others do not.

lessons.title: Simple If-Then in Daily Life
lessons.brief: Students recognize that when one thing happens, another thing follows.

lessons.title: All, Some, and None
lessons.brief: Students use these words to describe groups and what members have in common.

grade_3.focus: Organizing ideas into categories and understanding how one event causes another.

lessons.title: Making Categories That Make Sense
lessons.brief: Students learn to create groups based on shared properties and understand why grouping matters.

lessons.title: Cause and Effect in Stories and Real Situations
lessons.brief: Students identify what happens first and what happens because of it.

lessons.title: Statements That Are Always True, Sometimes True, or Never True
lessons.brief: Students learn to evaluate whether claims are certain, possible, or impossible.

lessons.title: Comparing Groups: Bigger, Smaller, and the Same
lessons.brief: Students compare the size and properties of different categories.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how parts work together in a system and how logical connections hold things together.

lessons.title: Parts and the Whole: How Systems Work
lessons.brief: Students learn that complex things are made of smaller parts that depend on each other.

lessons.title: AND, OR, and NOT: Building True Statements
lessons.brief: Students use logical connectors to combine ideas and test whether statements are true or false.

lessons.title: If-Then Rules in Systems and Sequences
lessons.brief: Students trace how one rule leads to another in chains of cause and effect.

lessons.title: What Fits the Pattern and What Breaks It
lessons.brief: Students identify rules that govern patterns and recognize when something violates those rules.

grade_5.focus: Asking why things work the way they do and proving ideas using logical reasoning.

lessons.title: Building Arguments Step by Step
lessons.brief: Students learn to connect reasons together to support a conclusion.

lessons.title: Finding Flaws in an Argument
lessons.brief: Students identify when reasoning breaks down or when a conclusion doesn't follow from the reasons given.

lessons.title: Necessity and Possibility: What Must Be True and What Could Be True
lessons.brief: Students distinguish between statements that are always necessary and those that are only sometimes true.

lessons.title: Following Complex Chains of Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students trace through longer sequences of connected ideas and predict what must come next.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how ideas connect logically across systems and evaluating the strength of reasoning.

lessons.title: Formal and Informal Logic: When Proof Matters and When It Doesn't
lessons.brief: Students learn the difference between everyday reasoning and formal logical proof.

lessons.title: Recognizing Logical Fallacies in Real Arguments
lessons.brief: Students identify common mistakes in reasoning and understand why they mislead.

lessons.title: Propositions, Premises, and Conclusions: The Structure of Proof
lessons.brief: Students learn the formal parts of an argument and how to test whether a conclusion actually follows.

lessons.title: Logic Across Different Subjects: When the Same Rules Apply Everywhere
lessons.brief: Students discover that logical patterns in mathematics, science, and language follow the same rules.

grade_7.focus: Recognizing good arguments and spotting logical fallacies in everyday language.

lessons.title: What Makes an Argument Valid?
lessons.brief: Students learn the difference between a claim and an argument, and discover what it means for reasoning to be logically sound.

lessons.title: Common Logical Fallacies in Debate and Social Media
lessons.brief: Students identify ten common fallacies (ad hominem, straw man, appeal to authority, etc.) and spot them in real-world examples.

lessons.title: Premises, Conclusions, and Hidden Assumptions
lessons.brief: Students break down arguments into their parts and learn to find the unstated assumptions that hold arguments together.

lessons.title: Evaluating Source Credibility
lessons.brief: Students develop criteria for judging whether a speaker or source is trustworthy and how that affects the strength of their argument.

grade_8.focus: Analyzing the structure of arguments and evaluating competing claims on the same issue.

lessons.title: Deductive vs. Inductive Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students explore two fundamental argument patterns: top-down logical chains and bottom-up reasoning from examples.

lessons.title: Building a Strong Inductive Argument
lessons.brief: Students learn how to evaluate sample size, relevance, and counterexamples to judge whether generalizations from evidence are justified.

lessons.title: Mapping Arguments: Finding Strength and Weakness
lessons.brief: Students create visual diagrams of multi-step arguments to reveal where reasoning breaks down or where evidence is thin.

lessons.title: Both Sides of a Debate: Weighing Opposing Arguments
lessons.brief: Students learn to analyze arguments for and against a claim fairly, identifying which side has stronger evidence and reasoning.

grade_9.focus: Understanding formal logical systems and how to apply them to evaluate real-world reasoning.

lessons.title: Categorical Logic and Syllogisms
lessons.brief: Students learn the rules of categorical propositions and valid syllogistic forms, then test them against everyday claims.

lessons.title: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
lessons.brief: Students explore when one thing must lead to another, when it might, and how to avoid confusing these relationships in arguments.

lessons.title: Probability, Statistics, and Logical Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students learn how to interpret statistical claims logically, spot misuses of percentages and correlations, and avoid probabilistic fallacies.

lessons.title: Constructing a Logically Sound Argument
lessons.brief: Students synthesize previous learning to build their own multi-part arguments with clear premises, valid structure, and strong evidence.

grade_10.focus: Evaluating reasoning in original texts and understanding how logical framework shapes interpretation.

lessons.title: Logic in Philosophical and Political Texts
lessons.brief: Students analyze arguments from primary sources (philosophy, law, historical debate) to identify logical structure, assumptions, and hidden premises.

lessons.title: Begging the Question and Circular Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students develop sensitivity to subtle forms of circular logic and learn to distinguish them from valid iterative or recursive arguments.

lessons.title: Conditional Statements and Logical Chains
lessons.brief: Students master if-then reasoning, understand contrapositive and converse, and trace how assumptions cascade through multi-step arguments.

lessons.title: Identifying Bias in Logical Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students examine how selective evidence, framing, and logical shortcuts can make biased arguments appear sound without being objective.

grade_11.focus: Comparing different logical frameworks and critiquing the foundations of arguments themselves.

lessons.title: Formal Systems and Informal Logic: When Each Applies
lessons.brief: Students compare deductive formal logic with informal reasoning, exploring what can and cannot be proven within each system.

lessons.title: Abductive Reasoning and Inference to the Best Explanation
lessons.brief: Students examine how scientists, historians, and detectives reason backwards from evidence to hypotheses, and what makes an explanation 'best.'

lessons.title: Evaluating Trade-offs Between Logical Rigor and Real-World Relevance
lessons.brief: Students critique arguments that are logically valid but practically weak, and those that are persuasive but logically questionable.

lessons.title: Meta-Logic: Questioning the Assumptions Behind Logical Rules
lessons.brief: Students examine alternative logical systems (three-valued logic, fuzzy logic, modal logic) and consider when classical logic assumptions might fail.

grade_12.focus: Synthesizing formal logic with evidence research and constructing original arguments that withstand rigorous critique.

lessons.title: Research Design and the Logic of Empirical Evidence
lessons.brief: Students analyze how research methodology shapes what can be logically concluded, and critique the reasoning behind published studies.

lessons.title: Building Multi-Disciplinary Arguments with Cross-Domain Logic
lessons.brief: Students construct original arguments that integrate logical reasoning, evidence from multiple fields, and address counterarguments systematically.

lessons.title: Logical Fallacies in Academic and Professional Contexts
lessons.brief: Students identify subtle logical errors in policy papers, scientific abstracts, and opinion journalism, assessing impact on credibility and validity.

lessons.title: Defending and Revising Your Own Argument Under Challenge
lessons.brief: Students present their own reasoned positions, respond to objections using formal logic, and revise their arguments where logic reveals weakness.

grade_1.focus: Learning to notice plants and seeds, and what they need to grow.

lessons.title: Seeds All Around Us
lessons.brief: Finding, touching, and comparing different seeds from real plants.

lessons.title: What Plants Need to Live
lessons.brief: Discovering water, sunlight, and soil by watching plants every day.

lessons.title: Planting My First Seed
lessons.brief: Putting a seed in soil and observing what happens week by week.

lessons.title: Roots, Stems, and Leaves
lessons.brief: Learning the names of plant parts and what each one looks like.

grade_2.focus: Growing plants from seeds and learning how different plants have different needs.

lessons.title: How a Seed Becomes a Plant
lessons.brief: Following the stages from seed sprouting through leaf growth to a mature plant.

lessons.title: Sunlight and Shade: Which Plants Prefer What
lessons.brief: Growing the same plant in different light and observing the differences.

lessons.title: Watering: Too Much, Too Little, Just Right
lessons.brief: Testing how different amounts of water affect plant health.

lessons.title: Gardens Around Our School
lessons.brief: Identifying and naming plants and vegetables in real gardens nearby.

grade_3.focus: Sorting plants by their traits and understanding how gardeners help plants grow.

lessons.title: Classifying Plants: Vegetables, Fruits, Flowers, and Herbs
lessons.brief: Grouping plants by what part we eat or use, and comparing their features.

lessons.title: The Soil Food Web: What Lives in Garden Soil
lessons.brief: Observing tiny creatures and decomposers, and why they matter for plants.

lessons.title: From Planting to Harvest: The Growing Timeline
lessons.brief: Following a plant through its life cycle and identifying key stages.

lessons.title: Garden Tools and Their Jobs
lessons.brief: Learning what each tool does and how to use it safely and well.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how gardens work as systems where soil, water, sunlight, and living things depend on each other.

lessons.title: Soil Structure: Sand, Silt, Clay, and Organic Matter
lessons.brief: Analyzing soil composition and how different textures affect water and root growth.

lessons.title: Nutrient Cycles: How Plants Get Fed
lessons.brief: Tracing nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium through soil and into plants.

lessons.title: Photosynthesis and Why Plants Make Their Own Food
lessons.brief: Investigating how sunlight, water, and air combine to feed a plant.

lessons.title: Pollinators and Plant Reproduction
lessons.brief: Observing how bees, insects, and wind move pollen and create seeds.

grade_5.focus: Designing and managing a productive garden by applying ecological and biological principles.

lessons.title: Crop Rotation and Soil Health: Planning a Multi-Year Garden
lessons.brief: Learning why different plant families should rotate through beds and how this prevents disease.

lessons.title: Composting: Turning Waste into Garden Gold
lessons.brief: Managing a compost system and understanding decomposition as a nutrient cycle.

lessons.title: Pest and Disease Management Without Chemicals
lessons.brief: Using companion planting, beneficial insects, and observation to keep plants healthy.

lessons.title: Water Efficiency: Irrigation and Conservation
lessons.brief: Calculating water needs, testing soil moisture, and choosing efficient watering methods.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how gardens interact with climate, ecosystems, and human food systems.

lessons.title: Microclimate and Plant Selection: Designing for Your Environment
lessons.brief: Mapping microclimates in a garden site and choosing plants suited to specific conditions.

lessons.title: Food Webs in the Garden: From Soil Microbes to Predators
lessons.brief: Mapping energy and nutrient flow through a garden ecosystem and the role of each level.

lessons.title: Seed Saving and Plant Genetics: Preserving Diversity
lessons.brief: Collecting and storing seeds, understanding heredity, and why genetic diversity matters.

lessons.title: Gardens and Global Food: Local Growing vs. Industrial Agriculture
lessons.brief: Comparing how home gardens, community gardens, and large farms produce food differently.

grade_7.focus: Garden planning and design: how to observe a space, choose plants, and create a functional layout.

lessons.title: Reading Your Garden Site
lessons.brief: Students map sunlight, soil type, water drainage, and microclimates to understand what a garden space can actually support.

lessons.title: Matching Plants to Place
lessons.brief: Students learn to select plants based on hardiness, water needs, and site conditions rather than just preference.

lessons.title: Garden Layout and Scale
lessons.brief: Students sketch garden designs on paper, considering plant spacing, height progression, and practical access.

lessons.title: Soil as Foundation
lessons.brief: Students test and amend soil, learning why soil composition matters more than starting with perfect conditions.

grade_8.focus: Garden systems: understanding how nutrients cycle, pests and beneficial insects interact, and gardens function as ecosystems.

lessons.title: Nutrient Cycling and Composting
lessons.brief: Students build compost systems and trace how organic matter breaks down to feed plants, closing the waste loop.

lessons.title: Pest and Predator Relationships
lessons.brief: Students observe and identify garden insects, debating when intervention is needed and comparing chemical versus ecological control.

lessons.title: Water Management in Gardens
lessons.brief: Students measure rainfall and irrigation, exploring how to conserve water while meeting plant needs in different seasons.

lessons.title: Building Soil Health Over Time
lessons.brief: Students monitor soil structure, microbial activity, and fertility changes across a growing season to understand soil as a living system.

grade_9.focus: Garden productivity and adaptation: maximizing yield, extending seasons, and adjusting practices based on changing conditions.

lessons.title: Succession Planting and Crop Rotation
lessons.brief: Students design multi-season planting schedules to produce food continuously and prevent soil depletion.

lessons.title: Starting from Seed: Germination and Propagation
lessons.brief: Students germinate seeds under controlled conditions and propagate plants vegetatively, comparing success rates and advantages of each method.

lessons.title: Season Extension Techniques
lessons.brief: Students build and use cold frames, row covers, or simple greenhouse structures to grow outside normal seasons.

lessons.title: Reading Plant Signals and Adjusting Care
lessons.brief: Students observe stress symptoms, nutrient deficiencies, and disease signs, then evaluate and adjust watering, feeding, and pruning responses.

grade_10.focus: Garden science and decision-making: interpreting research, evaluating horticultural methods, and making evidence-based choices.

lessons.title: Interpreting Seed Packets and Plant Labels
lessons.brief: Students decode botanical nomenclature, hardiness zones, days-to-maturity, and spacing recommendations, then source seeds from primary catalogs.

lessons.title: Fertilizer Types and Application Science
lessons.brief: Students analyze NPK ratios, organic versus synthetic fertilizers, and soil test results to justify fertilizer choices with evidence.

lessons.title: Pruning Strategy and Plant Architecture
lessons.brief: Students study plant growth habits, learn pruning cuts and timing for specific goals, and explain how pruning alters plant form and productivity.

lessons.title: Disease, Disorder, and Diagnosis
lessons.brief: Students distinguish between pathogenic disease, environmental stress, and nutrient deficiency using observation, research, and systematic elimination.

grade_11.focus: Garden philosophy and critique: examining horticultural frameworks (organic, conventional, permaculture), weighing trade-offs, and developing a personal gardening ethic.

lessons.title: Organic, Conventional, and Alternative Gardening: Comparing Frameworks
lessons.brief: Students examine the principles, trade-offs, and scientific evidence behind organic certification, synthetic inputs, and emerging methods like regenerative agriculture.

lessons.title: Indigenous and Traditional Gardening Knowledge
lessons.brief: Students research place-based gardening practices, polycultures, and food systems, evaluating how traditional knowledge differs from industrial horticulture.

lessons.title: Garden Scale and Sustainability: From Backyard to Food System
lessons.brief: Students critique how garden design choices (monoculture, diversity, scale) affect sustainability, resilience, and food justice.

lessons.title: Building an Evidence-Based Garden Experiment
lessons.brief: Students design and conduct a controlled gardening experiment (e.g., comparing fertilizer types or planting methods), collect data, and present findings.

grade_12.focus: Advanced horticultural research and synthesis: conducting independent investigations, connecting gardening to ecology and society, and arguing for a informed gardening practice.

lessons.title: Soil Science and Microbiology in Gardening
lessons.brief: Students engage with peer-reviewed soil science literature, analyze microbial relationships, and examine how soil biology informs sustainable amendment strategies.

lessons.title: Climate Adaptation and Phenology in Gardens
lessons.brief: Students research how shifting climate zones affect plant hardiness, bloom timing, and pest cycles, then propose adaptive gardening strategies with evidence.

lessons.title: Garden as Cultural and Ecological Commons
lessons.brief: Students examine gardening through lenses of food sovereignty, biodiversity conservation, and social equity, synthesizing horticultural practice with broader systems.

lessons.title: Capstone: Designing and Defending a Garden System
lessons.brief: Students design a comprehensive garden system for a real or hypothetical context, justify choices with research, and defend their framework against alternative approaches.

grade_1.focus: Learning to see and name the natural and human-made places around you.

lessons.title: Places I Can See and Touch
lessons.brief: Identifying simple places like home, school, park, and water using senses.

lessons.title: Weather Changes Every Day
lessons.brief: Noticing and naming different weather—sun, rain, wind, snow—and how it feels.

lessons.title: Maps Show Where Things Are
lessons.brief: Using simple pictures and symbols to find familiar places on a map.

lessons.title: Land and Water
lessons.brief: Recognising and naming mountains, fields, rivers, lakes, and oceans.

grade_2.focus: Describing how people and nature share different kinds of places and what makes each place special.

lessons.title: People Live in Different Kinds of Homes
lessons.brief: Exploring how houses, apartments, and shelters suit different places and climates.

lessons.title: Jobs People Do in Different Places
lessons.brief: Discovering why farmers, fishers, and builders work in different environments.

lessons.title: Seasons Change What We See
lessons.brief: Tracking how plants, animals, and weather change through spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

lessons.title: Maps Help Us Find Our Way
lessons.brief: Reading simple maps with symbols, directions, and labels to locate places.

grade_3.focus: Sorting places into types and understanding how geography affects the way people live.

lessons.title: Deserts, Forests, and Wetlands: Biomes Explained
lessons.brief: Categorising Earth's major environments by climate, plants, and animals that live there.

lessons.title: How Mountains, Rivers, and Plains Shape Communities
lessons.brief: Observing how landforms influence where people build towns and how they farm or fish.

lessons.title: Native Peoples and Their Landscapes
lessons.brief: Learning how indigenous groups adapted to their local geography and natural resources.

lessons.title: Compass Directions and Grid Maps
lessons.brief: Using compass points and grid lines to locate specific places on maps accurately.

grade_4.focus: Understanding Earth as interconnected systems where climate, landforms, resources, and human settlement form patterns.

lessons.title: The Water Cycle and River Systems
lessons.brief: Tracing how water evaporates, condenses, and flows through the landscape to shape geography.

lessons.title: Climate Zones and How They Determine Resources
lessons.brief: Analysing how latitude and ocean currents create climate patterns that affect what people can grow and build.

lessons.title: Trade Routes: Why People Connect Across Distance
lessons.brief: Exploring how geography influences where trade happens and how goods move between places.

lessons.title: Reading Complex Maps: Layers of Information
lessons.brief: Interpreting maps showing elevation, population density, resources, and political boundaries simultaneously.

grade_5.focus: Investigating how geographical processes—erosion, migration, urbanisation—reshape the world over time and affect human societies.

lessons.title: Plate Tectonics: Why Earthquakes and Volcanoes Occur
lessons.brief: Understanding how Earth's moving plates create mountains, earthquakes, and volcanic activity that reshape landscapes.

lessons.title: Erosion and Weathering: How Landscapes Change
lessons.brief: Examining how wind, water, and ice gradually wear down rock and soil, creating valleys, deltas, and beaches.

lessons.title: Population Growth and Urban Expansion
lessons.brief: Analysing why cities grow, what challenges rapid urbanisation creates, and how geography influences city location and sprawl.

lessons.title: Cultural Regions: Language, Religion, and Geography
lessons.brief: Exploring how geography influences cultural identity and why certain beliefs, languages, and traditions cluster in regions.

grade_6.focus: Evaluating how humans interact with and depend on Earth's physical systems, and predicting consequences of geographical change.

lessons.title: Climate Systems and Global Weather Patterns
lessons.brief: Analysing how Earth's rotation, atmospheric circulation, and ocean currents create weather and climate zones worldwide.

lessons.title: Resource Distribution and Geopolitical Conflict
lessons.brief: Investigating how unequal access to water, minerals, and fertile land creates competition, migration, and political tensions.

lessons.title: Ecosystems and Biodiversity Under Pressure
lessons.brief: Evaluating how deforestation, pollution, and climate change threaten ecosystems and what geographic solutions exist.

lessons.title: Sustainable Development: Balancing Growth and Environment
lessons.brief: Critically examining how societies can meet economic needs while protecting geography and natural resources for the future.

grade_7.focus: How physical geography shapes where people live and what resources are available to them.

lessons.title: Climate Zones and Human Settlement Patterns
lessons.brief: Explores how temperature, rainfall, and seasons determine where civilizations develop and how people adapt to different environments.

lessons.title: Landforms, Rivers, and Access to Water
lessons.brief: Examines how mountains, valleys, coastlines, and river systems influence population density, trade routes, and economic activity.

lessons.title: Natural Resources and What Societies Need
lessons.brief: Investigates how the location of forests, minerals, fertile soil, and fossil fuels drives where industries develop and what nations trade.

lessons.title: Natural Hazards and Risk Across Regions
lessons.brief: Analyzes why earthquakes, hurricanes, floods, and droughts affect some regions more than others and how geography makes communities vulnerable.

grade_8.focus: How human societies actively shape and respond to their geography, and how geography in turn shapes human choices and power.

lessons.title: Colonialism and Geographic Advantage
lessons.brief: Examines how European powers used geography—coastlines, navigable rivers, and resource wealth—to justify expansion and extract resources from colonized territories.

lessons.title: Why Cities Grow Where They Do
lessons.brief: Analyzes the geographic factors (rivers, harbors, trade crossroads) that attracted historical urban centers and continues to drive modern urban expansion.

lessons.title: Borders, Boundaries, and Disputed Territories
lessons.brief: Explores how political boundaries are drawn (often arbitrarily by colonial powers), how geography fuels territorial disputes, and why some borders are contested today.

lessons.title: The Geography of Inequality: Why Some Regions Are Richer
lessons.brief: Investigates whether geography determines poverty and wealth or whether historical, political, and economic choices matter more—and debates both sides.

grade_9.focus: Interconnected global systems: how geography, economics, culture, and politics link regions together and create unequal flows of people, goods, and power.

lessons.title: Global Supply Chains and Geographic Inequality
lessons.brief: Traces how manufactured goods move from resource-rich regions to factory zones to wealthy consumer markets, and examines who profits at each stage.

lessons.title: Migration, Diaspora, and Transnational Communities
lessons.brief: Analyzes why people move across borders (economic pull, climate push, conflict, persecution) and how migration networks create cultural and economic ties across regions.

lessons.title: Geopolitics: How Geography Shapes International Conflict and Alliances
lessons.brief: Examines how access to sea routes, shared borders, strategic location, and resource competition drive alliances, tensions, and power dynamics between nations.

lessons.title: Environmental Limits and Unequal Resource Use
lessons.brief: Integrates geography, ecology, and justice: explores how wealthy nations consume disproportionate resources and how pollution and climate impacts fall unevenly on poorer regions.

grade_10.focus: Critical interpretation of geographic data and sources: how to read maps, statistics, and primary documents to construct and question geographic arguments about development, inequality, and power.

lessons.title: Reading Maps as Arguments: Projection, Perspective, and Power
lessons.brief: Decodes how map projections distort reality (Mercator enlarges wealthy nations), how maps are used to legitimize claims, and how to recognize bias in cartographic representation.

lessons.title: Development Indicators and How We Measure Progress
lessons.brief: Critiques GDP, HDI, and other measures of development: examines what they reveal and conceal, why wealthy nations define 'development,' and whose interests are served by these measures.

lessons.title: Trade Data, Commodity Chains, and Economic Dependency
lessons.brief: Analyzes bilateral and multilateral trade statistics to identify economic relationships, shows how some nations export raw materials while others export finished goods, and questions fair trade models.

lessons.title: Sources of Geographic Knowledge: Whose Voices Matter?
lessons.brief: Evaluates academic geography, journalism, indigenous knowledge, and NGO reports as sources of geographic truth; asks whose perspectives are centered and whose are marginalized.

grade_11.focus: Competing geographic theories and frameworks: examining how different schools of thought explain global inequality, power, and change, and evaluating their strengths and limitations.

lessons.title: Development Theory: Modernization vs. Dependency vs. World-Systems Analysis
lessons.brief: Compares three major frameworks for explaining global inequality—which assumes poor regions will develop if they adopt Western practices, which highlights colonial extraction, which maps core-periphery relationships—and evaluates evidence for each.

lessons.title: Postcolonial Geography: Legacies of Empire in the Contemporary World
lessons.brief: Applies postcolonial critique to geography: examines how colonial boundaries, languages, and power structures persist; analyzes geographic knowledge itself as a colonial tool; critiques Western-centric frameworks.

lessons.title: Political Ecology: Environment, Justice, and the Politics of Nature
lessons.brief: Synthesizes ecology and political economy: shows how environmental problems are rooted in unequal power relations, how pollution and resource extraction are spatially uneven, and how marginalized communities organize for environmental justice.

lessons.title: Scale and Scalar Politics: Local, National, Global, and Everything Between
lessons.brief: Critically examines the concept of 'scale' itself; analyzes how power operates across scales; shows how global forces reshape local places and how local resistance reaches global levels.

grade_12.focus: Independent geographic research and argument: synthesizing theory, evidence, and critique to construct original arguments about contemporary geographic issues and their historical roots.

lessons.title: Researching a Geographic Controversy: Method, Sources, and Evidence
lessons.brief: Guides students through selecting a contested geographic issue (e.g., land rights, resource extraction, border disputes), locating primary sources and scholarship, evaluating competing claims, and building an evidence-based argument.

lessons.title: Comparative Analysis: How the Same Geographic Process Unfolds Differently Across Regions
lessons.brief: Teaches structured comparison of urbanization, migration, environmental degradation, or economic integration in contrasting national or regional contexts; identifies patterns while respecting context-specific particularities.

lessons.title: Interrogating Geography's Own Assumptions: Critique and Reflexivity
lessons.brief: Encourages students to question foundational geographic concepts (nature vs. culture, development, region, scale); examines whose interests are served by geographic knowledge; considers ethics and responsibility in geographic research and representation.

lessons.title: Futures Thinking: Projecting Geographic Change and Imagining Alternatives
lessons.brief: Applies geographic analysis to possible futures: scenarios for climate migration, resource scarcity, or geopolitical shifts; explores how different communities are imagining and building alternative geographic futures; considers geographic justice in planning.

grade_1.focus: Learning the names and functions of your body parts, and how to keep them clean and safe.

lessons.title: My Body: Head to Toe
lessons.brief: Identifying and naming the main parts of the body and what each part does.

lessons.title: Wash, Brush, and Stay Clean
lessons.brief: Learning daily hygiene routines like hand-washing, brushing teeth, and bathing.

lessons.title: Safe and Unsafe Touches
lessons.brief: Understanding which touches are safe, who can touch you, and what to do if someone makes you uncomfortable.

lessons.title: Foods That Help Me Grow
lessons.brief: Learning which foods are healthy and which are treats, and why our bodies need different foods.

grade_2.focus: Understanding how your body moves, grows, and tells you when something is wrong.

lessons.title: Bones, Muscles, and How I Move
lessons.brief: Discovering how bones and muscles work together to help you run, jump, and play.

lessons.title: My Senses: Seeing, Hearing, Tasting, Touching, and Smelling
lessons.brief: Exploring how your five senses help you learn about the world around you.

lessons.title: When My Body Needs Rest
lessons.brief: Learning why sleep and rest are important and how much your body needs.

lessons.title: Signals My Body Sends: Hunger, Tired, and Sick
lessons.brief: Recognising what your body tells you through hunger, tiredness, pain, and other feelings.

grade_3.focus: Categorising body systems and understanding how different parts work together to keep you healthy.

lessons.title: The Skeleton and Muscles: Building and Moving
lessons.brief: Learning how bones provide structure and muscles create movement, and how they depend on each other.

lessons.title: The Digestive System: From Mouth to Energy
lessons.brief: Tracing what happens to food from when you eat it until your body uses it for energy.

lessons.title: The Circulatory System: Your Heart Pumps Blood
lessons.brief: Understanding how your heart pumps blood through your body to carry oxygen and nutrients.

lessons.title: Germs, Illness, and How Your Body Fights Back
lessons.brief: Learning how germs cause illness and how your immune system protects you from getting sick.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how body systems interact as an integrated whole to maintain health and respond to your environment.

lessons.title: The Respiratory System: Breathing In and Out
lessons.brief: Exploring how lungs take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide, and why breathing is essential for every cell.

lessons.title: The Nervous System: Brain, Nerves, and Reactions
lessons.brief: Discovering how your brain and nerves control movement, thoughts, and your body's responses to the world.

lessons.title: How Systems Work Together: The Whole Body
lessons.brief: Examining how the skeletal, muscular, digestive, circulatory, respiratory, and nervous systems depend on each other.

lessons.title: Fitness and Flexibility: Exercise for a Healthy Body
lessons.brief: Learning how different types of exercise strengthen your heart, muscles, and flexibility.

grade_5.focus: Analysing how body systems regulate themselves and respond to physical challenges, and how lifestyle choices affect long-term health.

lessons.title: Hormones and Growth: How Your Body Changes
lessons.brief: Understanding how chemical messengers called hormones control growth, development, and body processes.

lessons.title: Nutrition and Energy: Proteins, Carbohydrates, Fats, and Vitamins
lessons.brief: Learning what different nutrients do in your body and why you need a balance of each type.

lessons.title: The Immune System: Defences Against Disease
lessons.brief: Exploring how white blood cells, antibodies, and inflammation protect you and help you recover from illness.

lessons.title: Stress, Sleep, and Mental Health
lessons.brief: Investigating how stress affects your body, why sleep is critical for recovery, and how emotions influence health.

grade_6.focus: Examining the physiological and psychological connections between body systems and evaluating how personal choices create patterns of health or disease across a lifetime.

lessons.title: Homeostasis: How Your Body Maintains Balance
lessons.brief: Analysing how the body uses feedback loops to regulate temperature, pH, water balance, and other internal conditions.

lessons.title: The Endocrine System: Hormones and Development
lessons.brief: Investigating how the endocrine system controls metabolism, growth, reproduction, and emotional responses.

lessons.title: Chronic Disease, Lifestyle, and Prevention
lessons.brief: Examining how repeated choices about exercise, nutrition, and stress accumulate to influence risk for heart disease, diabetes, and obesity.

lessons.title: Mental and Physical Health: The Mind-Body Connection
lessons.brief: Exploring how thoughts, emotions, and stress affect physical health outcomes and how physical activity influences mental wellbeing.

grade_7.focus: How the human body works as an interconnected system and why understanding it matters for making good decisions about health.

lessons.title: Systems Under the Skin: Organs, Nerves, and How They Talk to Each Other
lessons.brief: Exploration of major body systems (circulatory, nervous, digestive, respiratory) and how they communicate and depend on each other.

lessons.title: Fuel, Movement, and Growth: What Your Body Actually Needs
lessons.brief: How nutrition, hydration, sleep, and exercise work together to support development during puberty and adolescence.

lessons.title: When Things Go Wrong: Common Teen Health Issues and What Actually Helps
lessons.brief: Recognition and practical responses to common problems like acne, fatigue, headaches, and minor infections.

lessons.title: Your Brain on Change: Why Emotions and Moods Shift in Your Teens
lessons.brief: How hormonal and neurological changes during adolescence affect mood, stress, and decision-making.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating competing health claims and understanding the science behind what actually works versus what's marketing or myth.

lessons.title: Spotting the Difference: Science-Based Health Information vs. Marketing and Misinformation
lessons.brief: How to read and critique health claims using evidence, source credibility, and logical reasoning.

lessons.title: The Supplement Trap: What Evidence Actually Says About Vitamins, Protein Powders, and 'Natural' Products
lessons.brief: Examination of the supplement industry, what claims are supported, and why regulation differs from pharmaceuticals.

lessons.title: Mental Health Is Physical Health: Anxiety, Stress, and the Brain-Body Connection
lessons.brief: How psychological stress affects physical symptoms and how lifestyle changes can influence mental wellbeing.

lessons.title: Caffeine, Energy Drinks, and Sleep: What's Actually Happening in Your Body
lessons.brief: Analysis of stimulants, their effects on the nervous system, and why sleep science matters for teens.

grade_9.focus: Building a personal framework for health decisions by understanding risk, trade-offs, and the factors that influence individual health outcomes.

lessons.title: Why People Make Different Health Choices: Culture, Economics, Access, and Values
lessons.brief: Examination of how socioeconomic status, cultural beliefs, geography, and family history shape what health options are available and meaningful.

lessons.title: Risk, Reward, and Individual Variation: Why One Diet or Workout Plan Doesn't Fit Everyone
lessons.brief: Synthesis of genetics, metabolism, lifestyle, and personal circumstances to understand why health advice is contextual.

lessons.title: Mapping the Causes: Disease, Prevention, and Lifestyle vs. Luck
lessons.brief: Exploration of how chronic diseases develop, the role of prevention, and the limits of individual responsibility in outcomes.

lessons.title: Building Your Own Framework: How to Make Health Decisions When There's No Perfect Answer
lessons.brief: Development of personal decision-making tools for navigating uncertainty, conflicting advice, and trade-offs in health choices.

grade_10.focus: Reading and interpreting scientific literature on health to understand how evidence is generated, what it actually proves, and its limitations.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a Study: How Health Research Is Designed, Conducted, and Reported
lessons.brief: Close reading of study methodologies, sample sizes, controls, and limitations to evaluate what a single study can and cannot claim.

lessons.title: Correlation, Causation, and Confounding: Why Headlines Lie and Studies Sometimes Contradict
lessons.brief: Analysis of how media misrepresents research findings and interpretation of genuine disagreements in the scientific literature.

lessons.title: The Body as System: How Drugs, Nutrients, and Interventions Interact With Multiple Pathways
lessons.brief: Examination of pharmacology and biochemistry at a level that explains why a single molecule can have multiple effects and side effects.

lessons.title: Public Health Data: Reading Statistics, Epidemiology, and Population-Level Claims
lessons.brief: Interpretation of epidemiological data, disease incidence and prevalence, and the difference between individual and population-level truths.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing and comparing competing health frameworks—from biomedical to social models—and understanding the assumptions and evidence behind each.

lessons.title: Disease Models in Tension: Biomedical, Biopsychosocial, and Social Determinants Frameworks
lessons.brief: Critical comparison of how different theoretical models explain health, illness, and what counts as a solution, with evidence and limitations of each.

lessons.title: Whose Health? Power, Inequality, and the Politics of Medical Knowledge
lessons.brief: Analysis of how historical health practices, medical ethics violations, and systemic inequities shape who gets believed, studied, and treated fairly.

lessons.title: Precision Medicine vs. One-Size-Fits-All: When Individualization Makes Sense and When It Doesn't
lessons.brief: Evaluation of emerging genetic, pharmacogenomic, and personalized medicine claims against current evidence and practical feasibility.

lessons.title: Constructing Arguments About Prevention: What Society Should Fund and Why
lessons.brief: Development and defence of evidence-based arguments about public health priorities, trade-offs, and resource allocation using original sources.

grade_12.focus: Conducting original inquiry into a health question using multiple methodologies and evidence sources, while synthesizing across scientific, ethical, historical, and policy perspectives.

lessons.title: Designing a Health Inquiry: Formulating Researchable Questions and Selecting Appropriate Methods
lessons.brief: Development of a rigorous research question, literature review strategy, and methodological design (qualitative, quantitative, or mixed) appropriate to the inquiry.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Evidence Across Disciplines: When Medicine, History, Ethics, and Policy Intersect
lessons.brief: Integration of scientific data, historical context, ethical frameworks, and policy analysis to construct evidence-based arguments on complex health issues.

lessons.title: Evaluating Trade-Offs in Real Health Decisions: Individual Liberty, Collective Benefit, and Justice
lessons.brief: Rigorous analysis of competing values and stakeholders in health decisions (e.g., vaccination mandates, healthcare access) using philosophical and empirical tools.

lessons.title: Communicating Health Research to Different Audiences: Accuracy Without Oversimplification
lessons.brief: Crafting evidence-based health communication for multiple audiences (peers, policymakers, public) while preserving nuance and acknowledging uncertainty.

grade_1.focus: Rules keep us safe and fair: learning that laws are simple agreements we follow at home, at school, and in our community.

lessons.title: Rules in My Home
lessons.brief: Discovering that families have rules about bedtime, sharing toys, and being kind, and what happens when we break them.

lessons.title: Rules at School
lessons.brief: Learning why schools have rules about lining up, listening, and taking turns, and how teachers help us follow them.

lessons.title: Helpers in Our Community
lessons.brief: Meeting police officers, firefighters, and crossing guards as people who help keep our neighbourhood safe.

grade_2.focus: Laws protect people and property: understanding that communities have rules called laws, and people called officials enforce them to keep everyone safe.

lessons.title: What Is a Law?
lessons.brief: Naming real laws that affect everyday life—no stealing, no hitting, crossing at the light—and why communities make them.

lessons.title: Who Makes and Enforces Laws
lessons.brief: Learning that police, judges, and government leaders create and enforce laws to protect people and things we own.

lessons.title: Consequences of Breaking Laws
lessons.brief: Exploring what happens when someone breaks a law, including warnings, fines, and more serious punishments.

lessons.title: Rights and Responsibilities
lessons.brief: Discovering that laws give us rights (like being safe and going to school) and responsibilities (like following rules and respecting others).

grade_3.focus: Laws come from people and purposes: categorising different types of laws and understanding that they solve specific problems in a community.

lessons.title: Types of Laws Around Us
lessons.brief: Sorting laws into categories—safety laws (seatbelts, helmets), property laws (no stealing), and rules for fairness (equal treatment).

lessons.title: Why Communities Need Different Laws
lessons.brief: Connecting specific laws to the problems they solve: traffic lights stop accidents, food safety laws prevent sickness, school attendance laws ensure education.

lessons.title: How Laws Are Made
lessons.brief: Following the simple process of how people propose ideas, discuss them, vote, and create new laws to help the community.

lessons.title: Fair and Unfair Laws
lessons.brief: Comparing laws that treat everyone equally with historical laws that were unfair, and why some laws need to change.

grade_4.focus: Legal systems balance rights and order: understanding how courts, police, and government institutions work together to enforce laws fairly and protect citizens.

lessons.title: The Structure of Courts
lessons.brief: Mapping how small claims courts, criminal courts, and appeals courts work, and why different cases go to different courts.

lessons.title: Police, Prosecutors, and Defence
lessons.brief: Explaining the roles of police investigators, prosecutors who argue the case, and defence lawyers who protect the accused's rights.

lessons.title: Evidence and Proof in Court
lessons.brief: Understanding what counts as evidence (witnesses, documents, objects) and why courts require proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

lessons.title: Rights of the Accused
lessons.brief: Exploring protections built into law for people accused of crimes: the right to a lawyer, the right to a fair trial, and the right to silence.

grade_5.focus: Laws reflect society's values and change over time: tracing how legal systems develop, adapt to new challenges, and reflect what communities believe is right.

lessons.title: How Laws Evolve with Society
lessons.brief: Examining how laws change as values change—from slavery being legal to child labour laws to modern environmental protections—and why.

lessons.title: Rights, Freedoms, and Their Limits
lessons.brief: Analysing fundamental rights (speech, religion, privacy) and understanding where courts draw the line when rights conflict with public safety.

lessons.title: Criminal Law vs. Civil Law
lessons.brief: Distinguishing between crimes against society (theft, assault) that result in punishment and civil disputes (contracts, accidents) that result in compensation.

lessons.title: International Law and Human Rights
lessons.brief: Exploring laws that cross country borders, treaties between nations, and global agreements protecting human rights and preventing war.

grade_6.focus: Legal systems balance power, access, and justice: analysing how laws are applied unequally, how institutions maintain authority, and what makes justice truly fair.

lessons.title: Power and Inequality in Legal Systems
lessons.brief: Critically examining how wealth, race, and privilege affect who gets arrested, convicted, and sentenced—and efforts to reduce these disparities.

lessons.title: Constitutional Limits on Government Power
lessons.brief: Analysing how constitutions and charters restrict what governments can do, protecting citizens from abuse while balancing order and freedom.

lessons.title: Access to Justice: Who Can Use the Law?
lessons.brief: Investigating barriers to justice—cost, language, knowledge—and how legal aid, small claims courts, and reform try to make law accessible to everyone.

lessons.title: Reforming Laws and Justice Systems
lessons.brief: Examining current debates about sentencing, rehabilitation versus punishment, restorative justice, and how movements push legal systems to change.

grade_7.focus: Law is a system of rules that societies create to solve problems and protect people.

lessons.title: Why Laws Exist: From Playground Rules to Government
lessons.brief: Explores how rules emerge naturally in groups and why societies need formal laws to function fairly.

lessons.title: The Job of Courts: How Disputes Get Settled
lessons.brief: Examines how courts work as neutral spaces where disagreements are heard and decisions are made by judges or juries.

lessons.title: Rights and Responsibilities: What You Can and Cannot Do
lessons.brief: Introduces fundamental rights (safety, freedom, fairness) and how responsibilities balance those rights in a community.

lessons.title: Consequences: How Laws Are Enforced
lessons.brief: Explains why consequences exist, how they're decided, and the difference between civil and criminal penalties.

grade_8.focus: Laws are created by people through government systems, and different societies make different choices about what rules to enforce.

lessons.title: Who Makes Laws: Parliament, Congress, and Power
lessons.brief: Examines how legislatures are structured, how laws are debated and passed, and why representation matters.

lessons.title: When Laws Conflict: Constitutional Limits and Higher Authority
lessons.brief: Explores how constitutions act as a foundation that prevents governments from overstepping, and what happens when laws clash.

lessons.title: Comparing Legal Systems: Why Countries Have Different Laws
lessons.brief: Investigates how cultural values, history, and government type shape what is legal in different places (Common Law, Civil Law, Religious Law systems).

lessons.title: The Case for and Against a Law: Evaluating Arguments
lessons.brief: Develops skills to weigh competing arguments about whether a specific law is fair, effective, or necessary.

grade_9.focus: Laws reflect and enforce society's values, but those values change over time and people disagree about what the law should do.

lessons.title: How Laws Change: Reform, Repeal, and Social Movements
lessons.brief: Traces how laws have been challenged and rewritten through history, examining the role of activism and evidence in legal change.

lessons.title: Whose Values Count: Lawmakers, Citizens, and Minorities
lessons.brief: Analyzes tension between majority rule and minority rights, and how legal systems protect individuals from tyranny of the majority.

lessons.title: Evidence and Expertise in the Law: Science, Statistics, and Testimony
lessons.brief: Examines how courts evaluate evidence, what counts as proof, and the role of experts in legal decisions.

lessons.title: Theories of Justice: Punishment, Rehabilitation, and Fairness
lessons.brief: Compares different philosophies about why we punish crime (retribution, deterrence, rehabilitation) and their real-world outcomes.

grade_10.focus: The legal system operates through interpretation of written rules, precedent, and procedure, and understanding these mechanics reveals how justice is actually delivered.

lessons.title: Reading and Interpreting Statutes: What Does the Law Actually Say?
lessons.brief: Develops skills to parse legal language, identify ambiguities, and understand how judges resolve disputes about what words mean.

lessons.title: Precedent and Case Law: How Past Decisions Shape Present Law
lessons.brief: Explains the doctrine of stare decisis, analyzes landmark cases, and shows how courts build law through reasoning.

lessons.title: Procedural Justice: Rules of the Game in Courts
lessons.brief: Examines due process, burden of proof, rights of the accused, and how procedure affects the fairness of outcomes.

lessons.title: The Constitutional Hierarchy: Balancing Individual Rights and State Power
lessons.brief: Analyzes how constitutions protect rights (free speech, privacy, equality) while allowing government to regulate behavior for public good.

grade_11.focus: Legal systems embody competing theories of justice and social order; examining this conflict reveals how law shapes and is shaped by power, ideology, and choice.

lessons.title: Critiquing Legal Reasoning: Logic, Analogy, and Judicial Choice
lessons.brief: Deconstructs how judges argue, examines whether judicial decisions are determined by law or discretion, and evaluates the strength of legal reasoning.

lessons.title: Law and Inequality: Whose Interests Does the System Serve?
lessons.brief: Applies critical perspectives to examine how law has historically enforced discrimination, and analyzes whether legal reform can address structural inequality.

lessons.title: Comparative Constitutional Design: Rights, Structures, and Trade-offs
lessons.brief: Compares multiple constitutions to identify different approaches to balancing liberty, equality, security, and efficiency.

lessons.title: The Limits of Law: What Law Cannot Do and When It Fails
lessons.brief: Examines enforcement gaps, unintended consequences, and situations where law is ineffective or counterproductive as a tool for social change.

grade_12.focus: Law is a contested field where scholars, policymakers, and advocates use research and argument to defend different visions of justice; students develop their own informed position.

lessons.title: Original Legal Texts: Constitutions, Statutes, and Cases as Historical Documents
lessons.brief: Reads and analyzes primary legal sources to understand how language reflects historical context, power relationships, and competing values.

lessons.title: Legal Theory in Practice: Positivism, Naturalism, and Critical Approaches
lessons.brief: Compares foundational theories about what law *is* and evaluates their explanatory power through case studies and policy analysis.

lessons.title: Research and Evidence in Law: Policy Analysis, Impact Studies, and Advocacy
lessons.brief: Examines how empirical research shapes law, how advocates use evidence strategically, and how to evaluate claims about legal effectiveness.

lessons.title: Designing a Legal Regime: Building a Framework for a Specific Problem
lessons.brief: Applies accumulated knowledge to design law or policy for a novel challenge, justifying choices by reference to competing values and evidence.

grade_1.focus: Stories are about things that happen to people and animals, and we can listen, retell, and act them out.

lessons.title: What Happens in a Story
lessons.brief: Students learn that stories have a beginning, middle, and end by listening to short picture books and sequencing events.

lessons.title: Characters Do Things
lessons.brief: Students identify who is in a story and what they do, using words like happy, sad, silly, and brave.

lessons.title: Telling Stories with Our Voices and Bodies
lessons.brief: Students retell familiar stories through acting, sound effects, and simple dialogue to show what happens.

grade_2.focus: Stories have characters with feelings and faces choices, and we can describe what we see and feel when we read.

lessons.title: Characters Have Feelings and Change
lessons.brief: Students describe how characters feel at different moments in a story and notice when feelings change from start to finish.

lessons.title: The Problem and the Fix
lessons.brief: Students identify a simple problem that happens in a story and notice how the character solves it or what helps them.

lessons.title: Pictures and Words Tell the Story Together
lessons.brief: Students examine how illustrations and text work as a pair to show what is happening and help us understand the mood.

lessons.title: Favorite Parts and Why They Matter
lessons.brief: Students choose a favorite moment in a story and use words to say why they liked it.

grade_3.focus: Stories teach us something through how characters respond to problems, and we can compare stories and their messages.

lessons.title: Cause and Effect in Stories
lessons.brief: Students trace how one action leads to another consequence throughout a story using words like because and so.

lessons.title: Main Idea and Supporting Details
lessons.brief: Students identify the central idea of a story and point to specific moments and descriptions that support it.

lessons.title: Comparing Similar Stories and Characters
lessons.brief: Students read two versions or similar tales and describe what is the same and different about the characters and how they solve problems.

lessons.title: The Lesson a Story Teaches
lessons.brief: Students identify the message or moral of a story and explain how the character's journey shows this lesson.

grade_4.focus: Stories are built from craft choices—setting, dialogue, and plot structure—that work together to create meaning and shape how readers respond.

lessons.title: How Setting Shapes What Happens
lessons.brief: Students analyze how the time and place of a story affect the character's choices, conflicts, and what becomes possible.

lessons.title: What Characters Say Reveals Who They Are
lessons.brief: Students examine dialogue to infer character traits, motivations, and relationships without being told directly.

lessons.title: Plot Structure: Rising Action, Climax, and Resolution
lessons.brief: Students map the turning points and build-up of a story to see how tension grows and leads to a crucial moment.

lessons.title: Theme Across Different Stories
lessons.brief: Students identify a common theme (like courage or friendship) in multiple texts and trace how each story explores it differently.

grade_5.focus: Writers make deliberate choices about tone, perspective, and symbolism to communicate meaning, and readers can analyze why those choices matter.

lessons.title: Point of View and What the Reader Knows
lessons.brief: Students examine how a story told from first person, third person, or multiple perspectives controls information and shapes reader sympathy.

lessons.title: Tone: The Author's Attitude Toward the Story
lessons.brief: Students identify whether a story feels serious, humorous, bitter, or hopeful and trace the word choices and events that create that tone.

lessons.title: Symbols and What They Represent
lessons.brief: Students recognize when objects, colors, or images carry deeper meaning beyond their literal form and connect those meanings to themes.

lessons.title: Why Characters Make Choices: Motivation and Consequence
lessons.brief: Students analyze the internal and external reasons characters act as they do and evaluate whether their choices feel believable and earned.

grade_6.focus: Literature reflects and shapes how we understand ourselves and the world; readers analyze how writers construct meaning through technique and interpret texts within cultural and historical contexts.

lessons.title: Narrative Structure and Unreliable Narrators
lessons.brief: Students examine how a story's structure—flashbacks, multiple timelines, or an untrustworthy narrator—affects meaning and interpretation.

lessons.title: Conflict as Reflection of Larger Ideas
lessons.brief: Students analyze personal, social, and internal conflicts in literature to see how they represent bigger questions about identity, power, and belonging.

lessons.title: Cultural Context and How It Shapes Story
lessons.brief: Students research the historical and cultural background of texts to understand how setting, values, and conflicts reflect the world the author knew.

lessons.title: Text as Argument: What Literature Claims About the World
lessons.brief: Students identify implicit arguments in stories about what is true, right, or possible, and evaluate whether the text supports its own claims.

grade_7.focus: Stories reflect the real world: how authors use literature to explore conflict, identity, and social issues.

lessons.title: Why Authors Write About Real Problems
lessons.brief: Examining how novels and short stories tackle contemporary issues like bullying, inequality, and family conflict through character experience.

lessons.title: Character Decisions and Consequences
lessons.brief: Tracing how a character's choices drive plot forward and reveal their values, motivations, and growth throughout a story.

lessons.title: Perspective Matters: Whose Story Gets Told
lessons.brief: Comparing how the same event changes when told from different character viewpoints, and what that reveals about bias and understanding.

lessons.title: Historical Fiction as a Window to the Past
lessons.brief: Using novels set in historical periods to understand how ordinary people experienced major events and how authors blend fact with imagination.

grade_8.focus: Literature as argument: how authors persuade readers through narrative technique, rhetoric, and deliberate craft choices.

lessons.title: How Tone and Word Choice Shape Meaning
lessons.brief: Analyzing how an author's diction, figurative language, and narrative voice create emotional effect and guide reader interpretation.

lessons.title: Symbolism and Subtext: What Lies Beneath
lessons.brief: Decoding how objects, settings, and recurring motifs carry deeper thematic weight and communicate ideas beyond literal plot.

lessons.title: Rhetorical Devices in Non-Fiction Writing
lessons.brief: Identifying how essayists and journalists use appeals to logic, emotion, and credibility to build arguments and persuade audiences.

lessons.title: Unreliable Narrators and Competing Truths
lessons.brief: Recognizing when a narrator's perspective is limited or deliberately deceptive, and what this technique reveals about truth and storytelling.

grade_9.focus: Literature as cultural mirror: synthesizing how works reflect, challenge, and shape social values across time periods and cultures.

lessons.title: Genre as Cultural Code: What Different Forms Tell Us
lessons.brief: Exploring how genres (tragedy, comedy, romance, satire) embody different worldviews and reveal what a culture values or fears.

lessons.title: Power Structures in Literature: Class, Gender, and Identity
lessons.brief: Examining how literature depicts and critiques social hierarchies, and how marginalized characters challenge or reinforce dominant narratives.

lessons.title: Intertextuality: How Stories Speak to Each Other
lessons.brief: Tracing how authors reference, adapt, or subvert earlier works to add layers of meaning and enter conversations across centuries.

lessons.title: Conflict Between Individual and Society
lessons.brief: Analyzing how canonical and contemporary texts dramatize tensions between personal desire and social expectation, and what each author privileges.

grade_10.focus: Close reading as interpretation: using textual evidence and historical context to construct defensible arguments about authorial intent and literary meaning.

lessons.title: Primary Sources and Literary History: Reading in Context
lessons.brief: Using original documents, author letters, and historical records to understand how context shapes interpretation and authorial choices.

lessons.title: Metaanalysis of Literary Criticism: Competing Interpretations
lessons.brief: Reading and evaluating how different critics interpret the same text, recognizing that meaning-making is contested and evidence-based.

lessons.title: Narrative Structure and Reader Experience
lessons.brief: Analyzing how plot structure, pacing, foreshadowing, and narrative technique actively shape what readers think and feel at each moment.

lessons.title: Modernism and the Breaking of Literary Convention
lessons.brief: Examining how early 20th-century authors deliberately fragmented form, language, and reality to reflect psychological and social upheaval.

grade_11.focus: Literary theory as framework: applying critical lenses (feminist, postcolonial, Marxist, queer) to expose how literature constructs meaning and ideology.

lessons.title: Feminist Critique: Gender, Agency, and the Canon
lessons.brief: Applying feminist theory to analyze how texts represent women, construct masculinity, and how women writers have challenged patriarchal narratives.

lessons.title: Postcolonial Readings: Empire, Voice, and Representation
lessons.brief: Using postcolonial theory to examine how colonized peoples are depicted in canonical literature and how colonized writers reclaim narrative authority.

lessons.title: Marxist Analysis: Class, Labour, and Economic Systems in Text
lessons.brief: Applying Marxist criticism to reveal how literature naturalizes or critiques capitalism, class systems, and material conditions of existence.

lessons.title: Deconstructing Binaries: Race, Sexuality, and Identity Politics
lessons.brief: Using queer theory and critical race theory to destabilize fixed categories in literature and explore how texts construct or subvert identity.

grade_12.focus: Synthesis and independent scholarship: conducting literary research, arguing across multiple texts and theories, and developing a sophisticated personal critical voice.

lessons.title: Research Seminar: Building an Original Literary Argument
lessons.brief: Designing and executing a sustained research project that identifies gaps in existing criticism, stakes an original claim, and supports it with textual and theoretical evidence.

lessons.title: Comparative Analysis: Tracing Themes Across Disciplines and Media
lessons.brief: Analyzing how a theme or question manifests across novels, poetry, drama, film, and other media; evaluating what form reveals about content.

lessons.title: The Politics of Canonicity: What Gets Taught and Why
lessons.brief: Interrogating which texts are canonized, whose voices are excluded, and how institutional power shapes literary reputation and cultural memory.

lessons.title: Contemporary Literature and Global Perspectives
lessons.brief: Reading and critiquing 21st-century works from diverse cultures and traditions; evaluating how contemporary writers engage with legacy, diaspora, and global futures.

grade_1.focus: Numbers and counting are how we describe and compare things we can see and touch.

lessons.title: Counting and Making Groups
lessons.brief: Learning to count objects to 10 and gather them into groups of the same size.

lessons.title: More, Less, and the Same
lessons.brief: Comparing groups of objects to see which has more, less, or if they match.

lessons.title: Shapes All Around Us
lessons.brief: Finding and naming circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles in the classroom and outside.

grade_2.focus: Numbers up to 100 help us measure, order, and combine groups in everyday situations.

lessons.title: Counting to 100 by Ones and Tens
lessons.brief: Recognising patterns when counting by 10s and building two-digit numbers with tens and ones.

lessons.title: Adding and Taking Away
lessons.brief: Combining and removing small groups of objects to solve simple word problems.

lessons.title: Measuring Length and Weight
lessons.brief: Comparing how long and how heavy things are using non-standard units like hands and blocks.

lessons.title: Telling Time to the Hour
lessons.brief: Reading a clock to find out what hour it is and connecting time to daily activities.

grade_3.focus: Place value and basic operations reveal patterns in how numbers work and connect to real quantities.

lessons.title: Hundreds, Tens, and Ones
lessons.brief: Breaking three-digit numbers into parts to understand what each digit represents.

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Within 1000
lessons.brief: Using place value to add and subtract larger numbers with and without regrouping.

lessons.title: Groups of Equal Size and Arrays
lessons.brief: Arranging objects in rows and columns to introduce multiplication as repeated groups.

lessons.title: Measuring Length, Weight, and Capacity
lessons.brief: Using standard units like centimetres, kilograms, and litres to measure and compare objects.

grade_4.focus: Multiplication and division are inverse operations that reveal how quantities scale and relate in systems.

lessons.title: Multiplication Facts and Strategies
lessons.brief: Building fluency with multiplication facts 1–10 using arrays, skip-counting, and properties.

lessons.title: Division as Fair Sharing and Grouping
lessons.brief: Solving division problems by sharing items equally or forming groups of a set size.

lessons.title: Factors, Multiples, and Area
lessons.brief: Finding factor pairs, recognising multiples, and calculating area using multiplication.

lessons.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole
lessons.brief: Dividing shapes and sets into equal parts to understand halves, thirds, and quarters.

grade_5.focus: Fractions, decimals, and operations with larger numbers deepen understanding of how quantities can be represented and manipulated.

lessons.title: Equivalent Fractions and Comparing Size
lessons.brief: Creating and recognising equivalent fractions, then ordering fractions on a number line.

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions with Like Denominators
lessons.brief: Combining and removing fractional parts to solve problems with common denominators.

lessons.title: Decimals as Fractions and Place Value
lessons.brief: Understanding tenths and hundredths, reading decimals, and connecting them to fractions.

lessons.title: Multi-Digit Multiplication and Division
lessons.brief: Applying strategies to multiply and divide with two-digit and three-digit numbers, explaining remainders.

grade_6.focus: Ratios, rates, and proportional reasoning show how quantities relate and change together in connected systems.

lessons.title: Ratios and Equivalent Ratios
lessons.brief: Comparing two quantities using ratio notation and finding equivalent ratios to solve problems.

lessons.title: Unit Rates and Proportional Relationships
lessons.brief: Using unit rates to compare prices and speeds, and recognising when relationships are proportional.

lessons.title: Positive and Negative Numbers on a Number Line
lessons.brief: Extending the number system to include integers and applying them to real contexts like temperature.

lessons.title: Order of Operations and Algebraic Thinking
lessons.brief: Following rules for calculation order and writing expressions with variables to represent patterns and relationships.

grade_7.focus: Extending number systems beyond integers to include fractions, decimals, and negative numbers, and applying these to real-world contexts.

lessons.title: Negative Numbers on a Number Line
lessons.brief: Understanding how negative numbers extend the number system below zero and how to perform operations with positive and negative values.

lessons.title: Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages as Connected Systems
lessons.brief: Exploring the relationships between fractions, decimals, and percentages, and converting fluidly between these representations.

lessons.title: Ratio and Proportion in Real Situations
lessons.brief: Using ratios to compare quantities and applying proportional reasoning to scale, maps, recipes, and other practical problems.

lessons.title: Introduction to Algebraic Thinking with Variables
lessons.brief: Using letters to represent unknown numbers and writing simple equations to model real-world situations.

grade_8.focus: Mastering linear equations and graphs as tools for modeling relationships, and beginning to see algebra as a language for generalizing patterns.

lessons.title: Solving Linear Equations Systematically
lessons.brief: Developing step-by-step methods to isolate variables and solve equations, understanding inverse operations as a strategy.

lessons.title: Graphing Lines and Interpreting Slope
lessons.brief: Plotting points, drawing lines on a coordinate plane, and understanding slope as a rate of change.

lessons.title: Systems of Linear Equations
lessons.brief: Finding where two linear relationships intersect using graphing and algebraic methods, and interpreting solutions in context.

lessons.title: Exponents and Powers as Repeated Multiplication
lessons.brief: Using exponent notation, applying exponent rules (product, quotient, power), and connecting to scientific notation.

grade_9.focus: Expanding algebraic manipulation to quadratic expressions and equations, while connecting algebra to geometric properties and building function concepts.

lessons.title: Factoring and Expanding Quadratic Expressions
lessons.brief: Breaking quadratics into factors and expanding products, recognizing patterns like difference of squares and perfect trinomials.

lessons.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Multiple Methods
lessons.brief: Using factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula to find roots, and interpreting solutions geometrically.

lessons.title: Functions as Mappings and Machines
lessons.brief: Understanding functions as relationships between input and output, using function notation, domain, and range.

lessons.title: Properties of Geometric Shapes and the Pythagorean Theorem
lessons.brief: Proving and applying the Pythagorean theorem, exploring relationships in right triangles, and connecting to distance in coordinate geometry.

grade_10.focus: Developing a comprehensive understanding of functions—polynomial, radical, rational, and exponential—and their applications to modeling real phenomena.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions: Behavior, Roots, and End Patterns
lessons.brief: Analyzing the degree, leading coefficient, and roots of polynomials to sketch curves and predict long-term behavior.

lessons.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions as Inverse Pairs
lessons.brief: Exploring exponential growth and decay, introducing logarithms as inverse operations, and applying to real-world scenarios like compound interest and radioactive decay.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Asymptotic Behavior
lessons.brief: Examining functions with variables in denominators, identifying vertical and horizontal asymptotes, and understanding discontinuities.

lessons.title: Transformations and Composition of Functions
lessons.brief: Understanding how shifts, stretches, and reflections modify function graphs, and combining functions through addition, multiplication, and composition.

grade_11.focus: Analyzing function families through rigorous mathematical arguments, introducing trigonometric functions, and building tools for calculus.

lessons.title: Trigonometric Functions Beyond Right Triangles
lessons.brief: Defining sine, cosine, and tangent on the unit circle, establishing periodicity, and deriving identities that reveal deep structural relationships.

lessons.title: Sequences, Series, and Mathematical Induction
lessons.brief: Analyzing arithmetic and geometric sequences, summing infinite series conditionally, and using induction to prove general statements.

lessons.title: Limits and Instantaneous Rates of Change
lessons.brief: Formalizing the concept of a limit, computing average and instantaneous rates of change, and laying the foundation for derivatives.

lessons.title: Comparing Models: When to Use Which Function Family
lessons.brief: Evaluating real datasets, choosing appropriate function families, justifying choices through regression analysis and error assessment.

grade_12.focus: Mastering differential and integral calculus, and synthesizing mathematics across contexts to solve complex, open-ended problems.

lessons.title: Derivatives as a Framework for Optimization and Motion
