lessons.brief: Students calculate binding energy from mass defect, analyze decay modes using conservation laws, and critically examine the evidence for and risks of nuclear energy.

lessons.title: Waves and Particles: Complementary Models
lessons.brief: Students explore wave-particle duality, interpret double-slit experiments, and debate the measurement problem, developing a personal stance on how to interpret quantum behavior.

grade_12.focus: Physics synthesizes quantum mechanics, relativity, and field theory into a coherent framework, while examining fundamental open questions and the nature of physical knowledge.

lessons.title: Quantum Mechanics from Schrödinger to Superposition
lessons.brief: Students solve and interpret the Schrödinger equation, analyze energy levels in atoms and molecules, and research competing interpretations (Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, pilot-wave) using primary literature.

lessons.title: The Standard Model: Particles, Forces, and Symmetry
lessons.brief: Students map the periodic table of particles and fundamental forces, evaluate evidence from accelerator experiments, and critique the model's successes and unresolved problems.

lessons.title: General Relativity and Curved Spacetime
lessons.brief: Students explore how gravity arises from spacetime curvature, apply the concept to black holes and cosmology, and compare predictions against observational evidence.

lessons.title: Frontiers and Limits: What Physics Cannot (Yet) Explain
lessons.brief: Students synthesize quantum mechanics and gravity, investigate dark matter and dark energy, and conduct a research project on a frontier question, critiquing the evidence and methods.

grade_1.focus: Learning to notice and name feelings and how bodies show them.

lessons.title: What Are Feelings?
lessons.brief: Students learn the four basic feelings—happy, sad, angry, scared—and see them in faces and real situations.

lessons.title: My Body Tells a Story
lessons.brief: Students discover how feelings show up in their bodies: fast heartbeat, tears, smiles, tight muscles.

lessons.title: Other People's Feelings
lessons.brief: Students practice recognizing when someone else is happy, sad, angry, or scared by looking at their face and body.

grade_2.focus: Identifying different feelings, what causes them, and simple ways to calm down.

lessons.title: More Feelings Than Four
lessons.brief: Students learn that feelings come in shades—excited, worried, disappointed, proud—and how they differ from the basic four.

lessons.title: What Happens Before the Feeling?
lessons.brief: Students trace simple cause and effect: what happened, what feeling came next, and why.

lessons.title: Calming Down When Big Feelings Come
lessons.brief: Students learn and practice concrete tools: deep breathing, counting, moving, talking to someone they trust.

lessons.title: Reading Faces and Voices
lessons.brief: Students learn that tone of voice and face expressions help them understand how someone really feels.

grade_3.focus: Categorizing emotions, understanding triggers and responses, and recognizing feelings in yourself and others.

lessons.title: Sorting Feelings Into Groups
lessons.brief: Students sort emotions into categories: pleasant feelings, unpleasant feelings, and learn that all feelings are normal.

lessons.title: What Triggers a Feeling?
lessons.brief: Students identify patterns—events, people, or situations that make them feel certain ways—and see the cause-and-effect chain.

lessons.title: How I Act When I Feel
lessons.brief: Students learn that feelings lead to actions or reactions, and that they have some choice in what they do next.

lessons.title: Spotting Feelings in Stories and Real Life
lessons.brief: Students practice identifying characters' and peers' emotions in books, videos, and classroom moments using vocabulary and clues.

grade_4.focus: Understanding emotions as part of a system: triggers, thoughts, feelings, and behaviors all connected.

lessons.title: The Feeling Chain: Thought → Feeling → Action
lessons.brief: Students map how a thought or event leads to a feeling, which leads to a behavior, and how changing one part can shift the whole chain.

lessons.title: Why Different People Feel Different Ways
lessons.brief: Students explore how personality, past experience, and beliefs affect how someone reacts to the same event.

lessons.title: Managing Emotions Before They Manage You
lessons.brief: Students learn strategies for noticing early warning signs of big emotions and using techniques to stay calm and in control.

lessons.title: Empathy: Feeling With Someone Else
lessons.brief: Students learn what empathy is, practice imagining how someone else feels, and see how it changes how they treat others.

grade_5.focus: Understanding how emotions develop over time, how they function in relationships, and how thinking patterns shape feeling.

lessons.title: How Thoughts Create Feelings
lessons.brief: Students learn that the same event can create different feelings depending on what they think about it, and practice spotting their own thought patterns.

lessons.title: Emotions Across Time: From Moment to Mood to Temperament
lessons.brief: Students distinguish between quick feelings, longer moods, and lasting personality traits, and understand how they build on each other.

lessons.title: Emotions in Relationships: When Feelings Clash
lessons.brief: Students explore how their emotions affect others, how conflict happens when feelings are misunderstood, and how to communicate about feelings.

lessons.title: Resilience: Bouncing Back From Hard Feelings
lessons.brief: Students learn what resilience is, study how people recover from disappointment or failure, and practice building their own resilience habits.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing emotion as a biological and social system; connecting emotion to decision-making, culture, and identity.

lessons.title: The Brain's Role in Emotion: Why We Feel What We Feel
lessons.brief: Students learn how the brain processes emotions, why some feelings are automatic, and how the prefrontal cortex helps them think clearly even when upset.

lessons.title: Culture and Emotion: Why Feeling Rules Differ
lessons.brief: Students analyze how different cultures, families, and social groups teach different rules about which emotions are acceptable and how to express them.

lessons.title: Emotions in Decision-Making: Head vs. Heart
lessons.brief: Students explore how emotions influence choices—both helpfully and harmfully—and practice balancing feeling and thinking in decisions.

lessons.title: Identity and Emotion: How Feelings Shape Who We Are
lessons.brief: Students reflect on how their emotional patterns, values, and responses form part of their identity and affect how they relate to others.

grade_7.focus: Understand how your brain, emotions, and behaviour connect—and why you feel and act the way you do.

lessons.title: Your Brain: The Control Centre
lessons.brief: Explore the main parts of the brain, what they do, and how they influence your thoughts, feelings, and actions.

lessons.title: Emotions: Why We Feel What We Feel
lessons.brief: Investigate where emotions come from, why different situations trigger different feelings, and how to recognise emotions in yourself and others.

lessons.title: Personality and Differences
lessons.brief: Discover why people have different personalities, how early experiences shape who you are, and why no two people are exactly alike.

lessons.title: Stress, Sleep, and Wellbeing
lessons.brief: Learn how stress affects your body and mind, why sleep matters, and practical strategies to stay mentally and physically healthy.

grade_8.focus: Evaluate how social influence, communication, and relationships shape behaviour—and recognise when you're being influenced.

lessons.title: Peer Pressure and Conformity
lessons.brief: Analyse why people conform to group norms, examine real examples of peer pressure, and evaluate the difference between healthy influence and harmful pressure.

lessons.title: Communication: What We Say vs. What We Mean
lessons.brief: Examine verbal and non-verbal communication, interpret mixed messages, and explore how misunderstandings happen and how to prevent them.

lessons.title: Relationships: Friendship and Belonging
lessons.brief: Investigate what makes friendships work, analyse conflict in relationships, and evaluate different approaches to resolving disagreements.

lessons.title: Identity and Self-Esteem
lessons.brief: Explore how identity forms, examine the sources of self-esteem, and evaluate how media and comparison affect how you see yourself.

grade_9.focus: Synthesise psychological theories to explain complex behaviours—and develop your own framework for understanding people.

lessons.title: Motivation: Why People Do What They Do
lessons.brief: Synthesise multiple theories of motivation (biological, psychological, social), apply them to real behaviour, and evaluate which explanations fit different situations best.

lessons.title: Prejudice, Stereotyping, and Bias
lessons.brief: Examine how stereotypes form in the brain, trace the psychological roots of prejudice, and evaluate strategies for reducing implicit bias.

lessons.title: Learning and Memory: How Experience Shapes Us
lessons.brief: Compare classical conditioning, operant conditioning, and observational learning; analyse how memories form and distort; apply learning theory to real situations.

lessons.title: Mental Health: Anxiety, Depression, and Resilience
lessons.brief: Distinguish normal stress from mental health conditions, explore contributing factors (biological, cognitive, environmental), and evaluate evidence-based coping strategies.

grade_10.focus: Interpret original psychological research and nuanced evidence—and recognise the limitations of psychological claims.

lessons.title: Reading and Critiquing Psychological Studies
lessons.brief: Learn to evaluate research design, interpret data, recognise limitations and bias, and question whether conclusions are truly supported by evidence.

lessons.title: Nature vs. Nurture: The Evidence
lessons.brief: Analyse original studies on genetics, environment, and development; evaluate competing explanations; synthesise evidence that most traits result from both.

lessons.title: Cognitive Biases and Decision-Making
lessons.brief: Examine how heuristics, confirmation bias, and other cognitive shortcuts affect judgement; interpret original research on decision errors; apply findings to real choices.

lessons.title: Culture and Psychology: Are Psychological Principles Universal?
lessons.brief: Investigate how culture shapes personality, emotion, and behaviour; critique research conducted only on Western samples; evaluate claims about universal human nature.

grade_11.focus: Critique competing psychological frameworks and construct evidence-based arguments about human behaviour.

lessons.title: Comparing Theoretical Frameworks: Psychoanalytic, Behavioural, Cognitive, and Humanistic Approaches
lessons.brief: Compare how different schools of thought explain the same behaviour, critique their assumptions and evidence, and construct arguments for when each approach is most useful.

lessons.title: Neuroscience and Psychology: The Brain-Behaviour Link
lessons.brief: Examine how neuroscience explains psychology, critique reductionist thinking, and evaluate whether brain-level explanations always replace psychological ones.

lessons.title: Developmental Psychology: Continuity vs. Change Across the Lifespan
lessons.brief: Analyse competing theories of development, compare longitudinal and cross-sectional evidence, and construct your own argument about personality stability and change.

lessons.title: Ethics in Psychological Research and Practice
lessons.brief: Evaluate historical ethical violations, critique current ethical guidelines, and construct arguments about balancing research progress with participant protection.

grade_12.focus: Conduct independent psychological inquiry—synthesise evidence across frameworks, and develop a sophisticated personal perspective on human nature.

lessons.title: Independent Research Project: Designing and Critiquing Your Own Study
lessons.brief: Design an original psychological study, conduct data collection or analysis, interpret results critically, and position your findings within existing literature.

lessons.title: Integrating Psychology with Other Disciplines
lessons.brief: Synthesise psychological insights with neuroscience, sociology, philosophy, and economics; evaluate how interdisciplinary perspectives deepen or complicate psychological claims.

lessons.title: Consciousness, Free Will, and Responsibility
lessons.brief: Engage with philosophical and empirical questions about consciousness, examine evidence on free will, and construct nuanced arguments about moral responsibility and determinism.

lessons.title: Psychology in Society: Applications, Limitations, and Future Directions
lessons.brief: Analyse how psychology shapes education, criminal justice, and mental health systems; critique the use and misuse of psychology; synthesise evidence on emerging frontiers (AI, neurotechnology, global mental health).

grade_1.focus: Learning to recognize letters, sound them out, and read simple words that name things in the world around you.

lessons.title: Letter Sounds and Shapes
lessons.brief: Connecting each letter to the sound it makes and recognizing its shape in words.

lessons.title: Blending Sounds into Words
lessons.brief: Putting letter sounds together to read simple three-letter words like cat, dog, and sit.

lessons.title: Sight Words We See Every Day
lessons.brief: Learning to recognize common words (the, and, is, a) that appear in almost every sentence.

lessons.title: Reading Simple Picture Stories
lessons.brief: Using pictures and sounding-out to read short sentences about familiar things like pets and toys.

grade_2.focus: Reading longer words with blends and patterns, and understanding what simple sentences are telling you.

lessons.title: Consonant Blends and Word Families
lessons.brief: Learning how two consonants blend together (st, bl, cr) and recognizing rhyming word groups.

lessons.title: Short and Long Vowel Sounds
lessons.brief: Distinguishing between short vowel sounds (cat, bed) and long vowel sounds (cake, tree) to read new words.

lessons.title: Naming and Describing in Sentences
lessons.brief: Identifying who or what is doing something in a sentence and what they are doing.

lessons.title: Retelling What Happened in a Story
lessons.brief: Reading a short story and telling back the main events in order.

grade_3.focus: Understanding how stories are organized, recognizing how parts fit together, and learning that words have categories and meanings.

lessons.title: Comparing Characters and Their Choices
lessons.brief: Identifying what characters do differently and noticing how their choices lead to different story outcomes.

lessons.title: Cause and Effect: Why Things Happen
lessons.brief: Following the chain of events in a story to see what makes something happen and what happens as a result.

lessons.title: Sorting Words into Categories
lessons.brief: Grouping words by what they mean—animals, colors, actions—and using these categories to understand new words.

lessons.title: Main Idea and Supporting Details
lessons.brief: Finding the big idea of a passage and noticing which sentences give examples or proof of that idea.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how stories and texts are built from smaller parts working together, and recognizing the techniques authors use to communicate.

lessons.title: How Plot, Setting, and Character Work Together
lessons.brief: Analyzing how where a story takes place and who the characters are directly shape what happens in the plot.

lessons.title: Inferencing: Reading Between the Lines
lessons.brief: Using clues from the text along with what you already know to figure out what the author doesn't directly say.

lessons.title: Author's Word Choices and Tone
lessons.brief: Noticing how specific words and descriptions create different moods and feelings in a text.

lessons.title: Fact vs. Opinion in Non-Fiction
lessons.brief: Distinguishing between statements that can be proven and statements that show what someone believes or prefers.

grade_5.focus: Tracing how complex ideas develop through a text, understanding different perspectives, and analyzing why authors make specific choices.

lessons.title: How Themes Develop Across a Whole Story
lessons.brief: Following a big idea or message through a book by tracking how characters change and what they learn.

lessons.title: Multiple Perspectives: Whose Story Is This?
lessons.brief: Recognizing that different characters in a story have different viewpoints and how this shapes what we understand.

lessons.title: Sequence, Flashback, and Time Jumps
lessons.brief: Understanding how authors organize events out of order and how to track when things happen to follow the full story.

lessons.title: Evidence and Explanation in Informational Text
lessons.brief: Identifying what facts and examples an author uses to explain an idea, and evaluating whether they support the main point.

grade_6.focus: Critically analyzing how authors construct meaning through narrative and rhetorical techniques, and synthesizing ideas across multiple texts and disciplines.

lessons.title: Symbolism and Metaphor: Deeper Layers of Meaning
lessons.brief: Interpreting how objects, actions, and language represent bigger ideas and how authors use these techniques intentionally.

lessons.title: Credibility and Bias in Sources
lessons.brief: Evaluating whether a non-fiction source is reliable by examining the author's expertise, purpose, and what perspectives might be missing.

lessons.title: How Conflict Reveals Character and Theme
lessons.brief: Analyzing how the struggles characters face expose their values and drive the central ideas of a story forward.

lessons.title: Connecting Ideas Across Texts and Disciplines
lessons.brief: Using multiple sources from different subjects and genres to build a deeper understanding of a complex topic or question.

grade_7.focus: Reading texts for multiple layers of meaning: plot, character motivation, and author's message.

lessons.title: Finding the Author's Argument in Fiction
lessons.brief: Learning to identify what an author is trying to say about the world through story choices, character arcs, and conflict.

lessons.title: Unreliable Narrators and Hidden Truths
lessons.brief: Recognizing when a narrator cannot be fully trusted and what readers must infer beyond what they're told.

lessons.title: Historical Context and What Stories Reveal
lessons.brief: Using knowledge of when and where a story was written to understand what themes and conflicts mattered to the author.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating how writers construct arguments in both fiction and non-fiction, and recognizing bias and perspective.

lessons.title: Persuasion Tactics: Spotting Logos, Pathos, and Ethos
lessons.brief: Analyzing how writers appeal to reason, emotion, and credibility to convince readers, and how these tactics can manipulate.

lessons.title: Bias, Perspective, and What Gets Left Out
lessons.brief: Examining how a writer's background and beliefs shape what they choose to include or exclude, and whose voices are missing.

lessons.title: Comparing Versions of the Same Event
lessons.brief: Reading multiple accounts of one historical or current event to see how different sources present facts differently based on perspective.

lessons.title: Fact vs. Opinion in Mixed-Genre Texts
lessons.brief: Learning to distinguish verifiable claims from interpretations in texts that blend journalism, memoir, and analysis.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing ideas across multiple texts and recognizing how genre, structure, and literary devices shape meaning and argument.

lessons.title: How Genre Shapes What a Story Can Say
lessons.brief: Analyzing how choosing to write as science fiction, realism, poetry, or essay fundamentally changes what themes and arguments are possible.

lessons.title: Structure as Argument: Why Authors Arrange Ideas This Way
lessons.brief: Examining how the order, pacing, and organization of a text (flashback, parallel narratives, climax placement) creates meaning and persuasion.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Competing Ideas Across Texts
lessons.brief: Reading multiple texts with conflicting views on the same topic and developing a reasoned position by weighing evidence and logic.

lessons.title: Tone, Word Choice, and What They Reveal About the Author's Stance
lessons.brief: Close reading of language to infer the author's attitude, values, and assumptions about their audience and subject.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting primary and secondary sources critically, analyzing rhetorical strategies in depth, and recognizing how historical texts were shaped by their moment.

lessons.title: Reading Primary Sources: Context, Audience, and Intention
lessons.brief: Analyzing original documents (letters, speeches, newspapers, laws) by identifying who wrote them, for whom, and what they hoped to accomplish.

lessons.title: Rhetorical Devices and Their Effect on Credibility
lessons.brief: Studying metaphor, repetition, parallelism, irony, and other devices to understand how they strengthen or weaken an argument's persuasiveness.

lessons.title: Secondary Sources: Evaluating Interpretation and Evidence
lessons.brief: Assessing how historians and scholars use primary sources to build arguments, and recognizing when interpretations are well-supported or overreaching.

lessons.title: Power, Language, and Representation in Classic Texts
lessons.brief: Examining how canonical literature reflects and reinforces (or challenges) the beliefs and hierarchies of its time, and how modern readers can acknowledge this.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing intellectual frameworks, comparing competing interpretations of texts and history, and constructing independent arguments grounded in textual evidence.

lessons.title: Deconstructing Critical Readings: Whose Lens Are We Using?
lessons.brief: Evaluating literary criticism and historical interpretation through different frameworks (feminist, Marxist, post-colonial, etc.) and recognizing their insights and limits.

lessons.title: The Politics of Canon: Why Some Texts Matter and Others Don't
lessons.brief: Investigating why certain works are taught and celebrated while others are excluded, and how literary value is tied to power and culture.

lessons.title: Building an Argument: Evidence, Counterargument, and Revision
lessons.brief: Crafting multi-layered written arguments about texts that anticipate objections, revise initial claims, and distinguish between strong and weak evidence.

lessons.title: Comparing Intellectual Frameworks Across Texts and Disciplines
lessons.brief: Reading across genres and subjects (philosophy, science, history, literature) to identify shared ideas and conflicting worldviews.

grade_12.focus: Conducting independent textual research, synthesizing scholarship, and making original contributions to literary and historical interpretation.

lessons.title: Research Design: Asking Questions and Finding Sources
lessons.brief: Developing a focused research question about a text or historical topic, locating primary and secondary sources, and evaluating source reliability and relevance.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Competing Scholarly Arguments
lessons.brief: Reading multiple academic interpretations of the same text or event, mapping their disagreements, and building a reasoned position that engages all sides.

lessons.title: Making an Original Argument with Textual Evidence
lessons.brief: Writing sustained analytical essays that offer new insights about texts, supported by careful close reading and acknowledgment of alternative readings.

lessons.title: How Power, History, and Interpretation Shape What We Read
lessons.brief: Examining the relationship between a text's creation, its reception across time, and how changing contexts alter meaning and relevance.

grade_1.focus: Learning who is in my life and how I can show care for people close to me.

lessons.title: People in My Life
lessons.brief: Identifying family members, friends, and teachers, and learning their names and roles.

lessons.title: Showing Care and Kindness
lessons.brief: Simple ways to be kind: smiling, sharing, helping, and listening to others.

lessons.title: My Feelings and Others' Feelings
lessons.brief: Recognizing happy, sad, angry, and scared feelings in yourself and noticing them in others' faces.

grade_2.focus: Understanding how people in my life are different from each other and why we need different kinds of friends.

lessons.title: Different People, Different Families
lessons.brief: Exploring how families look different—different sizes, structures, and ways of living.

lessons.title: What Makes a Good Friend
lessons.brief: Identifying qualities of good friends: being honest, sharing, helping, and listening.

lessons.title: When Friends Disagree
lessons.brief: Learning that disagreements happen and practicing simple ways to solve them without hurting feelings.

lessons.title: Helpers in My Community
lessons.brief: Meeting people who help us: teachers, doctors, shopkeepers, mail carriers, and what they do.

grade_3.focus: Recognizing how my choices affect others and how relationships work both ways—give and take.

lessons.title: How My Actions Affect Others
lessons.brief: Connecting cause and effect: what happens when you are kind, unkind, helpful, or hurtful to someone else.

lessons.title: Respect and Boundaries
lessons.brief: Understanding that everyone has personal space and things that are private; learning to ask permission.

lessons.title: Making and Keeping Friendships
lessons.brief: Exploring how friendships grow through spending time together, cooperating, and working through problems.

lessons.title: Cooperation in Groups
lessons.brief: Learning that teams and groups work better when people listen, share ideas, and take turns.

grade_4.focus: Understanding relationships as systems where communication, trust, and roles work together.

lessons.title: How Communication Works
lessons.brief: Examining how words, tone, and body language send messages; what happens when communication breaks down.

lessons.title: Trust and Loyalty in Friendships
lessons.brief: Exploring how trust is built through reliability and honesty, and how it can be damaged.

lessons.title: Roles and Responsibilities
lessons.brief: Identifying different roles people play in families, schools, and groups, and the responsibilities that come with them.

lessons.title: Handling Conflict Fairly
lessons.brief: Learning structured approaches to resolving disagreements: listening, explaining, compromising, and seeking adult help when needed.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how relationships develop through stages and examining the deeper factors that strengthen or weaken connections.

lessons.title: The Stages of Friendship
lessons.brief: Tracing how friendships begin, deepen, and sometimes change; understanding that relationships follow patterns.

lessons.title: Empathy and Perspective-Taking
lessons.brief: Learning to understand others' viewpoints and emotions; practicing how empathy changes the way you respond to conflicts.

lessons.title: Peer Pressure and Decision-Making
lessons.brief: Examining how friends influence choices; learning to recognize pressure and make decisions that align with your own values.

lessons.title: Digital Communication and Relationships
lessons.brief: Understanding how texting, social media, and online interactions affect friendships; discussing tone, misunderstanding, and digital citizenship.

grade_6.focus: Critiquing relationship patterns across contexts and examining how social identity, power, and cultural values shape connections.

lessons.title: Identity and Belonging
lessons.brief: Exploring how identity (interests, background, values) influences which groups and people you connect with and how you fit in.

lessons.title: Power Dynamics in Relationships
lessons.brief: Analyzing how power imbalances—bullying, cliques, exclusion—affect relationships and community; examining fairness and respect.

lessons.title: Cultural and Social Influences on Relationships
lessons.brief: Investigating how culture, family background, and social norms shape expectations in friendships, dating, and family roles.

lessons.title: Healthy vs. Unhealthy Relationships
lessons.brief: Recognizing warning signs of unhealthy relationships (manipulation, disrespect, control) and understanding what healthy support looks like.

grade_7.focus: Recognizing different types of relationships and what healthy boundaries look like in each context.

lessons.title: Mapping Your Relationship Circles
lessons.brief: Students identify the different people in their lives (family, friends, mentors, acquaintances) and understand how relationships vary by closeness and role.

lessons.title: What Healthy Boundaries Sound Like
lessons.brief: Students learn to recognize and practice setting basic personal boundaries through real scenarios and dialogue.

lessons.title: Respect, Trust, and Honesty Across Relationships
lessons.brief: Students explore how respect, trust, and honesty show up differently in family, friendship, and school relationships.

lessons.title: When Relationships Feel Uncomfortable
lessons.brief: Students learn to identify red flags in relationships and when to ask for help from trusted adults.

grade_8.focus: Analyzing how power, communication, and conflict shape relationships, and evaluating what makes relationships fair.

lessons.title: Power Dynamics in Relationships
lessons.brief: Students examine how differences in age, status, or authority create power imbalances and affect how people interact.

lessons.title: Arguing Without Damaging the Relationship
lessons.brief: Students learn conflict resolution strategies and evaluate different approaches to disagreement across various relationships.

lessons.title: Digital Communication and Misunderstanding
lessons.brief: Students analyze how texting, social media, and online platforms change relationship dynamics and create opportunities for miscommunication.

lessons.title: Fairness in Friendship: Reciprocity and Imbalance
lessons.brief: Students evaluate whether their friendships feel balanced and learn how to recognize one-sided relationships.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing patterns across relationships to develop a personal framework for what healthy relationships require and what unhealthy ones look like.

lessons.title: The Cycle of Healthy and Unhealthy Relationship Patterns
lessons.brief: Students trace patterns across multiple relationships to identify recurring healthy and unhealthy dynamics, and connect these to their own experiences.

lessons.title: Consent and Autonomy Across Different Relationships
lessons.brief: Students examine consent beyond romantic contexts—in friendships, family, and peer groups—and how respecting autonomy builds trust.

lessons.title: Peer Pressure, Influence, and Staying True to Yourself
lessons.brief: Students analyze how different relationships influence their choices and develop strategies for maintaining their values when facing pressure.

lessons.title: Romantic Relationships: Expectations vs. Reality
lessons.brief: Students examine cultural narratives about romantic relationships and evaluate what they actually need in a healthy partnership.

grade_10.focus: Reading relationship dynamics through historical and contemporary texts, interpreting how social structures and inequality shape what relationships can be.

lessons.title: How History Shaped What Relationships Are 'Supposed' to Look Like
lessons.brief: Students analyze primary and secondary sources to understand how gender, class, and cultural norms have historically defined family, friendship, and marriage.

lessons.title: Intersectionality in Relationships: Race, Class, Gender, and Identity
lessons.brief: Students examine how multiple aspects of identity affect relationship experiences and interpret texts that illustrate these intersections.

lessons.title: Dependency, Independence, and Interdependence
lessons.brief: Students evaluate different models of emotional and financial interdependence and analyze how culture shapes expectations for self-sufficiency.

lessons.title: Recognizing Abuse: Patterns, Justifications, and Myths
lessons.brief: Students read case studies and expert sources to identify controlling and abusive behaviors, and understand why victims stay or struggle to leave.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing frameworks for relationships from psychology, sociology, and philosophy, and constructing evidence-based arguments about what relationships require.

lessons.title: Attachment Theory vs. Independence Models: Which Framework Fits?
lessons.brief: Students compare psychological theories of attachment and autonomy, evaluate their evidence, and critique their cultural assumptions.

lessons.title: Comparing Cultural Models of Family and Kinship
lessons.brief: Students analyze how different cultures define family, marriage, and obligation, and critique Western individualistic assumptions about relationships.

lessons.title: Power, Vulnerability, and Trust: Philosophical Tensions
lessons.brief: Students engage with philosophical texts on vulnerability, mutual aid, and power to analyze what conditions allow genuine trust to develop.

lessons.title: Systemic Barriers to Healthy Relationships
lessons.brief: Students research and argue how economic inequality, discrimination, and institutional structures constrain relationship choices and well-being.

grade_12.focus: Conducting original analysis of relationship dynamics using evidence from psychology, sociology, history, and personal research, and developing sophisticated arguments about equity and flourishing.

lessons.title: Researching Relationship Outcomes: What the Data Actually Shows
lessons.brief: Students conduct a critical review of empirical research on relationship satisfaction, longevity, and well-being, and evaluate methodological limitations.

lessons.title: Economics of Care: How Financial Systems Shape Intimate Relationships
lessons.brief: Students synthesize research on gender, labor, childcare, and interdependence to argue how economic structures enable or constrain relational choices.

lessons.title: Building a Personal Ethics of Relationships
lessons.brief: Students develop their own framework for relational ethics by synthesizing ideas from philosophy, psychology, and their own evidence-based reasoning.

lessons.title: Relationships in Crisis: Designing Support Systems
lessons.brief: Students research real relationship crises (abuse, addiction, grief, conflict) and design or critique existing support systems using evidence and ethical principles.

grade_1.focus: Learning to look carefully at things around you and notice what you see, hear, and feel.

lessons.title: My Five Senses Hunt
lessons.brief: Using eyes, ears, nose, mouth, and hands to explore and describe real objects in the classroom.

lessons.title: What Happens When I Do This?
lessons.brief: Noticing simple cause and effect by doing actions and watching what occurs (dropping things, mixing water and paint, moving toys).

lessons.title: Sorting Things Into Groups
lessons.brief: Putting objects into piles by one rule at a time (color, size, shape, what they feel like).

lessons.title: Drawing What I Saw
lessons.brief: Creating simple pictures and labels to remember and share what was observed.

grade_2.focus: Describing things carefully and naming the parts that make them work.

lessons.title: Parts and What They Do
lessons.brief: Learning that objects have pieces (wheels, handles, buttons) and finding out what each part does.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Things Side by Side
lessons.brief: Finding ways things are the same and different by looking at size, color, texture, weight, and how they work.

lessons.title: Following a Simple Recipe
lessons.brief: Doing steps in order to make or build something, noticing how mixing or combining things changes what happens.

lessons.title: Making a Picture Record
lessons.brief: Using drawings, words, and simple charts to show what was found out.

grade_3.focus: Organizing observations into groups and understanding how things connect in simple ways.

lessons.title: Sorting by More Than One Rule
lessons.brief: Classifying objects using two or three properties at the same time (things that are red AND round AND hard).

lessons.title: Cause and Effect Chains
lessons.brief: Understanding that one action can make something happen, which then causes something else to happen.

lessons.title: Pattern Spotting in Nature and Numbers
lessons.brief: Finding repeating sequences in leaves, weather, numbers, and daily routines.

lessons.title: Making a Simple Data Chart
lessons.brief: Collecting information about real questions (favorite colors, types of shoes) and showing results in tally marks or picture graphs.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how parts work together as a system and asking simple research questions.

lessons.title: Systems and How Parts Connect
lessons.brief: Seeing that objects and living things have many parts that work together for a purpose (a bicycle, a plant, a classroom).

lessons.title: Asking and Testing a Fair Question
lessons.brief: Forming a testable 'what if' question, changing only one thing, and keeping everything else the same.

lessons.title: Variables: The Things That Can Change
lessons.brief: Identifying what can be measured or changed in an experiment (temperature, light, amount of water) and what stays the same.

lessons.title: Reading and Building Data Tables
lessons.brief: Organizing information in rows and columns, making bar graphs, and spotting trends in the data.

grade_5.focus: Planning real investigations, explaining why things happen, and using data to support claims.

lessons.title: From Question to Hypothesis to Test
lessons.brief: Writing a prediction based on what you already know, then designing steps to test if it is true.

lessons.title: Controlling Variables in Experiments
lessons.brief: Understanding the difference between independent, dependent, and control variables, and why keeping some things steady matters.

lessons.title: Evidence and Explanation
lessons.brief: Using data and observations to explain why something happened, and learning the difference between a fact and an opinion.

lessons.title: Representing Data in Multiple Ways
lessons.brief: Converting information into tables, bar graphs, line graphs, and diagrams to find patterns and tell a story with numbers.

grade_6.focus: Designing multi-step investigations, analyzing sources of error, and connecting findings to larger ideas.

lessons.title: Reliability and Repeating Experiments
lessons.brief: Running tests multiple times to reduce error, calculating averages, and explaining why repeated trials make findings stronger.

lessons.title: Sources of Error and How to Minimize Them
lessons.brief: Identifying mistakes in measurement, procedure, or equipment, and designing controls to make investigations more trustworthy.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Data and Drawing Conclusions
lessons.brief: Combining information from multiple tests, comparing results to predictions, and writing supported conclusions.

lessons.title: Connecting Investigation Findings to Bigger Concepts
lessons.brief: Relating experimental results to scientific principles and real-world applications beyond the lab or classroom.

grade_7.focus: Learning how to ask good questions and find reliable information to answer them.

lessons.title: Questions That Matter: From Curiosity to Researchable Questions
lessons.brief: Students learn to transform everyday curiosity into focused, answerable research questions and distinguish between fact-seeking and opinion questions.

lessons.title: Sources Aren't All Equal: Evaluating Where Information Comes From
lessons.brief: Students explore different types of sources (books, websites, interviews, news) and develop criteria for judging whether a source is trustworthy.

lessons.title: Finding Your Way: Basic Research Strategies in Libraries and Online
lessons.brief: Students learn practical techniques for locating relevant information, including keyword searching, using databases, and navigating library systems.

lessons.title: Giving Credit: Why and How to Record Your Sources
lessons.brief: Students understand plagiarism, learn basic citation formats, and practice documenting where information came from.

grade_8.focus: Analyzing arguments and evidence to understand why people believe different things about the same topic.

lessons.title: Claims, Evidence, and Reasoning: The Building Blocks of Arguments
lessons.brief: Students identify how arguments are constructed and learn to distinguish between claims, the evidence that supports them, and the logic connecting them.

lessons.title: Bias in Information: Recognizing Perspective Without Dismissing Sources
lessons.brief: Students explore how sources reflect different perspectives and interests, and learn to account for bias while still extracting useful information.

lessons.title: Both Sides of the Story: Mapping Competing Arguments on One Issue
lessons.brief: Students research a contentious topic, map out opposing viewpoints fairly, and identify where disagreements actually originate.

lessons.title: Weak Evidence, Strong Evidence: Judging the Quality of Support
lessons.brief: Students learn to evaluate whether evidence is sufficient, relevant, and credible, and practice distinguishing anecdotes from systematic data.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing multiple sources and perspectives into a coherent understanding while recognizing complexity and limitations.

lessons.title: From Many Sources to One Argument: Synthesizing Conflicting Information
lessons.brief: Students learn to combine insights from multiple sources that disagree, identify genuine tensions versus misunderstandings, and build their own informed position.

lessons.title: Context Matters: How Historical and Social Background Shapes Research
lessons.brief: Students examine how the time period, culture, and circumstances in which research was conducted influence its findings and interpretation.

lessons.title: The Limits of What We Know: Uncertainty, Gaps, and Research Frontiers
lessons.brief: Students identify what remains unknown or contested in their research area and understand why experts disagree even when using rigorous methods.

lessons.title: Building Your Framework: Creating a Personal Research Lens
lessons.brief: Students reflect on their own assumptions and values, articulate how these shape what questions they ask, and begin developing their analytical framework.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting primary sources and original documents to construct knowledge while managing their own interpretive assumptions.

lessons.title: Reading Between the Lines: Analyzing Primary Sources and Original Documents
lessons.brief: Students learn to interrogate primary sources by examining authorship, audience, purpose, context, and what the source reveals both intentionally and unintentionally.

lessons.title: Comparing How Historians and Researchers Tell Different Stories from the Same Evidence
lessons.brief: Students examine how different scholars interpret identical primary sources differently, and practice evaluating competing interpretations against evidence.

lessons.title: What's Missing? Identifying Gaps, Silences, and Excluded Perspectives in Research
lessons.brief: Students learn to recognize what voices and viewpoints are absent from historical and contemporary research, and how this absence shapes conclusions.

lessons.title: Constructing Claims from Evidence: Moving from Observation to Argument
lessons.brief: Students practice building logical arguments directly from primary source evidence, learning when inference is justified and when claims overreach.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing research frameworks and methodologies while developing independent analytical positions on complex topics.

lessons.title: Methodology Matters: How Research Methods Shape What We Discover
lessons.brief: Students examine different research approaches (quantitative, qualitative, experimental, interpretive) and analyze how methodology constrains and enables different kinds of findings.

lessons.title: Comparing Frameworks: When Disciplines Approach the Same Question Differently
lessons.brief: Students explore how historians, scientists, economists, and social scientists apply different analytical lenses to shared phenomena and evaluate the strengths and limitations of each.

lessons.title: Power, Knowledge, and Critique: Questioning Who Gets to Claim Authority
lessons.brief: Students examine whose research is valued, funded, and believed, and learn to critique whose perspectives are centered or marginalized in established knowledge.

lessons.title: Developing Your Argument: Staking a Position on a Contested Issue
lessons.brief: Students construct original, evidence-based arguments on a complex topic, articulating their position relative to existing scholarship and acknowledging counterarguments.

grade_12.focus: Conducting original research and synthesizing across disciplines to make independent contributions to knowledge while situating work within scholarly conversation.

lessons.title: Designing a Research Project: From Question to Method to Feasibility
lessons.brief: Students learn to develop a research question, justify a methodological approach, anticipate limitations, and plan a realistic investigation.

lessons.title: Conducting Systematic Inquiry: Collecting, Organizing, and Analyzing Data Ethically
lessons.brief: Students practice gathering primary or secondary data, apply appropriate analytical techniques, and maintain ethical standards throughout the research process.

lessons.title: Positioning Your Work: Locating Your Research Within Existing Scholarship
lessons.brief: Students situate their findings within broader conversations, demonstrate how their work extends, challenges, or complicates existing knowledge.

lessons.title: From Research to Argument: Writing and Presenting Findings for Academic Audiences
lessons.brief: Students learn to communicate research clearly and persuasively to scholarly audiences, using appropriate conventions and acknowledging limitations and future questions.

grade_1.focus: Learning to hold a needle and thread, and making simple stitches by hand.

lessons.title: Threading a Needle
lessons.brief: How to put thread through a needle and tie a knot at the end.

lessons.title: The Running Stitch
lessons.brief: Making a simple up-and-down stitch to join two pieces of fabric together.

lessons.title: Sewing a Felt Bookmark
lessons.brief: Creating your first sewn project by stitching two pieces of felt and adding decorations.

grade_2.focus: Building hand-sewing skills and learning different stitch types for different purposes.

lessons.title: The Backstitch and Why It Holds Better
lessons.brief: Learning a stronger stitch that goes backwards and forwards to keep seams from splitting.

lessons.title: Sewing Straight Lines and Corners
lessons.brief: Practicing how to keep stitches even and how to turn corners neatly.

lessons.title: Making a Stuffed Fabric Square
lessons.brief: Sewing two squares together, leaving an opening, stuffing it with fibres, and closing it up.

lessons.title: Buttons and Simple Repairs
lessons.brief: Sewing a button onto fabric and learning how to fix a small hole.

grade_3.focus: Understanding how different stitches work and choosing the right one for different fabrics and projects.

lessons.title: Three Stitches, Three Jobs: Running, Back, and Whip
lessons.brief: Comparing how running stitches, backstitches, and whip stitches look different and work better for different tasks.

lessons.title: How Fabric Type Changes Your Sewing
lessons.brief: Exploring why thick felt sews differently than thin cotton, and how to adjust your stitch.

lessons.title: Seams and Edges: Keeping Fabric From Fraying
lessons.brief: Learning what a seam is and how finishing an edge stops fabric from coming apart.

lessons.title: Sewing a Simple Drawstring Bag
lessons.brief: Creating a functional project that uses running stitches, corners, and a drawstring opening.

grade_4.focus: Introducing the sewing machine and understanding how hand and machine sewing work as systems.

lessons.title: How a Sewing Machine Works: Needle, Thread, and Tension
lessons.brief: Learning what each part of a sewing machine does and how the needle and bobbin thread lock together.

lessons.title: Machine Stitching vs. Hand Stitching: Speed, Strength, and When to Use Each
lessons.brief: Comparing the advantages and disadvantages of hand stitches and machine stitches for different fabrics and projects.

lessons.title: Reading and Following a Simple Pattern
lessons.brief: Understanding pattern pieces, grain lines, and how to lay out a pattern on fabric before cutting.

lessons.title: Sewing a Lined Pouch Using a Machine
lessons.brief: Creating a two-layer project on a sewing machine with a turning opening and topstitched edge.

grade_5.focus: Mastering pattern reading and understanding how construction techniques affect durability and appearance.

lessons.title: Seam Finishes: Why We Bind, Overcast, and French Seam
lessons.brief: Exploring different methods of finishing raw edges to prevent fraying and create professional-looking seams.

lessons.title: Darts and Curves: How Shaping Changes Fit
lessons.brief: Understanding how darts remove fabric to create contours and how to sew curves smoothly on a machine.

lessons.title: Closures: Zippers, Snaps, and Hooks and Eyes
lessons.brief: Learning how different fastening systems work and when to choose each one based on the project.

lessons.title: Constructing a Simple Skirt or Shirt
lessons.brief: Completing a multi-step garment project that incorporates pattern pieces, seams, hems, and closures.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how design choices, materials, and construction methods work together to create function and quality in sewn items.

lessons.title: Fabric Properties and How They Affect Construction Choices
lessons.brief: Examining how weight, drape, stretch, and weave type influence stitch selection, seam finish, and pattern layout.

lessons.title: The Engineering of Garment Construction: Support, Movement, and Durability
lessons.brief: Investigating how reinforcement techniques, seam placement, and fabric grain work together to make clothing that lasts.

lessons.title: From Sketch to Garment: Modifying Patterns and Troubleshooting Fit
lessons.brief: Learning how to analyze a fit problem, make intentional pattern adjustments, and understand the consequences of design choices.

lessons.title: Designing and Sewing a Personalized Project from Concept
lessons.brief: Planning, selecting materials, adapting or drafting a pattern, and executing a garment or item that reflects individual design thinking.

grade_7.focus: Master fundamental hand-sewing techniques and learn how clothing construction has shaped human history and culture.

lessons.title: Essential Hand Stitches and Their History
lessons.brief: Learn running stitch, backstitch, and whip stitch while exploring how different cultures developed signature stitching patterns for survival and identity.

lessons.title: From Fiber to Fabric: How Cloth Was Made
lessons.brief: Trace the journey of natural fibers into wearable fabric, examining spinning, weaving, and dyeing practices across ancient civilizations.

lessons.title: Constructing Your First Garment: A Simple Drawstring Bag
lessons.brief: Apply hand stitches to create a functional drawstring bag while learning basic pattern layout and seam finishing.

lessons.title: Clothing as Culture: What Your Clothes Tell Your Story
lessons.brief: Investigate how garments reflect social status, geography, and time period, and design a simple piece inspired by a culture different from your own.

grade_8.focus: Develop precision with machine sewing and critically examine how fashion systems affect people and the environment.

lessons.title: Threading, Tension, and Troubleshooting a Sewing Machine
lessons.brief: Master sewing machine mechanics including threading, tension adjustment, and diagnosing common problems like skipped stitches and thread breakage.

lessons.title: Pattern Reading and Fabric Selection: Making Informed Choices
lessons.brief: Learn to read commercial patterns, interpret grain lines, and select appropriate fabrics for different projects while evaluating cost and sustainability.

lessons.title: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion: Labor, Waste, and Ethics
lessons.brief: Investigate garment industry practices, worker conditions, and environmental impact, then argue for or against sustainable alternatives to conventional manufacturing.

lessons.title: Sewing Your First Fitted Garment: Elastic Waistband Pants
lessons.brief: Apply machine-sewing skills to construct a wearable garment with curved seams, elastic insertion, and hem finishing.

grade_9.focus: Integrate advanced techniques with historical textile traditions and develop a personal sewing philosophy grounded in evidence.

lessons.title: Seam Finishes, Hems, and Professional Details
lessons.brief: Master binding seams, French seams, hand-stitched hems, and facings to elevate garment construction quality and durability.

lessons.title: Deconstructing Garments: Reverse Engineering Design
lessons.brief: Analyze existing garments by taking them apart to understand construction logic, then apply these principles to modify or create your own design.

lessons.title: Textile Traditions Across Continents: Indigo, Batik, and Embroidery
lessons.brief: Study historical dyeing and decorative techniques from Asia, Africa, and the Americas, then synthesize these methods with your own creative practice.

lessons.title: Designing Inclusive Clothing: Fitting Bodies Beyond Standard Sizes
lessons.brief: Examine how pattern grading works, explore bias in standard sizing, and create adaptations that accommodate diverse body types and abilities.

grade_10.focus: Critically interpret sewing as a technology and social practice, and apply nuanced design thinking to solve real problems through clothing.

lessons.title: Pattern Drafting from Measurements: Sloper Development and Adaptation
lessons.brief: Draft a basic bodice and pant sloper from body measurements, understand dartwork, and use it as a foundation for custom-fit garment design.

lessons.title: Reading Primary Sources: Fashion Magazines, Patents, and Archival Textiles
lessons.brief: Examine original sewing patterns, fashion plates, and technical drawings from different eras to understand how design reflects technology, values, and constraints of each period.

lessons.title: The Politics of Appearance: Fashion, Gender, and Resistance
lessons.brief: Analyze how clothing has been used to enforce, challenge, or subvert social norms, and create a garment that makes a deliberate statement about identity or values.

lessons.title: Zero-Waste and Circular Design: Minimum Input, Maximum Output
lessons.brief: Study zero-waste pattern engineering and upcycling techniques, then design and construct a complete garment using minimal or reclaimed materials.

grade_11.focus: Critique competing frameworks of sewing practice—craft versus industry, tradition versus innovation, individual versus collective—and develop an independent design philosophy.

lessons.title: Couture Versus Ready-to-Wear: Competing Models of Production and Value
lessons.brief: Compare artisanal hand-crafted and industrial mass-production models across historical and contemporary examples, critiquing assumptions about quality, authenticity, and worth.

lessons.title: Adaptive and Assistive Garment Design: Sewing Beyond Able Bodies
lessons.brief: Research adaptive clothing for disabled and neurodivergent people, examine how commercial design often fails marginalized bodies, and develop a prototype addressing a specific need.

lessons.title: Cultural Appropriation and Respectful Innovation in Textiles
lessons.brief: Analyze contested examples of designers borrowing from non-Western traditions, evaluate different ethical frameworks, and construct an argument for responsible creative practice.

lessons.title: Developing Your Design Thesis: From Concept to Finished Collection
lessons.brief: Create a cohesive 3–5 piece collection grounded in a personal statement about what sewing means to you and what problem it solves.

grade_12.focus: Conduct original research on sewing as a technology, art form, and social practice, and contribute to scholarly or creative conversation about fashion futures.

lessons.title: Research Seminar: Textile Innovation and Digital Fabrication
lessons.brief: Investigate emerging technologies—3D knitting, computational design, and smart textiles—and debate their implications for craft, sustainability, and labor.

lessons.title: Critical Historiography: Whose Stories Do We Tell About Sewing?
lessons.brief: Examine how sewing history has been written (often centering white, wealthy, Western perspectives), research marginalized communities' contributions, and produce a counter-narrative essay or documentary.

lessons.title: Economics of Scale: From Artisan Maker to Social Enterprise
lessons.brief: Develop a business plan for a sewing-based social enterprise addressing a specific community need, synthesizing ethical production, fair wages, sustainability, and market viability.

lessons.title: Capstone: Independent Research Project and Portfolio
lessons.brief: Conduct original research on a self-directed question in sewing, textiles, fashion, or design; create accompanying physical work; and present findings as a thesis or exhibition.

grade_1.focus: People live together in families and communities, and we all have jobs and roles.

lessons.title: My Family and My Home
lessons.brief: Students identify family members, learn what a family is, and describe where they live.

lessons.title: People Who Help Us
lessons.brief: Students name and describe what teachers, doctors, firefighters, and other helpers do in the community.

lessons.title: What We Do Together
lessons.brief: Students explore routines, rules, and activities that happen in families, schools, and neighborhoods.

grade_2.focus: Communities have different jobs, places, and rules that help people live and work together.

lessons.title: Different Types of Communities
lessons.brief: Students compare communities—farms, cities, towns, villages—and describe what makes each one different.

lessons.title: Jobs and Responsibilities
lessons.brief: Students identify many different jobs, explain what workers do, and understand why communities need different types of work.

lessons.title: Community Places and Services
lessons.brief: Students name and describe what happens in schools, shops, hospitals, parks, and libraries.

lessons.title: Rules Keep Us Safe
lessons.brief: Students explain why families, schools, and communities have rules, and what happens when people follow or break them.

grade_3.focus: Societies are organized by systems—roles, rules, and institutions—that meet people's basic needs.

lessons.title: Basic Needs and How Communities Meet Them
lessons.brief: Students categorize basic needs (food, shelter, safety, belonging) and identify institutions that provide them.

lessons.title: Roles and Responsibilities in Social Groups
lessons.brief: Students compare different roles within families, schools, and workplaces, and see how each role connects to the whole.

lessons.title: Norms and Customs Across Communities
lessons.brief: Students observe and compare how different groups have different ways of celebrating, greeting, eating, and dressing.

lessons.title: Cooperation and Conflict
lessons.brief: Students explore how cooperation helps groups work together and what happens when people disagree.

grade_4.focus: Societies function through interconnected systems of culture, economy, and governance that affect how people live.

lessons.title: Economic Systems: How We Exchange Goods and Services
lessons.brief: Students examine how people produce, trade, and consume resources; they compare barter, markets, and different economic roles.

lessons.title: Institutions and Social Organization
lessons.brief: Students identify major institutions (family, government, education, religion, business) and explain how they work together.

lessons.title: Culture: Shared Beliefs, Values, and Practices
lessons.brief: Students analyze cultural elements like language, traditions, art, and food as systems of shared meaning in communities.

lessons.title: Power, Authority, and Decision-Making
lessons.brief: Students explore different ways communities make decisions, establish rules, and distribute responsibility.

grade_5.focus: Societies change over time through historical processes, and people respond to changes in their social environment.

lessons.title: Social Change and Adaptation
lessons.brief: Students trace how societies adapt to new technologies, resources, and challenges, and examine both progress and consequences.

lessons.title: Inequality, Status, and Stratification
lessons.brief: Students investigate how societies distribute wealth, power, and resources unequally, and identify both causes and effects.

lessons.title: Socialization and Identity Formation
lessons.brief: Students explore how families, schools, peers, and media shape who people become and what they believe.

lessons.title: Conflict and Social Movements
lessons.brief: Students examine why conflicts arise in societies and how organized groups pursue change.

grade_6.focus: Societies are complex systems shaped by interactions between culture, economy, institutions, and individual agency across time and space.

lessons.title: Globalization and Interconnected Societies
lessons.brief: Students analyze how technology, trade, and communication connect societies worldwide and create both shared experiences and tensions.

lessons.title: Structural Inequality and Social Justice
lessons.brief: Students examine systemic discrimination based on race, gender, class, and other categories, and explore efforts toward equity.

lessons.title: Institutions as Systems of Power and Control
lessons.brief: Students critically analyze how institutions maintain order, distribute resources, and shape behavior—and where they succeed or fail.

lessons.title: Agency, Resistance, and Social Change
lessons.brief: Students evaluate how individuals and groups challenge established systems and create new social arrangements.

grade_7.focus: What is society and how do basic social structures shape who we are and how we live?

lessons.title: Society as a System
lessons.brief: Students explore how societies are made up of interconnected groups and institutions that work together to meet human needs.

lessons.title: Culture, Values, and Norms
lessons.brief: Students examine how shared beliefs, customs, and rules define different cultures and influence behaviour within groups.

lessons.title: Family, School, and Community
lessons.brief: Students investigate how primary social institutions shape identity, teach roles, and connect individuals to the wider society.

lessons.title: Social Roles and Socialisation
lessons.brief: Students learn how people learn to be members of society through families, peers, schools, and media.

grade_8.focus: How do inequality, diversity, and social categories create different experiences and opportunities for different people?

lessons.title: Social Class and Economic Inequality
lessons.brief: Students examine how access to wealth and resources creates different life chances and social positions.

lessons.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Identity
lessons.brief: Students analyse how racial and ethnic categories are socially constructed and shape privilege, discrimination, and belonging.

lessons.title: Gender Roles Across Cultures and Time
lessons.brief: Students explore how gender expectations vary across societies and history, and how they influence opportunities and power.

lessons.title: Stereotypes, Prejudice, and Discrimination
lessons.brief: Students investigate how generalised beliefs about groups lead to unfair treatment and how discrimination operates in institutions.

grade_9.focus: How do power, institutions, and social change interact to maintain or transform society?

lessons.title: Authority, Power, and Institutions
lessons.brief: Students analyse how power is distributed through government, law, education, and the economy, and who benefits from current arrangements.

lessons.title: Deviance, Crime, and Social Control
lessons.brief: Students examine why societies define certain behaviours as deviant or criminal, and how institutions maintain order and conformity.

lessons.title: Social Movements and Resistance
lessons.brief: Students study how groups challenge existing power structures through collective action and what enables social change.

lessons.title: Globalisation and Cultural Exchange
lessons.brief: Students explore how increased connection across borders reshapes economies, cultures, identities, and inequalities.

grade_10.focus: How do sociologists use theory and evidence to explain social patterns and test competing explanations?

lessons.title: Structural Functionalism and Social Stability
lessons.brief: Students engage with the functionalist perspective to analyse how institutions maintain social order and what happens when they fail.

lessons.title: Conflict Theory and Inequality
lessons.brief: Students apply conflict theory to examine how societies are sites of struggle over resources, power, and competing interests.

lessons.title: Symbolic Interactionism and Meaning-Making
lessons.brief: Students use interactionist theory to understand how individuals create meaning through social interaction and how identity is performed.

lessons.title: Reading and Interpreting Sociological Evidence
lessons.brief: Students learn to evaluate quantitative data, qualitative research, and original sources to assess sociological claims.

grade_11.focus: How do multiple theoretical frameworks reveal different dimensions of social reality, and what are their limitations?

lessons.title: Feminist Theory and Gendered Power
lessons.brief: Students critically examine how feminist perspectives expose gender as a system of power and critique other theories for ignoring it.

lessons.title: Postcolonial and Critical Race Theory
lessons.brief: Students analyse how colonialism and racism have been embedded in social structures and knowledge production, and how these frameworks challenge dominant narratives.

lessons.title: Comparing and Critiquing Theoretical Frameworks
lessons.brief: Students evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of functionalist, conflict, interactionist, and critical perspectives on specific social issues.

lessons.title: Methodology: How Sociologists Know What They Know
lessons.brief: Students interrogate research methods—surveys, interviews, ethnography—and consider whose perspectives are included or excluded in sociological knowledge.

grade_12.focus: How do sociologists conduct independent research and develop evidence-based arguments about contested social issues?

lessons.title: Designing and Conducting Sociological Research
lessons.brief: Students design original research projects, select appropriate methods, address ethical considerations, and collect data to answer their own questions.

lessons.title: Analysing and Synthesising Multiple Sources
lessons.brief: Students integrate primary research, peer-reviewed articles, statistical data, and theoretical frameworks to build comprehensive arguments.

lessons.title: Contemporary Debates: Work, Technology, and Identity
lessons.brief: Students apply sociological analysis to examine current social issues—labour precarity, social media, surveillance, and algorithmic power—using evidence and theory.

lessons.title: Sociology and Social Policy: Research Informing Change
lessons.brief: Students examine how sociological research informs policy decisions and critically analyse the relationship between academic knowledge and social intervention.

grade_1.focus: Learning to speak clearly about things you can see and touch right now.

lessons.title: My Voice and Me
lessons.brief: Students discover how their voice works, practice speaking loudly and softly, and learn that their words matter.

lessons.title: Naming Things Around Us
lessons.brief: Students learn to name objects in their classroom and say simple sentences about them.

lessons.title: Listening and Taking Turns
lessons.brief: Students practice waiting for their turn to speak and listening when others talk.

lessons.title: Telling What I Did Today
lessons.brief: Students share simple one-sentence stories about their own experiences using sequence words like 'first' and 'then'.

grade_2.focus: Describing things in more detail and explaining what things do.

lessons.title: Describing Objects with Senses
lessons.brief: Students use color, size, texture, and sound words to describe familiar objects in richer detail.

lessons.title: What Does It Do? Speaking About Actions
lessons.brief: Students observe things and animals and speak about what they do, using action verbs with confidence.

lessons.title: Telling Stories with a Beginning, Middle, and End
lessons.brief: Students organize their ideas into three parts and tell short personal stories in sequence.

lessons.title: Asking Questions Out Loud
lessons.brief: Students learn to ask 'who,' 'what,' and 'where' questions clearly and wait for answers.

grade_3.focus: Grouping ideas into categories and explaining why things happen the way they do.

lessons.title: Sorting and Grouping by Talking
lessons.brief: Students speak about how things belong together in groups and explain what makes each group special.

lessons.title: Because and So: Cause and Effect in Speech
lessons.brief: Students explain why things happen using 'because' and predict what comes next using 'so'.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Things
lessons.brief: Students speak about how two objects or ideas are the same and different, using comparison words.

lessons.title: Using Subject Words Correctly
lessons.brief: Students learn and use key vocabulary from science, maths, and other subjects when speaking aloud.

grade_4.focus: Explaining how parts work together as a whole and speaking about systems and processes.

lessons.title: How Parts Make a Whole
lessons.brief: Students identify and explain how separate parts of an object or system connect and depend on each other.

lessons.title: Step-by-Step: Speaking About Processes
lessons.brief: Students explain multi-step processes (like the water cycle or how food is made) in correct order with technical language.

lessons.title: Presenting Information Clearly
lessons.brief: Students learn to organize facts about a topic into a short presentation with an opening, details, and a closing.

lessons.title: Asking Deeper Questions
lessons.brief: Students move beyond simple questions to ask 'how' and 'why' questions that show they understand a topic.

grade_5.focus: Building longer explanations and asking meaningful questions about how and why things work.

lessons.title: Explaining Complex Processes
lessons.brief: Students give detailed explanations of longer processes, showing how one step leads to the next with accuracy.

lessons.title: Supporting Ideas with Evidence
lessons.brief: Students learn to state an idea and back it up with facts, examples, or observations when speaking.

lessons.title: Investigating Why Through Discussion
lessons.brief: Students ask 'why' questions in conversations and work with peers to explore possible answers together.

lessons.title: Giving Instructions So Others Can Follow
lessons.brief: Students create and deliver clear, detailed instructions for a task, checking that listeners understand.

grade_6.focus: Thinking critically about how ideas connect across subjects and presenting balanced analyses aloud.

lessons.title: Connections Across Subjects
lessons.brief: Students identify and articulate how concepts from science, maths, history, and literature relate and influence each other.

lessons.title: Analysing Different Perspectives
lessons.brief: Students present multiple viewpoints on a topic, explain what each person might believe and why, and discuss trade-offs.

lessons.title: Building an Argument with Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students construct multi-part spoken arguments with a claim, logical reasoning, and supporting examples.

lessons.title: Moderating Discussions
lessons.brief: Students lead conversations on topics, ask follow-up questions, manage turn-taking, and summarize key ideas heard.

grade_7.focus: Developing confidence and clarity in speaking by organizing thoughts logically and adapting voice to different audiences.

lessons.title: From Brain to Words: Organizing Your Ideas Before You Speak
lessons.brief: Learn how to structure thoughts using outlines, mind maps, and frameworks so your speaking flows naturally.

lessons.title: Speaking to Your Audience: Adjusting Tone, Language, and Examples
lessons.brief: Practice tailoring your message—vocabulary, formality, and examples—based on who is listening.

lessons.title: Presenting with Purpose: Facts, Stories, and Why They Matter
lessons.brief: Understand when to use data versus narrative, and how to connect both to a clear main idea your audience cares about.

lessons.title: Body Language and Your Message: What Your Posture Says When You Speak
lessons.brief: Explore how eye contact, gestures, and stance reinforce (or undermine) what you're saying.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating and constructing arguments by identifying claims, evidence, and counterarguments in spoken discourse.

lessons.title: Spotting Weak Arguments: Claims Without Evidence and False Logic
lessons.brief: Learn to identify logical fallacies, unsupported claims, and emotional manipulation in what others say.

lessons.title: Building Your Own Argument: Evidence, Reasoning, and Rebuttal
lessons.brief: Structure a spoken argument by selecting credible evidence, explaining your reasoning, and anticipating objections.

lessons.title: Both Sides of the Story: Presenting Opposing Views Fairly
lessons.brief: Practice articulating a viewpoint you disagree with charitably, then explain why you hold a different position.

lessons.title: Debates That Work: Listening, Conceding, and Building on What Others Say
lessons.brief: Engage in structured dialogue where you actively listen, acknowledge valid points, and advance the conversation.

grade_9.focus: Synthesizing multiple perspectives and sources into coherent spoken arguments while acknowledging complexity and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Connecting the Dots: Linking Ideas from Different Sources in Real Time
lessons.brief: Develop the ability to reference multiple texts, conversations, or viewpoints and explain how they relate to each other.

lessons.title: Nuance and Hedging: Speaking With Precision When the Answer Isn't Simple
lessons.brief: Learn language and techniques for acknowledging valid concerns, trade-offs, and contexts where your argument has limits.

lessons.title: Building a Framework: How Your Values Shape What You Argue
lessons.brief: Identify your underlying principles (fairness, efficiency, tradition, progress) and show how they guide your position on an issue.

lessons.title: Speaking Under Pressure: Defending Your Ideas When Challenged
lessons.brief: Practice staying composed, restating your position clearly, and addressing difficult questions without becoming defensive.

grade_10.focus: Interpreting and discussing primary sources, rhetorical moves, and historical context to construct evidence-based spoken analysis.

lessons.title: Reading Between the Lines: What a Historical Speech Actually Reveals
lessons.brief: Analyze primary texts—speeches, letters, documents—to understand the speaker's intent, audience, and hidden assumptions.

lessons.title: Rhetoric in Action: Identifying Persuasion Techniques and Their Effects
lessons.brief: Name and evaluate rhetorical devices (metaphor, repetition, appeal to authority) and discuss why speakers choose them.

lessons.title: Context Matters: How Time, Place, and Conflict Shape an Argument
lessons.brief: Explain how historical or social context changes the meaning and force of a spoken claim or debate.

lessons.title: Building a Case From Evidence: Selecting, Interpreting, and Presenting Sources
lessons.brief: Choose relevant primary and secondary sources, explain what they show, and use them to support your spoken thesis.

grade_11.focus: Critiquing frameworks, comparing competing interpretations, and constructing independent arguments with sophisticated evidence and self-awareness.

lessons.title: Comparing Frameworks: When Historians, Scientists, and Philosophers Disagree
lessons.brief: Examine how different disciplinary approaches or theoretical lenses produce different conclusions about the same event or question.

lessons.title: Unpacking Assumptions: What Do Speakers Take for Granted?
lessons.brief: Identify and articulate the unstated premises in an argument, and explain why examining them matters.

lessons.title: Constructing an Original Position: Moving Beyond Summary to Analysis
lessons.brief: Develop and defend an argument that is genuinely your own, showing awareness of existing viewpoints while advancing something new.

lessons.title: Acknowledging Limits: What Your Argument Cannot Claim and Why That Matters
lessons.brief: Demonstrate intellectual maturity by defining the scope of your argument, naming what you don't or can't prove, and why that distinction is important.

grade_12.focus: Conducting and presenting original research-based arguments that integrate evidence from multiple disciplines, acknowledge competing interpretations, and model academic discourse.

lessons.title: From Research to Argument: Synthesizing Primary Sources, Scholarship, and Data
lessons.brief: Design and deliver a spoken argument grounded in original research, integrating archival sources, peer-reviewed studies, and quantitative evidence.

lessons.title: Disciplinary Conversations: Speaking as a Historian, Economist, or Scientist
lessons.brief: Adopt the conventions, evidence standards, and concerns of a particular field to construct and defend discipline-specific arguments.

lessons.title: Revising Your Position: Updating Your Argument in Light of New Evidence
lessons.brief: Model intellectual flexibility by explaining how new sources or counterarguments have changed or refined your original thesis.

lessons.title: Presenting to Experts: Defending Your Argument in Front of Informed Skeptics
lessons.brief: Prepare for and conduct a sustained academic defense where you anticipate expert objections, cite scholarship precisely, and maintain credibility under scrutiny.

grade_1.focus: Learning to sort objects and count them in simple groups.

lessons.title: Sorting Toys by Color and Shape
lessons.brief: Students sort real objects into groups by one property at a time and name what they see.

lessons.title: Counting and Comparing Groups
lessons.brief: Students count objects in different piles and decide which group has more or fewer.

lessons.title: Making Simple Picture Charts
lessons.brief: Students draw pictures to show how many of each thing they have.
