grade_2.focus: Recording data by drawing and making tallies to answer simple questions about things around them.

lessons.title: Asking Questions We Can Answer with Objects
lessons.brief: Students think of yes-or-no questions about themselves or their classroom and collect answers by sorting.

lessons.title: Using Tally Marks to Keep Count
lessons.brief: Students learn to use tick marks to record data and count them up at the end.

lessons.title: Picture Graphs and What They Show
lessons.brief: Students create and read simple picture graphs where each picture stands for one object or person.

lessons.title: Comparing Data: More, Fewer, and Equal
lessons.brief: Students look at their recorded data and describe which group is biggest, smallest, or the same size.

grade_3.focus: Collecting data by asking questions, organizing it in different ways, and describing patterns in what they find.

lessons.title: Designing a Simple Survey Question
lessons.brief: Students learn to ask a clear question, predict some answers, and collect data from classmates.

lessons.title: Bar Graphs: Reading Heights and Comparing Amounts
lessons.brief: Students build and read bar graphs using blocks or drawn rectangles to compare groups of data.

lessons.title: Spotting Patterns and Most/Least
lessons.brief: Students look for patterns in their data and identify which category has the most and least entries.

lessons.title: Real-World Data: Tracking Weather and Favorite Things
lessons.brief: Students collect data over time about the weather or classroom preferences and discuss what it tells them.

grade_4.focus: Designing investigations with a question and hypothesis, collecting organized data, and drawing conclusions from what the data shows.

lessons.title: From Question to Hypothesis: What Do We Think Will Happen?
lessons.brief: Students learn to turn a question into a prediction and plan how to test it with data.

lessons.title: Frequency Tables and Scaled Bar Graphs
lessons.brief: Students organize data in tables and create bar graphs where the scale represents more than one item.

lessons.title: Line Plots and Measuring Data
lessons.brief: Students record measurements of objects on a number line to see the spread and clusters in their data.

lessons.title: Drawing Conclusions: What Does Our Data Tell Us?
lessons.brief: Students compare their hypothesis to their results and explain what they learned from the data.

grade_5.focus: Investigating relationships between variables, displaying data in multiple formats, and using data to support explanations.

lessons.title: Variables and How They Relate to Each Other
lessons.brief: Students identify which factors change together and test whether one variable affects another using controlled data collection.

lessons.title: Dot Plots, Histograms, and Choosing the Right Display
lessons.brief: Students learn when to use different graph types and create histograms to show distribution of measurements.

lessons.title: Describing Data: Center, Spread, and Outliers
lessons.brief: Students calculate the mean, median, and range to describe what is typical in their data and notice unusual values.

lessons.title: Using Data to Solve Real Problems
lessons.brief: Students design a multi-step investigation to answer a complex question and present findings with supporting evidence.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing data distributions and relationships, evaluating the quality of data collection methods, and recognizing how data can inform decisions.

lessons.title: Comparing Distributions: Shape, Center, and Spread
lessons.brief: Students analyze two or more data sets side by side, comparing their shapes and statistical measures to draw meaningful comparisons.

lessons.title: Scatter Plots and Linear Association
lessons.brief: Students create scatter plots to investigate whether two numerical variables have a relationship and describe the strength of that connection.

lessons.title: Evaluating Data Quality: Bias, Sample Size, and Method
lessons.brief: Students examine whether data was collected fairly, consider how sample size and method affect results, and identify potential bias.

lessons.title: Statistics in the News: Interpreting Claims from Data
lessons.brief: Students find real-world data claims in media, analyze the underlying data, and evaluate whether the conclusions are justified.

grade_7.focus: Students learn to collect, organize, and describe real-world data using basic statistical tools.

lessons.title: Why Data Matters: Questions We Can Answer
lessons.brief: Students explore how data answers real questions about their lives, school, and world.

lessons.title: Collecting Data: Surveys, Samples, and Sources
lessons.brief: Students design and conduct surveys, understand sampling, and learn the difference between reliable and biased sources.

lessons.title: Organizing and Displaying Data: Tables, Graphs, and Patterns
lessons.brief: Students organize raw data into tables, create bar graphs and line graphs, and identify patterns.

lessons.title: Describing Data: Averages, Ranges, and What They Tell Us
lessons.brief: Students calculate mean, median, mode, and range, and learn what each reveals about a dataset.

grade_8.focus: Students evaluate the reliability of data and recognize how statistical choices can shape conclusions.

lessons.title: Bias in Data: How Questions Shape Answers
lessons.brief: Students analyze how survey design, wording, and sample selection introduce bias, and why this matters.

lessons.title: Comparing Data Sets: Which Graph Tells the Real Story?
lessons.brief: Students compare multiple representations of the same data and evaluate which choices are misleading or fair.

lessons.title: Probability and Prediction: When Data Doesn't Tell the Whole Story
lessons.brief: Students explore probability, randomness, and the limits of what past data can predict about the future.

lessons.title: Statistics in the News: Spotting Dodgy Claims
lessons.brief: Students critique real news stories and advertisements that misuse statistics, and learn to ask critical questions.

grade_9.focus: Students model and interpret relationships between variables, connecting data patterns to causation and prediction.

lessons.title: Correlation vs. Causation: Distinguishing Coincidence from Connection
lessons.brief: Students analyze scatter plots and real examples to understand why correlation doesn't prove one variable causes another.

lessons.title: Lines of Best Fit: Making Predictions from Trends
lessons.brief: Students use scatter plots to identify linear relationships, fit trend lines, and use them to make reasonable predictions.

lessons.title: Two-Way Tables: Understanding Relationships Between Categories
lessons.brief: Students organize categorical data in two-way tables and calculate conditional frequencies to find associations.

lessons.title: Designing Fair Comparisons: Experiments vs. Observational Studies
lessons.brief: Students design simple studies, understand confounding variables, and evaluate whether data supports causal claims.

grade_10.focus: Students work with distributions, quantify uncertainty, and evaluate evidence in research and policy contexts.

lessons.title: The Normal Distribution: Shape, Spread, and the Standard Deviation
lessons.brief: Students analyze bell curves, calculate standard deviation, and use z-scores to locate data within distributions.

lessons.title: Sampling Distributions and Margin of Error: Why Polls Aren't Always Right
lessons.brief: Students explore how sample size affects precision, calculate margins of error, and interpret confidence intervals.

lessons.title: Comparing Populations: Statistical Significance and What It Means
lessons.brief: Students compare two groups using statistics, distinguish between meaningful and random differences, and read research claims.

lessons.title: Evaluating Studies: Methodology, Assumptions, and Real-World Limits
lessons.brief: Students critique methodology in published studies, identify limitations, and assess whether conclusions are justified.

grade_11.focus: Students develop frameworks for inference, analyze complex data structures, and evaluate competing statistical arguments.

lessons.title: Hypothesis Testing: Constructing and Evaluating Claims with Data
lessons.brief: Students formulate null and alternative hypotheses, calculate test statistics, and interpret p-values and significance levels.

lessons.title: Regression Analysis: Modeling Relationships and Assessing Fit
lessons.brief: Students fit regression models to multivariate data, interpret coefficients and R², assess assumptions, and discuss limitations.

lessons.title: Bayesian Reasoning: Updating Beliefs with New Evidence
lessons.brief: Students apply conditional probability to real scenarios, understand how prior beliefs affect interpretation, and critique misapplications.

lessons.title: Statistical Arguments in Policy and Science: Competing Interpretations
lessons.brief: Students analyze how different statistical framings lead to different policy conclusions and evaluate the rigor of each argument.

grade_12.focus: Students conduct independent statistical research, integrate multiple methods, and critically synthesize evidence across disciplines.

lessons.title: Designing and Conducting a Statistical Research Project
lessons.brief: Students formulate research questions, collect and manage data, choose appropriate methods, and communicate findings with evidence.

lessons.title: Causal Inference: Moving Beyond Correlation in Observational Data
lessons.brief: Students study causal reasoning frameworks, propensity matching, instrumental variables, and when causal claims are and aren't justified.

lessons.title: Advanced Models: Classification, Prediction, and the Role of Assumptions
lessons.brief: Students explore logistic regression, decision trees, and other models; evaluate trade-offs between accuracy and interpretability.

lessons.title: The Philosophy and Ethics of Statistical Practice
lessons.brief: Students examine reproducibility, p-hacking, publication bias, data privacy, and the responsibility of statisticians in society.

grade_1.focus: Discovering colours, shapes, and textures through play and exploration with real materials.

lessons.title: Colours All Around Us
lessons.brief: Learning to name and mix primary colours using paint, and spotting colours in everyday objects.

lessons.title: Shapes in My Hand
lessons.brief: Exploring circles, squares, and triangles by drawing, tracing, and finding them in the classroom and nature.

lessons.title: How Things Feel
lessons.brief: Touching and drawing different textures like bumpy, smooth, and rough using pencils, brushes, and fingers.

grade_2.focus: Creating pictures by combining colours, shapes, and marks to show real things and feelings.

lessons.title: Making Lines Tell Stories
lessons.brief: Using thick, thin, wavy, and straight lines to draw movement, paths, and simple scenes.

lessons.title: Painting What I See
lessons.brief: Observing objects in the classroom and painting them by layering colours and deciding where things go on the page.

lessons.title: Patterns and Repeats
lessons.brief: Creating patterns using shapes and colours that repeat, and finding patterns in nature and decorations.

lessons.title: Building Sculptures from Scraps
lessons.brief: Stacking, joining, and arranging found materials to make 3D objects that stand up.

grade_3.focus: Comparing and sorting art ideas by understanding how artists use light, space, and subject matter to create meaning.

lessons.title: Light and Shadow in Drawing
lessons.brief: Using shading and tone to show which parts of an object are light and dark, making pictures look more real.

lessons.title: Arranging Space on the Page
lessons.brief: Learning how placing objects near, far, high, and low creates different feelings and tells viewers where to look.

lessons.title: What Artists Choose to Paint
lessons.brief: Comparing portraits, landscapes, and still lifes to understand why artists pick different subjects and what they show.

lessons.title: Printmaking: Stamping and Pressing
lessons.brief: Creating repeated images by carving, stamping, and pressing materials, and experimenting with how pressure changes the print.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how colour, form, and composition work together as a system to create balanced and expressive artworks.

lessons.title: The Colour Wheel and Harmony
lessons.brief: Learning secondary and tertiary colours, complementary pairs, and warm/cool relationships to make colour choices intentional.

lessons.title: Proportion and the Human Figure
lessons.brief: Measuring and drawing the body by understanding how parts relate to the whole, using head-heights and landmarks.

lessons.title: Foreground, Middle Ground, and Background
lessons.brief: Creating depth in 2D art by layering and sizing objects to show distance, and understanding how perspective works.

lessons.title: Symmetry, Balance, and Movement
lessons.brief: Using symmetrical and asymmetrical composition to create stable or dynamic feelings in a piece.

grade_5.focus: Analyzing how artists use technique, material, and process deliberately to communicate ideas, emotion, and cultural meaning.

lessons.title: From Concept to Finished Work
lessons.brief: Planning a piece through sketches, material choices, and revisions; understanding how process shapes the final artwork.

lessons.title: Texture and Mixed Media: Building Surfaces
lessons.brief: Combining paint, collage, wire, and found objects to create layered textures that express meaning beyond the image alone.

lessons.title: Art Movements and Why They Changed
lessons.brief: Exploring how artists in different periods (Impressionism, Cubism, Abstraction) solved problems differently and reflected their times.

lessons.title: Portraiture: Showing Identity and Emotion
lessons.brief: Studying how artists use facial features, posture, background, and colour to reveal character and psychological depth.

grade_6.focus: Critically examining how artists across cultures use visual language to respond to social issues, personal experience, and aesthetic questions.

lessons.title: Perspective Systems: From Renaissance to Abstraction
lessons.brief: Analyzing one-point, two-point, and non-linear perspective as tools or rejections of realism, and what each choice communicates.

lessons.title: Symbolism, Metaphor, and Meaning-Making
lessons.brief: Decoding how artists embed cultural references, personal symbols, and metaphors in their work to layer meaning beyond the literal.

lessons.title: Art as Social Commentary
lessons.brief: Examining how contemporary and historical artists address identity, power, environment, and justice through visual art and installation.

lessons.title: Materials, Production, and Authenticity
lessons.brief: Investigating how artists' choices of medium, technique, and scale reflect aesthetic values and connect to issues of craft, reproducibility, and originality.

grade_7.focus: How artists use elements and principles to communicate meaning and emotion in visual work.

lessons.title: Color as a Language: Warm, Cool, and Emotional Temperature
lessons.brief: Students explore how color choice conveys mood and meaning, moving beyond aesthetic preference to intentional communication.

lessons.title: Composition and Balance: Why Artists Place Things Where They Do
lessons.brief: Students analyze how artists use symmetry, asymmetry, and focal points to guide the viewer's eye and create visual stories.

lessons.title: Light and Shadow: Creating Depth and Drama
lessons.brief: Students investigate how artists manipulate light and shadow to create dimension, focus attention, and evoke atmosphere.

lessons.title: Art Movements as Responses to Their Time
lessons.brief: Students connect Impressionism, Cubism, and Surrealism to the historical moments and questions that inspired them.

grade_8.focus: How cultural context shapes artistic choices and how artists challenge or reflect the values of their society.

lessons.title: Perspective as Power: Who Gets Centered in Art and Why
lessons.brief: Students examine how Western linear perspective became dominant and whose viewpoints were historically excluded or marginalized in visual representation.

lessons.title: Symbol and Allegory: Reading Hidden Meanings in Artwork
lessons.brief: Students decode symbols in religious, political, and social art to understand how artists embed commentary within their work.

lessons.title: Portraiture Across Cultures: Identity, Status, and Representation
lessons.brief: Students compare portraiture traditions from different cultures to explore how societies define and display identity and power.

lessons.title: Art and Protest: When Artists Challenge Authority
lessons.brief: Students analyze how artists have used visual work to critique injustice, from Diego Rivera's murals to contemporary street art.

grade_9.focus: How artists synthesize multiple influences, techniques, and ideas to develop distinctive visual voices that address complex themes.

lessons.title: Style as Synthesis: How Artists Build on What Came Before
lessons.brief: Students trace how individual artists (Picasso, Frida Kahlo, Basquiat) absorbed and transformed influences to create recognizable personal styles.

lessons.title: Medium Shapes Meaning: Why Artists Choose Specific Materials and Techniques
lessons.brief: Students investigate how the choice of paint, clay, photography, or digital media affects what an artwork can express and communicate.

lessons.title: Narrative and Non-Narrative: Different Ways to Tell Stories Visually
lessons.brief: Students compare sequential art, abstraction, and visual metaphor to understand how meaning can be conveyed without literal representation.

lessons.title: Art Institutions and Gatekeeping: Museums, Galleries, and Who Decides What Matters
lessons.brief: Students examine how museums, collectors, and critics have historically determined which artists are valued and how this is beginning to change.

grade_10.focus: How to read, interpret, and evaluate visual arguments by analyzing form, context, and artist intent with textual and historical evidence.

lessons.title: Formal Analysis: Reading Visual Texts Like Written Arguments
lessons.brief: Students develop methods to closely examine composition, color, line, texture, and form as evidence supporting interpretation of an artwork's meaning.

lessons.title: Primary Sources in Art History: What Archives, Letters, and Manifestos Reveal
lessons.brief: Students interpret original documents—artist statements, exhibition catalogs, reviews—to reconstruct artist intent and historical context.

lessons.title: Contested Interpretations: When Experts Disagree About Artworks
lessons.brief: Students examine multiple scholarly interpretations of a single work to understand how evidence, bias, and perspective shape art historical argument.

lessons.title: Global Visual Traditions and Western Art History: Whose Canon Is This?
lessons.brief: Students question the dominance of European/American art in curricula and explore equally sophisticated traditions from Africa, Asia, and Indigenous cultures.

grade_11.focus: How to construct and defend original arguments about visual culture by comparing frameworks, analyzing power structures, and engaging with contemporary debates.

lessons.title: Competing Theories: Marxist, Feminist, and Postcolonial Readings of the Same Artwork
lessons.brief: Students apply different critical frameworks to a single work and evaluate which interpretations are most persuasive and what each reveals or obscures.

lessons.title: The Politics of Representation: Whose Stories Get Told and How
lessons.brief: Students analyze how gender, race, class, and nationality have been visualized (and erased) in canonical art, and how contemporary artists are rewriting these narratives.

lessons.title: Digital Culture and Image Manipulation: Truth, Authenticity, and Authority in the Image Age
lessons.brief: Students examine how digital tools, social media, and AI challenge historical concepts of artistic authenticity and authorship.

lessons.title: Commissioning and Critique: Making an Argument for Why a Public Artwork Should or Shouldn't Exist
lessons.brief: Students research a contested public artwork, synthesize perspectives from artists/communities/institutions, and construct a defended position on its value.

grade_12.focus: How to conduct independent visual research, synthesize knowledge across disciplines, and make evidence-based arguments about art's role in culture and politics.

lessons.title: Archival Research and Visual Evidence: Building Arguments from Museum Collections and Historical Records
lessons.brief: Students design and conduct original research using primary sources, digital archives, and interviews to support an independent thesis about an artist, movement, or artwork.

lessons.title: Art and Social Change: Evaluating Claims About Whether Art Can (or Should) Transform Society
lessons.brief: Students examine competing case studies (from suffragette posters to Black Lives Matter aesthetics) and construct a nuanced argument about art's political efficacy.

lessons.title: Interdisciplinary Connections: How Visual Culture Reflects and Shapes Economics, Science, and Philosophy
lessons.brief: Students research how art both reflects and influences developments in capitalism, technology, and intellectual thought, using evidence from multiple disciplines.

lessons.title: Curating Knowledge: Designing an Exhibition That Argues Something
lessons.brief: Students develop a research-based exhibition concept that makes a coherent argument through selection, sequencing, and framing of artworks.

grade_1.focus: Learning the names and feel of wood, and making simple things with hands and basic tools.

lessons.title: What is Wood? Touching and Seeing Different Kinds
lessons.brief: Students explore softwood and hardwood by touch, smell, and sight to discover how wood feels different depending on where it comes from.

lessons.title: Hammering and Nailing: My First Tool Skills
lessons.brief: Students learn how to hold a hammer safely and drive a nail into soft wood to make their first joined structure.

lessons.title: Sawing Straight: Using a Handsaw with a Partner
lessons.brief: Students practice cutting wood in a straight line using a handsaw, learning how to hold the wood steady and move the saw smoothly.

lessons.title: Joining Two Pieces: Nails, Screws, and Glue
lessons.brief: Students compare three ways to hold wood pieces together and decide which method works best for different joining tasks.

grade_2.focus: Building simple structures and learning how wood pieces fit together to make things that stand up and work.

lessons.title: The Shape of Wood: Grain, Grain Direction, and How It Moves
lessons.brief: Students examine wood grain patterns and discover that wood shrinks and swells depending on how wet it is and which way the grain runs.

lessons.title: Building a Box: Planning and Joining Four Sides
lessons.brief: Students design and build a simple wooden box by cutting four pieces and joining them with nails or screws to understand how pieces make a solid shape.

lessons.title: Edges and Corners: Smoothing Wood with Sandpaper and Files
lessons.brief: Students use sandpaper and files to make rough edges smooth and safe, and name the tools and techniques they use.

lessons.title: Finishing Wood: Stain, Paint, and Oil
lessons.brief: Students apply different finishes to wood samples and observe how each one changes the color and feel of the surface.

grade_3.focus: Comparing different wood types and joinery methods, and understanding why woodworkers choose specific materials and techniques for different projects.

lessons.title: Sorting Wood by Type: Properties That Matter for Building
lessons.brief: Students categorize wood samples by hardness, color, grain, and weight, then match each type to a project where those properties are useful.

lessons.title: Joints That Hold: Butt, Lap, and Mortise Joins Side by Side
lessons.brief: Students build three different wood joints, test their strength, and identify which joint works best for different purposes.

lessons.title: How a Hand Plane Works: Shaving Wood Thin
lessons.brief: Students learn how a hand plane cuts wood by scraping, practice planing a board flat, and observe how grain direction changes how easily the plane cuts.

lessons.title: From Tree to Board: Sawing, Drying, and Figuring Out Waste
lessons.brief: Students trace how a tree becomes usable lumber and calculate how much wood is lost when you cut out a project from a rough board.

grade_4.focus: Understanding how wood structure, tool mechanics, and joinery methods work together as systems to create strong, durable projects.

lessons.title: Wood Anatomy: Cells, Grain Structure, and Why Wood Splits
lessons.brief: Students examine wood cells under magnification and explain why wood is stronger along the grain than across it, and how this affects cutting and splitting.

lessons.title: Mechanical Advantage in Woodworking Tools: Levers, Wedges, and Screws
lessons.brief: Students classify woodworking tools by their mechanical systems and calculate how each tool multiplies human effort to cut or fasten wood.

lessons.title: Strong Joinery: Load, Grain Direction, and Joint Selection
lessons.brief: Students design and test wood joints under different load directions, then explain why a mortise-and-tenon joint is stronger than a butt joint for specific uses.

lessons.title: Moisture Content and Wood Movement: Planning for Seasonal Changes
lessons.brief: Students measure how wood expands and contracts with humidity, and design frame-and-panel joinery that allows for movement without cracking.

grade_5.focus: Planning and executing multi-step projects that require understanding wood properties, tool selection, and how each step affects the final result.

lessons.title: Reading a Woodworking Plan: Interpreting Drawings, Measurements, and Joinery Symbols
lessons.brief: Students learn to read technical drawings with views from multiple angles, decode joinery symbols, and calculate cut lists for a complete project.

lessons.title: Sequencing a Project: Why Order Matters From Rough Milling to Finishing
lessons.brief: Students plan the logical sequence of steps for a project—milling to size, joinery, assembly, shaping, and finishing—and explain why doing steps out of order creates problems.

lessons.title: Grain Direction and Tool Marks: Controlling How Tools Cut Wood
lessons.brief: Students experiment with planing, sawing, and chiseling in different grain directions to understand how grain affects the quality of the cut and practice techniques to minimize tearout.

lessons.title: Finishing Systems: Stain, Sealers, and Topcoats Working Together
lessons.brief: Students apply and compare multi-step finishing systems, understanding how each layer protects the wood and how surface prep between coats affects final quality.

grade_6.focus: Analyzing how wood, joinery, design, and tool choices interact across a complete project, and connecting woodworking decisions to broader design and engineering principles.

lessons.title: Structural Design in Wood: Load Paths, Stress, and How Joinery Distributes Force
lessons.brief: Students analyze a furniture design using diagrams of force distribution, predict where stress concentrates, and explain how joint design and wood grain orientation manage those stresses.

lessons.title: Wood Species Selection for Function and Aesthetics: Trade-Offs Across Projects
lessons.brief: Students research multiple wood species with different properties—hardness, density, color, workability, sustainability—and justify species choices for different project requirements.

lessons.title: Precision and Tolerance: Why Measurements Matter From Layout to Assembly
lessons.brief: Students apply increasingly tight tolerances across a project, measure with calipers and gauges, and analyze how accumulated small errors affect final fit and function.

lessons.title: Sustainable Sourcing, Waste Reduction, and the Environmental Cost of Wood
lessons.brief: Students research forestry practices, compare the carbon footprint of different finishes and adhesives, and design project layouts that minimize waste while meeting specifications.

grade_7.focus: Master fundamental hand tools and basic joinery techniques to build simple, functional wooden objects.

lessons.title: Reading and Marking Wood Grain
lessons.brief: Learn to identify grain direction and properly mark wood for cutting to prevent tearout and ensure quality finishes.

lessons.title: Hand Planes: From Setup to Shaving
lessons.brief: Understand plane anatomy, blade sharpening, and technique to produce clean surfaces without power tools.

lessons.title: Mortise and Tenon: The Foundation Joint
lessons.brief: Cut and fit the most reliable traditional joint by hand, understanding why this connection has endured for centuries.

lessons.title: Finishing Wood: Oils, Stains, and Sealers
lessons.brief: Apply protective finishes that enhance wood's natural beauty while understanding how each product affects appearance and durability.

grade_8.focus: Apply hand skills to design and construct multi-piece projects while evaluating different woodworking traditions and approaches.

lessons.title: Frame-and-Panel Construction: Solving Wood Movement
lessons.brief: Design and build panels that account for seasonal wood expansion using floating panels and restraint joints.

lessons.title: European vs. Asian Tooling: Comparative Techniques
lessons.brief: Compare push-plane and pull-saw approaches from different traditions, testing both to understand the trade-offs in each method.

lessons.title: Hand-Cut Dovetails: Precision Without Templates
lessons.brief: Master laying out and cutting interlocking dovetail joints freehand, developing the spatial reasoning required for complex joinery.

lessons.title: Wood Selection and Sustainability
lessons.brief: Research local and imported species, understanding how grain, stability, and ethical sourcing affect design and construction decisions.

grade_9.focus: Synthesize design principles, material science, and hand techniques to build finished furniture that solves a real functional problem.

lessons.title: Designing for Function: Load, Span, and Joinery Selection
lessons.brief: Analyze how intended use determines which joints, wood species, and thicknesses are appropriate for chairs, tables, and storage pieces.

lessons.title: The History and Physics of Bent Lamination
lessons.brief: Study historical curved furniture, then apply steam-bending and lamination techniques to create forms impossible with solid wood alone.

lessons.title: Surface Preparation: From Rough Milling to Final Sanding
lessons.brief: Develop the systematic workflow that transforms raw lumber into dimensioned stock, learning how planing sequence affects grain tearout and flatness.

lessons.title: Building Your First Piece: From Sketch to Finished Cabinet
lessons.brief: Plan and construct a complete storage cabinet, integrating joinery, finishing, and design decisions made throughout the year.

grade_10.focus: Interpret historical and contemporary woodworking design movements while developing a personal making philosophy that balances tradition and innovation.

lessons.title: Arts and Crafts vs. Machine Production: Philosophy in Wood
lessons.brief: Analyze primary sources and built examples from the Arts and Crafts movement, then debate whether hand-tool values apply to modern making.

lessons.title: Reading Technical Drawings and Adapting Historical Plans
lessons.brief: Interpret original Shaker, Mission, and Arts and Crafts blueprints; modify proportions for contemporary use while respecting design intent.

lessons.title: Wood Movement Science: Predicting Failure and Preventing It
lessons.brief: Study the physics of wood shrinkage and expansion in different grain directions, then design joinery and grain orientation to prevent warping and cracking.

lessons.title: Case Study: Comparative Analysis of Two Design Traditions
lessons.brief: Research Scandinavian and Japanese furniture design, analyzing how climate, available materials, and cultural values shaped their distinct approaches.

grade_11.focus: Critique and compare competing woodworking philosophies and methods while executing an advanced project that demonstrates informed aesthetic and technical choices.

lessons.title: The Craft vs. Industry Debate: Evidence and Arguments
lessons.brief: Evaluate historical and contemporary arguments about the value of handmade versus industrial furniture, using primary sources and material evidence.

lessons.title: Sustainability and Material Ethics: Global Timber Trade Analysis
lessons.brief: Research certification systems, illegal logging, and ecological impact; make sourcing decisions for your own work grounded in evidence.

lessons.title: Advanced Joinery: Choosing the Right Connection for Your Design
lessons.brief: Study mortise-and-tenon variations, bridle joints, and specialty joinery; select based on load, aesthetics, and maker philosophy rather than habit.

lessons.title: Developing Your Design Voice Through Material Constraint
lessons.brief: Execute a complex piece that reflects a deliberate position on aesthetics (minimalism, ornamentation, modularity, etc.), justified through material and historical analysis.

grade_12.focus: Conduct independent research into woodworking's cultural, environmental, and aesthetic dimensions while proposing and executing a self-directed project that synthesizes technical mastery with critical thinking.

lessons.title: Research Seminar: Tracing a Technique Across Cultures and Time Periods
lessons.brief: Select one joinery method or design tradition; trace its origins, evolution, and regional variations using scholarly sources and museum archives.

lessons.title: Environmental Footprint: From Forest to Finish—Systems Thinking in Timber
lessons.brief: Model the full lifecycle of a wooden object, including harvesting, transport, processing, and disposal; propose interventions that reduce environmental impact.

lessons.title: Contemporary Makers: Studio Practice and Scale
lessons.brief: Interview or research living furniture makers; analyze how they balance artistic vision, economics, sustainability, and the role of machines in hand-craft.

lessons.title: Thesis Project: Designing and Executing a Significant Commission
lessons.brief: Develop a detailed proposal for a substantial furniture piece that solves a real functional and aesthetic problem, supported by research and justification of all technical and design decisions.

grade_1.focus: People live in different places around the world and do different things based on where they live.

lessons.title: Homes Around the World
lessons.brief: Students learn what homes look like in different countries and why they are built differently.

lessons.title: Food From Different Lands
lessons.brief: Students discover what people eat in different parts of the world and where food comes from.

lessons.title: Families and Communities
lessons.brief: Students explore how families live together and help each other in communities near and far.

lessons.title: Work People Do
lessons.brief: Students see different jobs people have and how work helps communities survive.

grade_2.focus: People in different times and places have different tools, clothes, and ways of living based on their environment.

lessons.title: Then and Now: How Life Has Changed
lessons.brief: Students compare what life was like a long time ago with what it is like today, looking at clothes, tools, and homes.

lessons.title: Tools People Invented
lessons.brief: Students learn about simple tools people created to help them hunt, farm, build, and cook.

lessons.title: Weather and Where People Live
lessons.brief: Students see how hot, cold, wet, and dry places shape what people wear, eat, and build.

lessons.title: Trade: Sharing Things Across Distance
lessons.brief: Students discover how people trade goods with each other even when they live far apart.

grade_3.focus: Early civilizations developed in river valleys where people farmed, built cities, and created systems to organize their lives.

lessons.title: Why Rivers Were Perfect for the First Cities
lessons.brief: Students learn why the Nile, Tigris, Euphrates, and Yellow Rivers attracted people to settle and farm nearby.

lessons.title: From Hunters to Farmers: The Agricultural Revolution
lessons.brief: Students trace how people stopped hunting animals and started growing crops, and how this changed everything.

lessons.title: Kings, Priests, and Regular People: Social Order in Ancient Civilizations
lessons.brief: Students compare how different ancient societies organized themselves with leaders, workers, and systems of rules.

lessons.title: Writing and Numbers: How Civilizations Kept Records
lessons.brief: Students explore why ancient peoples invented writing and number systems, and what they recorded.

grade_4.focus: Ancient empires grew by conquering land and people, developing governments, religions, and technologies that shaped entire regions.

lessons.title: How Empires Expand: The Strategies of Ancient Rome and China
lessons.brief: Students examine how empires built armies, roads, and administrations to control vast territories and populations.

lessons.title: Religion as a System: How Beliefs Organized Society
lessons.brief: Students analyze how religions like Hinduism, Buddhism, Judaism, and Christianity provided laws, values, and explanations for how societies should work.

lessons.title: Technology and Power: Weapons, Architecture, and Trade
lessons.brief: Students investigate how innovations in engineering, military technology, and transport gave empires advantages over neighboring peoples.

lessons.title: Trade Networks: The Silk Road and Beyond
lessons.brief: Students map how goods, ideas, and diseases moved along routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa, reshaping civilizations.

grade_5.focus: The fall of empires, the rise of new powers, and the movement of peoples created the medieval world where feudalism, faith, and kingdoms reorganized society.

lessons.title: Why Empires Collapsed: Rome's Fall and Its Consequences
lessons.brief: Students examine the economic, military, and political reasons Rome declined and how invading peoples reshaped Europe.

lessons.title: Feudalism: A System Built on Loyalty and Land
lessons.brief: Students understand how feudal relationships between lords and vassals created a decentralized system of power and protection.

lessons.title: The Power of the Church in Medieval Life
lessons.brief: Students analyze how the Christian Church became the largest institution in Europe, controlling land, education, and moral authority.

lessons.title: Medieval Kingdoms and the Birth of Nations
lessons.brief: Students trace how small kingdoms merged into larger, more organized nations with defined borders and centralized governments.

grade_6.focus: The Renaissance, Reformation, and Age of Exploration marked a transition from medieval to early modern thinking, challenging old authorities and connecting continents.

lessons.title: Humanism and the Renaissance: Why Europeans Rediscovered the Classical World
lessons.brief: Students analyze how scholars and artists revived Greek and Roman ideas, emphasizing human potential and individualism over purely religious authority.

lessons.title: The Reformation: When Religious Authority Was Questioned
lessons.brief: Students examine why Martin Luther and others challenged the Catholic Church's power, fragmenting Western Christianity and reshaping European politics.

lessons.title: Global Exploration and Its Causes: Technology, Trade, and Empire-Building
lessons.brief: Students investigate why European powers sailed to Africa, Asia, and the Americas—examining navigation advances, economic incentives, and competitive nationalism.

lessons.title: Encounters and Consequences: How Global Connection Transformed Societies
lessons.brief: Students evaluate the immediate and long-term effects of European exploration on Indigenous peoples, African societies, Asian trade networks, and European wealth.

grade_7.focus: How empires rise and fall: the patterns of conquest, trade, and cultural exchange that shaped the ancient and medieval worlds.

lessons.title: Why Empires Build: Power, Resources, and Trade Routes
lessons.brief: Explores the economic and military motivations behind imperial expansion in ancient Rome, Persia, and China.

lessons.title: The Silk Road: How Ideas and Goods Traveled Across Continents
lessons.brief: Traces the interconnected networks of trade and cultural contact between Europe, Asia, and Africa from 200 BCE to 1400s.

lessons.title: Fall and Rise: Why Empires Collapse and What Comes Next
lessons.brief: Examines the collapse of Rome, the rise of Islamic empires, and the transition from ancient to medieval societies.

lessons.title: Power from Faith: How Religion Shaped Medieval Kingdoms
lessons.brief: Analyzes the role of Christianity, Islam, and Buddhism in organizing medieval societies and legitimizing rulers.

grade_8.focus: Competing worldviews and systems: how different societies organized themselves politically, religiously, and economically, and what tensions arose when they met.

lessons.title: Feudalism vs. Centralized Power: Two Models of Governance in Medieval Europe and China
lessons.brief: Compares decentralized feudal systems in Europe with strong centralized dynasties in China, examining their strengths and weaknesses.

lessons.title: The Age of Exploration: Whose Perspective Counts When Worlds Collide?
lessons.brief: Examines the motivations of European explorers, the perspectives of Indigenous peoples, and the immediate consequences of contact.

lessons.title: Religious Reformation: When Authority Is Questioned
lessons.brief: Analyzes the Protestant Reformation and Catholic Counter-Reformation as conflicts over power, interpretation, and allegiance.

lessons.title: Empires in Conflict: The Ottoman, Spanish, and British Paths to Global Influence
lessons.brief: Compares different imperial strategies and their effects on colonized peoples and rival European powers.

grade_9.focus: The industrial and political revolutions that reshaped society: how technological change, Enlightenment thinking, and mass movements transformed power structures and daily life.

lessons.title: Enlightenment Ideas Meet Old Power: Why Revolutions Erupted in America, France, and Haiti
lessons.brief: Traces how Enlightenment philosophy challenged monarchical authority and inspired three revolutionary movements with different outcomes.

lessons.title: The Industrial Revolution: Progress for Whom?
lessons.brief: Analyzes how mechanization created wealth and urban society while generating exploitation, environmental change, and new class tensions.

lessons.title: Nationalism and the Redrawing of Europe: From Empires to Nation-States
lessons.brief: Examines how the idea of the nation-state emerged, unified Italy and Germany, and created conflicts over identity and territory.

lessons.title: Imperialism and Resistance: Power Dynamics in the 19th Century Colonial World
lessons.brief: Explores European imperial expansion into Africa and Asia, Indigenous resistance movements, and the ideologies that justified colonialism.

grade_10.focus: Ideologies in conflict: how competing visions of society—liberalism, socialism, fascism, and imperialism—collided in the 20th century and shaped modern institutions.

lessons.title: World War I: When Industrial Power Met Political Failure
lessons.brief: Analyzes the causes, course, and consequences of WWI using primary sources to understand how technology, nationalism, and alliance systems led to stalemate.

lessons.title: The Russian Revolution and the Rise of Communism: Ideology Meets Reality
lessons.brief: Examines Marxist theory, Bolshevik strategy, and the establishment of the Soviet state, using documents to evaluate competing interpretations of its significance.

lessons.title: The Interwar Crisis: Economic Collapse, Extremism, and the Road to WWII
lessons.brief: Traces the Great Depression, the rise of fascism in Europe, and the failure of international institutions using original speeches and policy documents.

lessons.title: World War II: Total War, Ideology, and Moral Reckoning
lessons.brief: Analyzes WWII as a global ideological conflict using primary sources to examine militarization, the Holocaust, and competing narratives of victory.

grade_11.focus: Power after ideology: how decolonization, Cold War competition, and economic globalization reshaped international order and left unresolved tensions that define the contemporary world.

lessons.title: Decolonization and Its Contradictions: National Independence vs. Economic Dependency
lessons.brief: Compares decolonization movements in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, analyzing how formal independence masked continued structural inequality and competing Cold War interests.

lessons.title: The Cold War as Ideological and Geopolitical Struggle: Beyond the Binary
lessons.brief: Critiques simple Cold War narratives by examining how both superpowers pursued imperial interests, proxy conflicts, and ideological competition while developing nuclear deterrence.

lessons.title: Development, Modernization, and the Global South: Whose Framework Prevails?
lessons.brief: Evaluates competing development theories and policies imposed on postcolonial states, examining whose interests they served and alternative visions proposed by Global South thinkers.

lessons.title: The End of Bipolarity: Why the Cold War Ended and What Came After
lessons.brief: Analyzes the causes of Soviet collapse, the 1990s moment of unipolarity, and the emergence of new power centers, using historical frameworks to evaluate predictions about global order.

grade_12.focus: Interpreting the contemporary world: how to evaluate competing historical narratives about globalization, power, identity, and justice in order to understand present debates and future possibilities.

lessons.title: Historiography and Perspective: How Do We Know What We Know About the Past?
lessons.brief: Examines how historical method, evidence, bias, and narrative frameworks shape our understanding, using case studies to critically evaluate different interpretations of the same events.

lessons.title: Neoliberalism and Global Capitalism: The Ascendancy of Market Logic and Its Critics
lessons.brief: Analyzes the intellectual and political rise of neoliberal economics from the 1970s onward, using primary sources to assess its advocates' claims and its critics' alternative frameworks.

lessons.title: Identity, Memory, and Reckoning: How Societies Confront Historical Injustice
lessons.brief: Compares different approaches to historical trauma—truth commissions, reparations, memorialization—using case studies to evaluate their effectiveness and limitations.

lessons.title: Contemporary Power Structures: Evaluating Arguments About Multipolarity, Hegemony, and Global Futures
lessons.brief: Synthesizes historical patterns to critically evaluate competing frameworks for understanding 21st-century geopolitics, using evidence and historiographical tools to build independent arguments.

grade_1.focus: Different families around the world have different special days, clothes, and things they do together.

lessons.title: Special Days That Families Celebrate
lessons.brief: Learning about holidays and festivals from different religions and why families gather on these days.

lessons.title: What People Wear for Special Times
lessons.brief: Exploring clothes and items that people wear during religious celebrations and what they mean.

lessons.title: Sacred Places Where People Gather
lessons.brief: Visiting and describing different buildings where people go to pray, worship, or celebrate together.

grade_2.focus: Every religion has stories, leaders, and ways of doing things that teach people how to live.

lessons.title: Stories That Religions Tell
lessons.brief: Learning key stories from different religions that explain beliefs and teach lessons about right and wrong.

lessons.title: Holy Books and Where They Come From
lessons.brief: Discovering what sacred texts are and how they guide people in Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism.

lessons.title: Leaders and Teachers in Religions
lessons.brief: Meeting important figures like Jesus, Muhammad, Moses, Buddha, and Krishna, and understanding what they taught.

lessons.title: Daily Practices and Rules
lessons.brief: Seeing how people follow their religion through daily habits, prayers, and the rules they follow.

grade_3.focus: Religions share common themes like prayer, community, and rules for living, but express them in different ways.

lessons.title: Prayer and Worship: How Different Religions Connect to God or the Sacred
lessons.brief: Comparing how different religions pray, meditate, and show respect to what they believe is sacred.

lessons.title: What Religions Believe Is Right and Wrong
lessons.brief: Exploring moral teachings and ethical guidelines across religions and how they shape how people treat each other.

lessons.title: Community and Coming Together
lessons.brief: Examining how religions build community through shared meals, ceremonies, and gatherings that strengthen bonds.

lessons.title: Birth, Growing Up, and Death Rituals
lessons.brief: Understanding ceremonies that mark life's major transitions and how different religions mark these moments.

grade_4.focus: Major world religions developed in specific places and times, and their core beliefs about God, the world, and human purpose form a complete system.

lessons.title: Origins and Spread: How Religions Started and Moved Across the World
lessons.brief: Tracing where the five major religions began, who founded them, and how they expanded across different regions and centuries.

lessons.title: Core Beliefs: What Each Religion Teaches About God and the Universe
lessons.brief: Mapping the central theological concepts of Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism, including beliefs about creation and the divine.

lessons.title: Sacred Texts and Their Authority
lessons.brief: Analyzing how different religions view their holy books, what they contain, and how believers use them to guide decisions and practice.

lessons.title: Paths to Salvation or Enlightenment
lessons.brief: Comparing how each religion defines ultimate spiritual goals and the practices followers use to reach them.

grade_5.focus: Religions address universal human questions about meaning, suffering, and morality through different theological frameworks and practices that shape cultures and societies.

lessons.title: The Problem of Suffering: How Religions Explain and Address Human Pain
lessons.brief: Examining how different religions understand why suffering exists and what spiritual resources they offer to people facing hardship.

lessons.title: Law, Ethics, and Society: How Religious Rules Shape How People Live Together
lessons.brief: Analyzing how religious moral codes function in society and how they influence legal systems, family structures, and social norms.

lessons.title: Ritual and Symbolism: Why Religions Use Ceremony and Objects
lessons.brief: Exploring the purpose of religious rituals and symbols—what they communicate, how they function spiritually, and what they reveal about religious priorities.

lessons.title: Diversity Within Religions: Branches, Sects, and Different Interpretations
lessons.brief: Discovering that major religions contain different schools of thought and practices, and understanding what causes these divisions.

grade_6.focus: Religions interact with philosophy, science, history, and contemporary society; studying them reveals patterns in how humans create meaning and address fundamental questions.

lessons.title: Religion and Reason: Tensions Between Faith and Science Across Cultures
lessons.brief: Analyzing how different religions have historically engaged with scientific discovery and how believers reconcile faith with evidence.

lessons.title: Power, Authority, and Corruption: How Religions Have Been Used and Misused
lessons.brief: Critically examining how religious institutions and leaders have wielded political power, from crusades to colonialism to modern conflicts.

lessons.title: Interfaith Dialogue: Where Religions Agree, Conflict, and Can Learn From Each Other
lessons.brief: Investigating shared values across religions, sources of historic and contemporary conflict, and models for peaceful coexistence and mutual understanding.

lessons.title: Religion in the Modern World: Identity, Change, and Belonging
lessons.brief: Exploring how religions adapt to globalization, immigration, secularism, and social change while maintaining tradition and addressing current issues.

grade_7.focus: What are the world's major religions and how do their core beliefs shape the way believers live?

lessons.title: The Five Major World Religions: Core Beliefs and Practices
lessons.brief: Survey of Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, and Buddhism with focus on central teachings and how followers practice their faith daily.

lessons.title: Sacred Texts and Oral Traditions: How Religions Pass Down Their Stories
lessons.brief: Exploration of the Bible, Quran, Torah, Vedas, and Buddhist sutras as living sources that guide believers and communities.

lessons.title: Pilgrimage, Prayer, and Ritual: Why Religious Practices Matter
lessons.brief: Examination of how pilgrimage, prayer, meditation, and ceremony function across religions to deepen belief and community bonds.

lessons.title: Religion in My Community: Who Practices What Around Us
lessons.brief: Local investigation into religious diversity, places of worship, and how different faiths coexist in contemporary neighborhoods.

grade_8.focus: How have historical events shaped religious beliefs, and how have religions influenced the course of history?

lessons.title: Origins and Founders: How Religions Began in Their Historical Moment
lessons.brief: Analysis of when, where, and why each major religion emerged, including the social and political conditions that gave rise to new faiths.

lessons.title: Religious Conflict and Coexistence: When Faiths Collide
lessons.brief: Examination of historical religious wars, persecution, and reform movements alongside examples of interfaith cooperation and dialogue.

lessons.title: Branches and Denominations: Why Religions Split and Evolve
lessons.brief: Study of theological disagreements and cultural adaptation that led to Sunni–Shia Islam, Catholic–Protestant Christianity, and sectarian divisions within other faiths.

lessons.title: Religion and Power: How Beliefs Shaped Empires and Nations
lessons.brief: Investigation of how religious authority legitimized rulers, inspired conquest, and determined laws across different historical periods and regions.

grade_9.focus: How do religions interpret eternal questions differently, and what philosophical frameworks underlie their answers?

lessons.title: The Problem of Suffering: Four Religious Responses to Evil and Pain
lessons.brief: Comparative analysis of how Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, and Hinduism each explain suffering—theodicy, karma, divine will—and justify their answers.

lessons.title: Afterlife and Salvation: What Different Faiths Promise Beyond Death
lessons.brief: Examination of heaven, hell, reincarnation, nirvana, and enlightenment as competing visions of the ultimate human destiny and how one achieves it.

lessons.title: God, Gods, and the Sacred: Monotheism, Polytheism, and Other Frameworks
lessons.brief: Philosophical comparison of how religions conceptualize the divine—as one God, many gods, impersonal force, or ultimate reality—and what this means for practice.

lessons.title: Ethics Across Faiths: How Religions Decide Right from Wrong
lessons.brief: Analysis of differing moral frameworks—divine command, natural law, compassion, dharma—and how they produce both universal similarities and stark disagreements.

grade_10.focus: How do religions interpret their own sacred texts, and what role does interpretation play in religious identity and change?

lessons.title: Reading Scripture: Literal, Allegorical, and Historical Interpretations
lessons.brief: Close examination of how different communities read the same passages from Bible, Quran, and Vedas—literal, metaphorical, and historical-critical approaches—and why.

lessons.title: Reform and Modernism: How Religions Adapt While Claiming Continuity
lessons.brief: Case studies of Islamic modernism, Protestant reformation, Jewish enlightenment, and Hindu renaissance showing how faiths reinterpret tradition to fit new contexts.

lessons.title: Heresy, Orthodoxy, and Authority: Who Gets to Decide What a Religion Means?
lessons.brief: Investigation of how religious institutions establish doctrine, judge deviance, and enforce boundaries—and the tensions this creates between tradition and dissent.

lessons.title: Women, LGBTQ+ People, and Marginalized Voices in Religious Texts and Communities
lessons.brief: Analysis of how sacred texts address gender and sexuality, and how contemporary religious communities debate inclusion, reinterpretation, and exclusion.

grade_11.focus: How do sociological, psychological, and philosophical theories explain religion—and what do religions claim theories cannot capture?

lessons.title: Religion as Society, Psychology, and Meaning: Comparing Theoretical Frameworks
lessons.brief: Critical engagement with Marx, Durkheim, Weber, Freud, and contemporary theorists: do they explain religion fully, or does reductionism miss something essential?

lessons.title: Religious Experience and Mysticism: Can Personal Encounters With the Sacred Be Explained?
lessons.brief: Examination of mystical traditions across faiths (Sufism, Kabbalah, Contemplative Christianity, Hindu yoga) and competing interpretations of visionary and transcendent experiences.

lessons.title: Fundamentalism, Literalism, and Religious Certainty: Modern Phenomenon or Timeless Response?
lessons.brief: Analysis of what fundamentalism is, why it emerges, and whether it represents corruption or authentic retrieval of original faith across Christianity, Islam, Judaism, and Hinduism.

lessons.title: Religion and Science: Conflict, Complementarity, or Incommensurable Domains?
lessons.brief: Philosophical investigation of whether faith and reason are enemies, partners, or operate in entirely different registers—with case studies from evolution, cosmology, and medicine.

grade_12.focus: How do religions respond to modernity, secularism, and pluralism—and what does the future of religion look like in a global, secular age?

lessons.title: Secularization Theory and Its Critics: Is Religion Declining or Transforming?
lessons.brief: Debate over whether modernity inevitably erodes religious belief, using historical data, regional variation, and competing scholarly arguments to evaluate the thesis.

lessons.title: Syncretism, Hybridity, and Religious Innovation: When Faiths Meet and Merge
lessons.brief: Case-study analysis of how religions blend (African diaspora religions, Chinese folk religion, Latino Catholicism) and whether fusion strengthens or dilutes authentic faith.

lessons.title: Religious Nationalism and Political Identity: When Faith Becomes Ideology
lessons.brief: Examination of how religions are weaponized for national projects, ethnic identity, and political power—in India, the Middle East, and the West—and ethical implications.

lessons.title: Religion Beyond Belief: Community, Ethics, and Meaning in a Post-Christian West
lessons.brief: Investigation of 'religious nones,' spiritual-but-not-religious movement, and whether secular worldviews can fulfill functions religion historically served—belonging, purpose, transcendence.

grade_1.focus: Writing is making marks that tell a story or show what you see and feel.

lessons.title: Making Letters with Your Hand
lessons.brief: Students learn to form letters by drawing lines and shapes, connecting hand movements to letter sounds.

lessons.title: Words for Things I Know
lessons.brief: Students write simple words for everyday objects and people in their lives using invented or correct spelling.

lessons.title: A Picture and Words Together
lessons.brief: Students combine drawings with single words or very simple sentences to tell what they see or did.

grade_2.focus: Writing is putting words in order to tell someone what happened or what something is like.

lessons.title: Sentences That Tell a Story
lessons.brief: Students write short sentences about events in their day, using a beginning, middle, and end.

lessons.title: Describing What You See and Hear
lessons.brief: Students use adjectives and sensory words to describe objects, animals, and places in more detail.

lessons.title: Writing a List That Makes Sense
lessons.brief: Students organize related words or simple ideas into a list (like things in a backpack or steps in a recipe).

grade_3.focus: Writing is organizing ideas clearly so a reader can follow what happened and why it matters.

lessons.title: Why Did That Happen? Writing Cause and Effect
lessons.brief: Students write sentences and short paragraphs explaining what caused something to happen and what happened as a result.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Things in Writing
lessons.brief: Students describe how two things are alike and different, using comparison words like 'both,' 'but,' and 'unlike.'

lessons.title: Putting Events in Order with Time Words
lessons.brief: Students use time-order words (first, next, then, finally) to write about a sequence of events clearly.

lessons.title: Writing a Topic Sentence and Details
lessons.brief: Students learn to write a main idea sentence, then add 2–3 detail sentences that support it.

grade_4.focus: Writing is building paragraphs where each sentence serves a purpose and works together to explain or describe something complete.

lessons.title: Topic Sentences That Control a Paragraph
lessons.brief: Students learn how a strong topic sentence announces the main idea and guides all the sentences that follow.

lessons.title: Supporting Details: Facts, Examples, and Reasons
lessons.brief: Students select and organize specific details—facts, examples, and reasons—that prove or explain their main idea.

lessons.title: Paragraph Structure: Beginning, Middle, and Closing
lessons.brief: Students write multi-sentence paragraphs with an introduction, supporting sentences, and a concluding sentence that relates back to the main idea.

lessons.title: Combining Sentences and Using Transitions
lessons.brief: Students use connecting words (and, because, so, also, however) to link related ideas and make writing flow smoothly.

grade_5.focus: Writing is explaining complex ideas and processes by breaking them into clear steps and showing how parts connect to a larger purpose.

lessons.title: Explaining a Process Step-by-Step
lessons.brief: Students write instructions or explanations of how something works by breaking it into logical, sequential steps with clear transitions.

lessons.title: Building an Argument with Reasons and Evidence
lessons.brief: Students learn to state an opinion or claim, then support it with multiple reasons and specific evidence that proves their point.

lessons.title: Asking 'Why?' and Answering in Writing
lessons.brief: Students identify cause-and-effect relationships in their own writing, explaining not just what happened but the reasons and consequences behind it.

lessons.title: Organizing Multi-Paragraph Writing
lessons.brief: Students plan and write 3–4 connected paragraphs with an introduction, body paragraphs with different ideas, and a conclusion.

grade_6.focus: Writing is synthesizing information and ideas across different sources to develop and support a position or interpretation with analytical depth.

lessons.title: Identifying Main Ideas and Analyzing Supporting Evidence
lessons.brief: Students examine how writers use specific evidence and reasoning to support claims, and practice distinguishing between strong and weak support.

lessons.title: Writing an Analytical Essay with Multiple Perspectives
lessons.brief: Students develop a thesis, present multiple viewpoints or pieces of evidence, and analyze how they connect to and strengthen their central argument.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Information from Multiple Texts
lessons.brief: Students gather information from different sources on a single topic and write to show how ideas relate, compare, and build on one another.

lessons.title: Evaluating Claims and Distinguishing Fact from Opinion
lessons.brief: Students learn to identify whether a statement is factual or opinion-based, and write analytically about the credibility and purpose of different types of claims.

grade_7.focus: Writing for a purpose: learning to shape ideas for different audiences and contexts.

lessons.title: Audience and Tone: Writing for Different People
lessons.brief: Students learn how to adjust their writing style, vocabulary, and formality based on who they're writing to and why.

lessons.title: Building an Argument: Claim, Evidence, and Reasoning
lessons.brief: Students structure persuasive writing by clearly stating a position, supporting it with facts, and explaining why the evidence matters.

lessons.title: Narrative with Purpose: Stories That Reveal Something
lessons.brief: Students write narratives that go beyond plot—using personal or fictional stories to explore themes or make a point.

lessons.title: Revising for Clarity: Making Your Ideas Easier to Follow
lessons.brief: Students learn to reread their work as a reader would, identifying confusing parts and strengthening weak explanations.

grade_8.focus: Evaluating and integrating multiple perspectives: writing that acknowledges complexity and competing viewpoints.

lessons.title: Counterargument and Rebuttal: Addressing the Other Side
lessons.brief: Students learn to identify opposing viewpoints and respond to them thoughtfully, strengthening their own position in the process.

lessons.title: Synthesizing Sources: Combining Ideas from Multiple Texts
lessons.brief: Students practice pulling ideas from different sources and weaving them together to build a larger argument or analysis.

lessons.title: Bias in Writing: Recognizing and Avoiding Slant
lessons.brief: Students examine how word choice, selection of evidence, and framing reveal bias—then practice writing with greater fairness.

lessons.title: Analyzing Rhetoric: How Writers Persuade
lessons.brief: Students identify techniques like repetition, analogy, and emotional appeal, then use these tools deliberately in their own persuasive writing.

grade_9.focus: Developing a writerly voice: crafting writing that is both technically sound and distinctly your own.

lessons.title: Style and Voice: Beyond Correctness
lessons.brief: Students move beyond following rules to make deliberate choices about sentence rhythm, word selection, and tone that reflect their perspective.

lessons.title: Building Nuance in Analysis: Moving Past Simple Conclusions
lessons.brief: Students learn to explore complications, exceptions, and layers in their thinking rather than settling for surface-level observations.

lessons.title: Integrating Evidence Without Losing Your Voice
lessons.brief: Students practice weaving quotations and data into their writing while maintaining their own analysis and commentary.

lessons.title: Genre Experimentation: Writing Across Forms
lessons.brief: Students write in multiple genres—essay, letter, dialogue, annotated text—to understand how form shapes what can be said.

grade_10.focus: Close reading and interpretive writing: analyzing texts deeply and building arguments from careful observation.

lessons.title: Reading Between the Lines: Inference and Subtext
lessons.brief: Students learn to identify what a text implies but doesn't state directly, then use these insights to write original interpretations.

lessons.title: Textual Evidence: Selecting and Analyzing Specific Passages
lessons.brief: Students practice choosing precise excerpts and examining them word-by-word to support claims, rather than relying on paraphrase.

lessons.title: Contextualizing Sources: Author, Time, and Purpose
lessons.brief: Students research the background of texts they analyze, considering how historical moment and author's position shape meaning.

lessons.title: Argument Architecture: Complex Thesis and Subordinate Claims
lessons.brief: Students structure multi-layered arguments where each claim builds logically on the previous one, creating a coherent whole.

grade_11.focus: Intellectual critique: questioning assumptions, comparing frameworks, and building original arguments grounded in evidence.

lessons.title: Interrogating Assumptions: What Does This Text Take for Granted?
lessons.brief: Students identify unstated premises in texts and arguments, then explore how different assumptions lead to different conclusions.

lessons.title: Comparing Interpretive Frameworks: How Perspective Shapes Meaning
lessons.brief: Students apply multiple analytical lenses—historical, feminist, economic, psychological—to the same text and argue for the value of different approaches.

lessons.title: Crafting an Original Argument: Beyond Summary and Analysis
lessons.brief: Students develop thesis statements that make a debatable claim not readily obvious from the text, then defend it with rigorous evidence.

lessons.title: Engaging with Scholarly Conversation: Building on Existing Criticism
lessons.brief: Students research what others have written about a topic, position their argument in relation to existing scholarship, and explain their contribution.

grade_12.focus: Research-driven, multi-source argumentation: synthesizing complex evidence to make persuasive, original claims.

lessons.title: Designing a Research Question: From Curiosity to Inquiry
lessons.brief: Students learn to formulate focused, researchable questions that are narrow enough to investigate thoroughly but broad enough to engage with real complexity.

lessons.title: Evaluating and Integrating Primary and Secondary Sources
lessons.brief: Students assess source credibility, identify bias, and weave together firsthand documents, data, and scholarly analysis into a unified argument.

lessons.title: Managing Counterargument and Limitation: Strengthening Claims Through Concession
lessons.brief: Students acknowledge gaps in their evidence, competing interpretations, and limits of their argument—then explain why their position remains strongest.

lessons.title: Writing for Academic and Public Audiences: Adapting Complexity
lessons.brief: Students learn to write the same argument for different contexts—a formal research paper, a policy brief, a public essay—adjusting depth and accessibility without sacrificing rigor.
